name: Saffron and cardamom shrikhand with papaya and pomegranate
inspiredBy: Gujarati and Maharashtrian shrikhand, lighter and sweetened with fruit
about: Thick Greek yogurt sweetened with ripe papaya, scented with saffron and cardamom and topped with ruby pomegranate seeds. It is the Gujarati and Maharashtrian dessert, lightened. The yogurt brings **protein and calcium**, and the almonds add a little crunch.
steps: Soak the saffron in a spoonful of warm water.
Whisk the yogurt with the mashed papaya, cardamom and saffron water until smooth and creamy.
Spoon into a bowl and top with the pomegranate seeds and almonds.
tip: Sweeten with a teaspoon of honey or jaggery if the papaya is not very ripe.

name: Masala boiled eggs
inspiredBy: Indian street-stall masala eggs
about: Hard-boiled eggs halved and dusted with Kashmiri chili, black pepper and a few drops of lemon, with cilantro on top. It is the simplest road-side snack, and it keeps you full. The eggs bring **protein and choline**.
steps: Boil the eggs for 9 minutes, cool them in cold water and peel.
Halve the eggs and sprinkle with the Kashmiri chili, pepper, salt and lemon juice, then top with cilantro.
tip: Boil a few on Sunday; they keep 5 days in the shell.

name: Cabbage and carrot kosambari with toasted sesame
inspiredBy: Karnataka kosambari, here made with sesame instead of soaked dal
about: Crisp shredded cabbage and sweet grated carrot tossed with lemon, mustard seeds and toasted sesame, in the spirit of a Karnataka kosambari. It is crunchy, tangy and refreshing. The carrot brings **plenty of vitamin A**, and the toasted sesame adds crunch.
steps: Toss the cabbage, carrot and green chili with the lemon juice and salt.
Dry-roast the sesame seeds in a small pan, then dry-fry the mustard seeds for 20 seconds until they pop.
Fold the sesame, mustard seeds and cilantro into the salad just before serving.
tip: Dress it just before serving so the cabbage stays crunchy.

name: Tandoori-style chicken bites
inspiredBy: North Indian chicken tikka
about: Little chunks of chicken thigh marinated in yogurt, lemon, ginger, garlic and Kashmiri chili, roasted until browned at the edges. They are the high-protein snack for a hungrier day. The chicken brings **protein, zinc and B6**.
steps: Mix the chicken with the yogurt, ginger, garlic, lemon juice, Kashmiri chili, turmeric, cumin, salt and oil and leave it for at least 20 minutes.
Thread onto skewers or spread on a tray and roast at 230 C (450 F) for 15 to 18 minutes, turning once, until browned and cooked through.
Rest for 3 minutes and serve warm.
tip: Marinate in the morning and it takes 15 minutes in the oven at snack time.
ingredients: skinless thigh, cut in small chunks

name: Chickpea sundal
inspiredBy: Tamil sundal
about: Soft chickpeas tempered with mustard seeds, curry leaves and green chili, with fresh coconut and lemon. It is the humble protein snack of Tamil festivals. The chickpeas bring **protein, fibre and iron**.
steps: Use the kala chana you cooked for Friday's kadala curry, or canned, drained and rinsed.
Warm the oil, add the mustard seeds and let them pop, then the green chili and curry leaves.
Toss the chickpeas through the tempering with the coconut and lemon juice.
tip: A pinch of black pepper wakes it up.

name: Haldi doodh with almonds and cardamom
inspiredBy: North Indian and Gujarati haldi doodh, with ground almonds as in badam doodh
about: Warm milk simmered with turmeric, black pepper and cardamom and whisked with finely ground almonds until it is silky. It is the Gujarati and Maharashtrian bedtime cup, and a snack that feels like a hug. The milk brings **calcium and B12** to the day, and the almonds add a little vitamin E.
steps: Grind the almonds as fine as you can, with a spoonful of the milk, into a smooth paste.
Warm the rest of the milk with the turmeric, pepper and cardamom over medium-low heat for about 5 minutes, until steaming, without letting it boil over.
Whisk in the almond paste and heat for 1 more minute. Pour into a mug.
tip: Stir in a teaspoon of jaggery or honey if you like it sweet. Skip the pepper for children.

name: Egg chaat with onion, tomato and lemon
inspiredBy: Indian street-stall anda chaat
about: Chopped hard-boiled eggs tossed with red onion, tomato, cilantro, lemon and chaat masala, with a few roasted peanuts for crunch. It is tangy, salty and fresh, and it takes ten minutes. The eggs bring **protein and choline**.
steps: Boil the eggs for 9 minutes, cool them in cold water, peel and chop roughly.
Toss the eggs gently with the onion, tomato, cilantro, lemon juice, chaat masala, pepper and salt.
Scatter the peanuts (toasted in a dry pan if raw) on top just before eating.
tip: Boil the eggs a day or two ahead and the chaat takes 3 minutes.

name: Gulf foul with lemon, cumin and khubz
inspiredBy: Saudi and Emirati foul, the fava bean breakfast every Gulf family knows, with a boiled egg
about: Warm fava beans mashed with garlic, cumin and lemon, then piled with fresh tomato, onion, parsley and a little green chili, with a spoon of tahini, a boiled egg and hot whole-wheat khubz for scooping. A proper Gulf breakfast that keeps you going until lunch. The fava beans bring **folate, iron and fibre**, and the tahini adds calcium.
steps: Lower the egg into a pot of boiling water and cook it for 8 minutes, then cool it under cold water and peel. Do this first so it is ready when the beans are.
Warm half the oil in a small pan, add the garlic and cumin for 20 seconds, then tip in the fava beans with a splash of water and the salt.
Warm over medium heat for 5 minutes, then mash about half of the beans with a fork so it is chunky and creamy.
Warm the khubz in a dry pan or the toaster until it is soft with a few toasty spots.
Spoon the foul into a shallow bowl and top it with the tomato, onion, parsley and green chili.
Squeeze over the lemon, drizzle with the rest of the oil and the tahini, and serve with the halved egg and the khubz.
tip: Fresh chopped mint is a common addition. Cook a double batch of fava, or open a tin with no salt added, and a second breakfast is quick.
ingredients: cooked from dried, or a tin with no salt added, drained

name: Balaleet-inspired saffron vermicelli with a cardamom omelette
inspiredBy: Emirati balaleet, the sweet-savoury vermicelli with a thin omelette on top, made here with whole wheat pasta and much less sugar
about: Thin strands of whole wheat pasta fried in a little ghee, then simmered with saffron, cardamom and a chopped date for just enough sweetness, and topped with a soft, lightly spiced omelette and toasted almonds. It's the sweet and salty breakfast of the Emirates and Qatar. The two eggs bring **protein and choline**, and the almonds add vitamin E.
steps: Steep the saffron in 2 tablespoons of hot water. Melt the ghee in a small pan and stir-fry the broken pasta for 2 to 3 minutes until it smells toasty and turns a shade darker.

Add about a third of a cup (80 ml) of hot water, the chopped date, half the cardamom and half the salt. Simmer, stirring now and then, adding a splash more water only if the pasta is still hard, until it is tender and has soaked up nearly all the liquid, about 8 minutes. Stir in most of the saffron water and let it finish drying.

Beat the eggs with the rest of the cardamom, a teaspoon of the saffron water and the rest of the salt. Warm the oil in a non-stick pan and pour in the eggs, tilting the pan so they spread thin. Cook until just set, about 2 minutes, then fold or roll the omelette.
Toast the almonds in a dry pan until golden. Pile the vermicelli on a plate, lay the omelette over it and scatter with the almonds. Serve with the orange segments on the side.
tip: Rose water is traditional if you have a bottle: a few drops in the saffron water. A little date syrup (dibs) or honey over the omelette is a common finish. On a weekday, cook the vermicelli the night before. It reheats in a minute with a splash of water while the omelette cooks.
ingredients: thin spaghetti, snapped into short pieces
a small date, pitted and finely chopped

name: Eggs with tomato and green chili, with cucumber and khubz
inspiredBy: Gulf beid wa tamatem, the everyday tomato and egg skillet
about: Eggs set gently into a juicy skillet of tomato, onion, garlic and green chili, with crunchy cucumber and warm khubz. Quick and homey, and very Gulf. The eggs bring **protein and choline**, and cooked tomato is a good source of lycopene.
steps: Warm the oil in a small skillet and soften the onion with the garlic and green chili until golden at the edges, about 4 minutes. Stir in the turmeric and black pepper for a few seconds.
Add the tomato and the salt. Cook over medium heat, mashing the tomato with your spoon, until it has collapsed into a thick, jammy sauce, about 7 minutes.

Make two wells in the sauce and crack the eggs into them. Cover and cook gently for 3 to 4 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks are still soft. If you prefer them scrambled, stir the eggs in instead.
Scatter with the cilantro. Serve straight from the pan with the cucumber and warm khubz.
tip: The tomato base keeps for three days in the fridge, so cook a double batch on Wednesday and reheat it on Saturday morning.

name: Gulf lentil soup with lemon and khubz
inspiredBy: Shorbat adas, the red lentil soup of Gulf kitchens, brightened with lemon
about: A smooth, golden red lentil soup with carrot, onion and cumin, finished with lots of lemon and fresh herbs. A crisp cucumber and khubz on the side make it a full lunch. The lentils bring **iron, folate and plenty of fibre**, and the lemon helps your body use that iron.
steps: Warm the oil in a pot and soften the onion and carrot for 5 minutes. Add the garlic, cumin and turmeric and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the lentils, the salt and about 2½ cups (600 ml) of water. Bring to a boil, then simmer gently for 20 minutes, until the lentils have fallen apart and the carrot is tender.
Blend with a stick blender until smooth, or leave it a little rustic. Add a splash of water if it is thicker than you like.
Stir in the lemon juice, taste and add more salt or lemon if it needs it.
Ladle into a bowl and scatter with the cilantro and parsley. Serve with the khubz, the cucumber and an extra squeeze of lemon.
tip: Make it Sunday evening. It keeps three days and thickens as it sits, so loosen it with a splash of water. Double it and freeze a portion if you like. A pinch of chili flakes on top is common.

name: Spiced chickpeas (nakhi) with labneh, radish and khubz
inspiredBy: the Gulf street-side boiled chickpeas, nakhi, here served over labneh with a fresh salad
about: Warm chickpeas tossed with garlic, cumin and lemon, spooned over thick labneh with crunchy radish, cucumber, mint and parsley, and eaten with khubz. It comes together in 15 minutes and tastes fresh and tangy. Chickpeas and labneh together give you **protein, fibre and calcium** in one plate.
steps: Warm half the olive oil in a small pan, add the garlic and cumin and stir for 20 seconds, until it smells toasty.
Add the chickpeas with a splash of water and the salt. Warm them through for 4 to 5 minutes, crushing a few with the back of the spoon, then take off the heat and stir in the lemon juice.
Spread the labneh across a plate and spoon the warm chickpeas over it. Drizzle with the rest of the olive oil.
Toss the radish, cucumber, mint and parsley together and pile them on top. Dust with the sumac.
Warm the khubz and tear it up to scoop everything.
tip: A teaspoon of toasted sesame seeds over the top is a nice touch. Warm the chickpeas gently so they stay soft.

name: Gulf-style chicken shawarma plate with garlic labneh sauce and salata
inspiredBy: Gulf chicken shawarma, pan-seared at home with baharat instead of on a spit
about: Chicken marinated in labneh, garlic, lemon and baharat, seared until browned, with a cool garlic-labneh sauce, a crisp cucumber and tomato salata, quick-pickled radish and carrot and warm khubz. It tastes like a shawarma shop but sits on a plate. The chicken brings **protein and niacin**, and the carrot, herbs and tomato add vitamins A and C.
steps: Mix half the labneh with half the garlic, half the lemon juice, the baharat, half the oil and a pinch of the salt. Toss the chicken strips in it and leave for 15 minutes, or up to a day in the fridge.
Toss the radish and grated carrot with a squeeze of lemon and a pinch of salt and leave them to pickle while the chicken marinates.
For the sauce, whisk the rest of the labneh with the remaining garlic, a squeeze of lemon and a splash of water until it pours like thick cream.
Warm the remaining oil in a heavy pan over high heat and sear the chicken in a single layer, turning once, until browned at the edges and cooked through, about 6 minutes.
Toss the cucumber, tomato and parsley with the last of the lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Warm the khubz. Pile the chicken, salata and pickled radish and carrot on a plate or into the bread and spoon the garlic sauce over.
tip: Roll everything into the khubz for a handheld wrap, or use chicken breast if you prefer it leaner.
ingredients: for the marinade and the sauce

name: Chicken machboos with brown basmati, almonds and raisins
inspiredBy: Kuwaiti, Emirati and Bahraini chicken machboos, made with brown basmati and less oil
about: Chicken browned with onion and tomato, then simmered with baharat, saffron and sour dried loomi into a fragrant pot of brown basmati rice, finished with toasted almonds and sweet raisins. A Friday lunch favourite in homes across the Gulf. The brown rice and almonds add **fibre and vitamin E**, and tomorrow's lunch is already made.
steps: Soak the rinsed rice in cold water for 20 minutes if you have time, then drain. Steep the saffron in 2 tablespoons of hot water. Pierce the loomi a few times with a knife.
Melt the ghee with the oil in a wide, heavy pot and fry the onion over medium heat until deep golden, about 10 minutes. Stir in the garlic, baharat and tomato paste for a minute.
Add the chicken and brown it for 5 minutes, turning, then add the tomato and the salt. Cook until the tomato breaks down and the pot smells rich, about 6 minutes.
Pour in enough hot water to cover the chicken by a finger, add the loomi, then bring to a boil, cover and simmer for 15 minutes.

Add the rice, pressing it just under the liquid, and top up with hot water if needed so it is covered by about 1 cm. Simmer, covered, over low heat for 30 to 35 minutes, until the rice is tender and the water is gone. Drizzle over the saffron water and rest, covered, for 10 minutes.
While the rice rests, toast the almonds in a dry pan until golden, then scatter them over the rice with the raisins.
Fluff gently and serve, nudging the loomi aside or squeezing it over your plate. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: Dried black limes (loomi) are sold whole at Middle Eastern grocers. Add a cinnamon stick and a few cardamom pods with the water for a more traditional pot, and a handful of chopped cilantro on top.
ingredients: 1 whole for the pot of 2 servings, pierced

name: Grilled kanaad (Spanish mackerel) with dakkous and khubz
inspiredBy: Gulf samak mashwi with dakkous, the garlicky tomato and chili sauce served beside grilled fish across the Emirates, Qatar and Bahrain
about: A thick steak of kanaad, the Spanish mackerel the Gulf loves, rubbed with turmeric and grilled, with a punchy dakkous of crushed tomato, garlic, green chili, cumin and lemon, and a crunchy cucumber and carrot salad. It gives you **omega-3, vitamin D and B12**, the carrot adds vitamin A and the sauce adds vitamin C.
steps: Pat the fish dry and rub it with the turmeric and half the salt. Leave it on the counter while you make the sauce.

For the dakkous, warm half the vegetable oil in a small pan and cook the garlic and green chili for 30 seconds. Add the tomato, cumin and a pinch of salt and cook, crushing the tomato with a spoon, until thick and saucy, about 8 minutes. Off the heat, stir in half the lemon juice and the parsley.

Heat a heavy pan or a grill until very hot. Brush the fish with the rest of the vegetable oil and cook for 5 to 6 minutes on each side, until the skin is crisp and the flesh just flakes at the thickest part.
Toss the cucumber and carrot with the rest of the lemon juice, the olive oil and a pinch of salt.
Warm the khubz. Serve the fish with a generous spoonful of dakkous on top, the salad alongside and the bread for mopping.
tip: Frozen Spanish mackerel from an Asian or Middle Eastern market is the usual source. King mackerel, Atlantic mackerel or hammour also work if you want a milder fish. Dakkous is great on rice and eggs too, so a double batch will not go to waste.

name: Lamb saloona with eggplant and pumpkin
inspiredBy: Emirati saloona, the everyday tomato and vegetable stew eaten with rice or bread, made with extra vegetables, less meat and no potato
about: Tender lamb simmered with tomato, onion, eggplant and sweet pumpkin in a turmeric and baharat sauce with a whole chili and a tang of loomi, thick enough to scoop with khubz. An everyday Emirati stew. The pumpkin and eggplant bring **vitamin A, potassium and fibre**, and the lamb adds iron and zinc.
steps: Warm the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat. Brown the lamb in batches, about 5 minutes, then lift it out.
Soften the onion in the same pot for 6 minutes, then stir in the garlic, turmeric, half the baharat and the tomato paste until fragrant.
Return the lamb with the tomato, the loomi, the whole green chili, the salt and 2 cups of water. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer gently for 40 minutes, until the lamb is nearly tender.
Add the eggplant and pumpkin and simmer for 20 to 25 minutes, until everything is soft and the sauce has thickened. Add a splash of water if it gets dry.
Stir in the rest of the baharat, taste and adjust the salt. Fish out the chili and loomi, or leave them in for the table.
Serve with warm khubz. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch, with its bread wrapped separately.
tip: Saloona is even better the next day. Chicken, fish or just vegetables with chickpeas all make good saloona too.
ingredients: in large cubes, butternut or kabocha squash works
1 whole for the pot of 2 servings, pierced

name: Beef and okra marag with chickpeas and a little brown basmati
inspiredBy: Kuwaiti and Emirati marag bamia, the tomato and okra stew eaten over rice
about: Beef and okra simmered in a bright, garlicky tomato broth with crushed coriander, a good squeeze of lemon and chickpeas, ladled over a small portion of brown basmati. Homely and tangy, and not slimy when the okra is cooked whole and gently. The okra and chickpeas bring **folate, fibre and vitamin K**, and it makes tomorrow's lunch.
steps: Warm the oil in a heavy pot and brown the beef in batches, about 5 minutes. Lift it out, then soften the onion in the same pot for 6 minutes.
Add the garlic, coriander and tomato paste, then the tomato. Cook for 6 minutes, until the tomato starts to break down.
Return the beef with the salt and 2 cups of water. Cover and simmer for about 1 hour and 15 minutes, until the beef is nearly tender.
Add the chickpeas and the whole okra. Simmer gently, without stirring too much, for 15 minutes, until the okra is soft but holds its shape. Stir in the lemon juice.
Meanwhile, cook the rice in plenty of boiling salted water for about 35 to 40 minutes until tender, then drain.
Serve the marag over the rice with the cilantro scattered on top. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: Frozen whole okra works well and is easy to find. Trimming the cap without cutting into the pod, and adding lemon or tomato, keeps it from turning slimy.

name: Roasted sardines with cumin sweet potatoes and a cucumber and radish salata
inspiredBy: Omani and Gulf grilled sardines with garlic and coriander, with a crisp salata in the style of salata Arabiya
about: Fresh sardines marinated in garlic, lemon, cumin and cilantro, then roasted until the skin crackles, with cumin-roasted sweet potato wedges and a crisp salata of cucumber, radish, onion, parsley and lemon. Quick and bright. Sardines give you **omega-3, vitamin D and B12**, and the sweet potato gives you vitamin A.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Toss the sweet potato wedges with half the vegetable oil, half the cumin and a pinch of salt on a baking tray and roast for 20 minutes.
Mash the garlic with a pinch of salt and mix it with the cilantro, the rest of the cumin, half the lemon juice and the rest of the vegetable oil. Rub it over the sardines inside and out.
Turn the wedges and push them to one side. Lay the sardines on the tray and roast for 8 to 10 minutes, until the skin is blistered and the flesh flakes easily.
Toss the cucumber, radish, onion and parsley with the rest of the lemon juice, the olive oil, the sumac and a pinch of salt.
Serve the sardines and sweet potatoes with the salata on the side and a lemon wedge if you like.
tip: Frozen sardines work well once thawed. Open the window or use the exhaust fan, since sardines are fragrant. Mackerel can stand in for the sardines.

name: Lamb harees with ghee and cinnamon, laban and cucumber
inspiredBy: Emirati, Qatari and Saudi harees, the slow wheat and meat porridge of Ramadan and celebrations
about: Cracked wheat and tender lamb cooked slowly with onion and cardamom until they melt into a thick, silky porridge, finished with a spoon of melted ghee and a dusting of cinnamon. Cold laban and a cucumber, mint and parsley salad cut the richness. The cracked wheat brings **fibre, magnesium and B vitamins**, and the laban adds calcium. It makes two portions, so Sunday's lunch is done.
steps: Rinse the cracked wheat and cover it with plenty of cold water. Leave it to soak while the lamb cooks, at least an hour.

Put the lamb, the onion, the cardamom and the salt in a heavy pot with about 5 cups of water. Bring to a boil, skim off any foam, then cover and simmer for 1 and a half hours, until the lamb is very tender.

Lift out the onion and discard it. Drain the wheat and add it to the pot with the black pepper. Simmer, covered, over the lowest heat for 1 hour, stirring from time to time and adding hot water whenever it looks dry, until the wheat is very soft and has broken down.

Take the pot off the heat and beat the porridge hard with a wooden spoon or a masher for 5 to 10 minutes, until the lamb shreds into the wheat and it turns smooth and stretchy. Add a little hot water if it is too stiff; it should fall from a spoon in a thick ribbon.
Melt the ghee in a small pan until it just starts to smell nutty.
Spoon the harees into shallow bowls and make a small well in the middle. Pour the hot ghee into the well and dust with the cinnamon.

Toss the cucumber with the mint, parsley and lemon juice and serve it alongside with a glass of cold laban. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch; loosen it with a splash of water when you reheat it.
tip: A drizzle of date syrup (dibs) is a real Saudi finish. Whole wheat berries soaked overnight make a more traditional, silkier harees, but they need about 2 more hours. A pressure cooker does the wheat and lamb together in about 50 minutes. Chicken works well in place of the lamb, and some families add a pinch of sugar with the ghee.

name: Shrimp with tamarind and tomato over brown basmati, with carrot salad
inspiredBy: Kuwaiti and Bahraini robyan, the shrimp cooked in a tangy tamarind and chili sauce and served over rice
about: Plump shrimp cooked in a sour-spicy sauce of tamarind, tomato, chili and coriander, spooned over fragrant brown basmati with a crunchy carrot salad. Quick, bright and very Gulf. The shrimp give you lean **protein, selenium and iodine**, the carrot brings vitamin A and the tomato vitamin C.
steps: Cook the rice in plenty of boiling salted water for about 30 minutes, until tender, then drain and keep covered.
Whisk the tamarind into 3 tablespoons of warm water until smooth.
Warm the oil in a wide pan and soften the onion for 6 minutes. Add the garlic, coriander and dried chili for 30 seconds.
Add the tomato and the salt and cook until it has broken down into a sauce, about 7 minutes. Stir in the tamarind.
Add the shrimp and cook, stirring, for 3 to 4 minutes, until they are pink and curled. Take off the heat and fold in most of the cilantro.
Toss the carrot with the lemon juice and a pinch of salt. Spoon the shrimp over the rice and serve with the carrot salad and the rest of the cilantro.
tip: Start the rice first and the rest comes together while it cooks. Fresh lime is an easy swap for the lemon.
ingredients: peeled and deveined, no added salt or phosphate on the label

name: Dates with cold laban and cardamom
inspiredBy: Tamr w laban, dates with laban, a classic Gulf pairing
about: A couple of soft dates with a large glass of cold, lightly salted laban and a pinch of cardamom, the way many Gulf families break a fast or end an afternoon. Dates give quick energy and the laban brings **calcium and protein**.
steps: Stir the cardamom into the cold laban and drink it with the dates on the side.
tip: Khalas, sukkari or ajwa are the traditional dates and are worth looking for at a Middle Eastern grocer. Medjool works fine if that is what you can find.

name: Cold cucumber and mint laban
about: Cold laban with grated cucumber, mint and a pinch of salt, a thin, sippable salad that Gulf families have with hot meals and on hot afternoons. Cooling and tangy, and the laban brings **calcium and protein**.
steps: Stir the cucumber, mint and salt into the cold laban.
Chill it for 10 minutes if you have time, then drink it or eat it with a spoon.

name: Warm saffron and cardamom milk with a date and almonds
inspiredBy: the saffron and cardamom milk of Gulf evenings, with the sugar swapped for a date
about: Milk warmed with cardamom and a thread of saffron, with a date and a few almonds on the side instead of sugar. Soothing and fragrant. The milk adds **calcium** and the almonds add vitamin E.
steps: Warm the milk with the cardamom and saffron until steaming, about 3 minutes, and let it sit for a minute so the saffron blooms.
Pour into a glass and sip it with the date and almonds.

name: Orange and pistachios
about: Juicy orange segments with a small handful of pistachios, a fresh and crunchy pairing. The orange brings **vitamin C** and the pistachios add vitamin E and B6.
steps: Peel the orange and eat it with the pistachios.
ingredients: unsalted, in the shell or shelled

name: Pomegranate seeds with pistachios and mint
about: Ruby pomegranate seeds with chopped pistachios and torn mint, a juicy and crunchy bowl. Sweet, tart and refreshing. Pomegranate brings **vitamin C and potassium** and the pistachios add vitamin E.
steps: Scatter the pomegranate seeds in a bowl with the pistachios and mint and eat.

name: Roasted chickpeas with lemon and cumin
about: Chickpeas roasted until crisp with cumin, paprika and a squeeze of lemon, a crunchy snack to nibble on. They are crunchy, tangy and lightly salted. Chickpeas bring **protein, fibre and folate**.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F).
Toss the dry chickpeas with the oil, cumin and paprika and spread on a tray.
Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, shaking the tray halfway, until golden and crisp. Toss them straight away with the salt and the lemon, so the salt clings, and eat them warm.
ingredients: no salt added, drained and patted very dry

name: Dates stuffed with almonds
about: A date split open and tucked with an almond and a pinch of cardamom, with a few more almonds on the side, chewy and crunchy together. A small, sweet snack for the afternoon. The almonds bring **vitamin E and magnesium**.
steps: Split the dates and remove the pits.
Tuck one or two almonds into each date, dust with the cardamom and press closed. Eat the rest of the almonds alongside.
tip: Khalas, sukkari or ajwa dates are traditional. Medjool works fine too.

name: Dates with pistachios and cardamom
about: Chopped dates pressed with crushed pistachios and a pinch of cardamom, rolled into small bites. They are sweet and a little green. The pistachios bring **vitamin B6 and vitamin E**.
steps: Mash the dates with the cardamom and half the pistachios until sticky.
Roll into two small balls, then roll them in the remaining pistachios.

name: Almonds, pistachios and raisins
about: A small bowl of toasted almonds, pistachios and sweet raisins, the kind of mix that sits out for guests all over the Gulf. Salty-sweet and crunchy. The nuts bring **vitamin E and magnesium**.
steps: Toast the almonds in a dry pan for 2 minutes, then toss with the pistachios and raisins in a bowl.

name: Khubz with tahini and date
about: A warm piece of whole-wheat khubz spread with tahini and topped with chopped date, the same sweet-and-nutty pairing as tahini with date syrup. Chewy and gently sweet. The tahini adds **calcium and copper**.
steps: Warm the khubz in a dry pan for a minute.
Spread with the tahini, scatter over the chopped date and fold in half.

name: Creamy oat porridge with stewed pear and walnuts
inspiredBy: Inspired by Scottish porridge and a Canadian oatmeal breakfast
about: Rolled oats simmered in milk with soft diced pear and cinnamon until thick and spoonable, with a spoonful of almond butter stirred in, then topped with cool Greek yogurt, toasted walnuts and a little honey. The **milk and yogurt bring protein and calcium**, and the almond butter adds vitamin E.
steps: Rinse the pear under running water, then core it and dice it small so it cooks down soft.
Put the oats, milk, pear, cinnamon and a pinch of iodized salt in a small pot over medium-low heat. Stir often.
Simmer gently for 7 to 8 minutes, until the oats are thick and creamy and the pear is completely soft. Add a splash of milk if it gets too thick.
Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 2 minutes, until they smell nutty.
Stir the almond butter into the porridge, spoon it into a bowl and top with the Greek yogurt, walnuts and honey.
tip: For an even softer bowl, mash the cooked pear into the porridge with the back of the spoon.

name: Soft scrambled eggs with tomato white beans on toast
inspiredBy: Inspired by British beans on toast, with white beans simmered in tomato
about: Creamy scrambled eggs over white beans simmered in tomato, garlic and a little spinach, with soft toast to mop it up and a small glass of milk on the side. The **eggs and beans bring plenty of protein**, the milk adds calcium, and the beans and spinach add fibre and iron.
steps: Rinse the spinach and parsley under running water.

Warm two thirds of the olive oil in a small pan over medium heat. Cook the garlic for 30 seconds, then stir in the paprika, tomato and beans. Simmer for 6 minutes, until thick and the beans are soft enough to squash with a fork.
Stir in the spinach until it wilts, about 1 minute. Keep the pan warm over the lowest heat.

Beat the eggs with a pinch of iodized salt, then wash your hands. Warm the rest of the olive oil in a second pan over medium-low heat, add the eggs and stir slowly for about 4 minutes, until set and creamy with no liquid egg left, 74 °C (165 °F).
Spoon the beans onto the toast, top with the eggs and scatter with parsley.
tip: Make the bean base ahead and keep it in the fridge up to 3 days; reheat it until steaming hot, 74 °C, before adding the eggs. Small appetite? Have the glass of milk with a mid-morning snack instead.
ingredients: a small glass on the side
crushed by hand with its juice
lightly toasted so it stays soft in the middle

name: Okayu rice porridge with salmon, egg and spinach
inspiredBy: Inspired by Japanese okayu
about: A soft, savoury rice porridge with flaked canned salmon, a stirred-in egg, wilted spinach and fresh ginger. The **soft salmon bones add calcium and vitamin D**, along with plenty of protein, in a bowl that is easy to eat.
steps: Rinse the rice in a sieve until the water runs clearer, and rinse the spinach and scallion under running water.

Put the rice and about 5 times its volume of water (add a splash more if it gets too thick) in a small pot with the ginger. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until the rice has broken down into a soft porridge.
Stir in the salmon, breaking the bones into the porridge, with the spinach. Cook 3 minutes, until the spinach is soft.
Beat the egg (wash your hands after cracking it), stir it in and keep stirring for 1 minute, until the egg is cooked through and the porridge is steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).
Add the soy sauce, then top with the scallion and sesame seeds. Eat it right away. Keep the rest of the salmon tin in a lidded container in the fridge and use it within 2 days.
tip: A rice cooker's porridge setting does the 25 minutes for you. Start it before you shower.

name: Red lentil and carrot soup with lemon, yogurt and soft bread
inspiredBy: Inspired by Turkish mercimek corbasi
about: A silky soup of red lentils, carrot and onion warmed with cumin and paprika, finished with lemon and a spoonful of Greek yogurt. Red lentils melt into the soup, so it is silky and easy to eat, and the **lentils and yogurt bring plenty of protein**, with iron and fibre too.
steps: Rinse the carrot and parsley under running water, then peel and dice the carrot. Rinse the lentils in a sieve.
Warm the olive oil in a pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and carrot until soft, about 8 minutes, adding the garlic, cumin and paprika for the last minute.
Add the lentils, the broth and about 400 ml of water. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 20 to 25 minutes, until the lentils and carrot are completely soft.
Blend the soup with a hand blender until smooth. Stir in the lemon juice and iodized salt, and thin with a little water if you like.
Ladle one portion into a bowl, swirl in about half of the yogurt and top with parsley. Serve with the warm bread and the rest of the yogurt on the side.

Keep the second portion without yogurt (add fresh yogurt when you reheat it). Spoon the second portion into a shallow container and get it into the fridge within 2 hours. It keeps up to 3 days; reheat it once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F). To freeze a single portion, cool it fully first; thaw it in the fridge overnight, use within 2 days and never refreeze.
tip: Freeze single portions in jars or small containers; this soup is best frozen without the yogurt.

name: Baked salmon with lemon and dill, buttery mash and garlicky spinach
inspiredBy: Inspired by a Canadian Sunday salmon supper
about: A tender salmon fillet baked with lemon and fresh dill, served on creamy mashed potato with garlicky spinach wilted until soft. The **salmon brings omega-3 and vitamin D**, and flakes apart with a fork.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F). Rinse the potatoes, spinach and dill under running water, and wash your hands and board after handling the raw salmon.
Cover the potatoes with cold water, add a pinch of iodized salt and boil for 15 to 18 minutes, until a knife slides in with no resistance.
Put the salmon on a lined tray, rub with the rest of the olive oil and the lemon juice and scatter with half the dill. Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, until it flakes easily and reaches 70 °C (158 °F).
Warm half the olive oil in a pan, cook the garlic for 30 seconds and add the spinach. Cook, turning, for 2 to 3 minutes, until soft. Drain the potatoes, saving a splash of the water.
Mash the potatoes with the milk, butter and a little of the cooking water until smooth. Stir in the rest of the dill.
Serve the salmon over the mash with the spinach and a squeeze of lemon.
tip: Swap the dill for chives or parsley.

name: Shepherd's pie with lamb, lentils and peas
inspiredBy: Inspired by the British shepherd's pie, with lentils stretching the lamb
about: Lean minced lamb and red lentils in a rich gravy of carrot, peas and tomato, topped with a thick mash. It is soft and comforting, and the **lamb and lentils bring protein, iron and zinc** in one dish that freezes in single portions.
steps: Rinse the potatoes, carrot, peas and lentils under running water. Peel and chunk the potatoes, cover with cold water and boil about 18 minutes, until completely soft.
Meanwhile warm the olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Cook the onion and carrot until soft, about 8 minutes.
Add the lamb and cook, breaking it up, until no pink remains. Wash your hands after handling the raw lamb.

Stir in the tomato, thyme, soy sauce, the rinsed red lentils and the broth. Simmer for 15 minutes, until the lentils have melted into the gravy, then add the peas and cook 2 minutes more, until thick. The lamb must reach 71 °C (160 °F).
Drain the potatoes and mash with the milk, butter and iodized salt until smooth.
Spoon the filling into a baking dish, cover with the mash and rough it up with a fork. Bake at 200 °C (400 °F) for 15 minutes, until bubbling and golden at the edges.

Divide into two. Spoon the second portion into a shallow container and get it into the fridge within 2 hours. It keeps up to 3 days; reheat it once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F). To freeze a single portion, cool it fully first; thaw it in the fridge overnight, use within 2 days and never refreeze.
tip: Bake the two portions in separate small dishes so one goes straight into the freezer.

name: Niku-dofu, beef and tofu simmered in ginger soy
inspiredBy: Inspired by Japanese niku-dofu and nikujaga
about: Tofu, potato, onion and carrot simmered in a gently sweet ginger soy broth, with thin slices of lean beef laid in at the end so they stay tender, and spinach folded through. The **beef and calcium-set tofu bring protein and calcium**, and it tastes even better the next day.
steps: Rinse the vegetables and spinach under running water. Peel and cut them. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw beef.
Warm the olive oil in a wide pot over medium heat and soften the ginger for 1 minute.
Add the potato, onion, carrot, soy sauce, honey and 350 ml of water. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook gently for 15 minutes, until the potato and carrot are soft.
Add the tofu and simmer 4 minutes. Lay in the beef slices and the spinach, push them under the broth and cook 2 to 3 minutes, until no pink remains and the beef reaches 71 °C (160 °F).

Serve one portion in a deep bowl, topped with the scallion. Spoon the second portion into a shallow container and get it into the fridge within 2 hours. It keeps up to 3 days; reheat it once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Serve it over a small bowl of soft rice if you want a bigger meal. Keep this one in the fridge, not the freezer: frozen tofu turns spongy and chewy. Keep the rest of the tofu block covered in fresh water in the fridge, change the water daily and use it within 3 days; it goes into the miso soup.
ingredients: very thin slices, from the butcher or sliced half-frozen across the grain
peeled and cut into small chunks

name: Braised chicken thighs with white beans, fennel and tomato
inspiredBy: Inspired by Tuscan chicken and beans
about: Chicken thighs braised until they fall apart, with creamy white beans, fennel, carrot, tomato and spinach, scented with rosemary and finished with lemon. The **chicken and beans bring plenty of protein**, and the fennel and carrot cook down to nearly a sauce.
steps: Rinse the vegetables, spinach and parsley under running water. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw chicken.
Warm the olive oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Brown the chicken lightly for 2 minutes a side, then lift it out.
Cook the onion, fennel and carrot in the same pot until soft, about 8 minutes, adding the garlic and rosemary for the last minute.
Add the tomato, broth, beans and iodized salt, then nestle the chicken back in. Cover and simmer gently for 35 minutes, until the chicken is fork-tender and reaches 74 °C (165 °F).
Break the chicken into big pieces with a fork. Stir in the spinach until it wilts, then add the lemon juice and parsley.

Serve one portion with the soft bread. Spoon the second portion into a shallow container and get it into the fridge within 2 hours. It keeps up to 3 days; reheat it once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F). To freeze a single portion, cool it fully first; thaw it in the fridge overnight, use within 2 days and never refreeze.
tip: Make it in a slow cooker on low for 6 hours if you prefer.

name: Miso-simmered mackerel with ginger, soft rice and sesame spinach
inspiredBy: Inspired by Japanese saba no misoni
about: Atlantic mackerel simmered in a ginger miso glaze until it flakes apart, with soft rice and spinach dressed with soy and sesame. The **mackerel is rich in omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the glaze is salty-sweet.
steps: Rinse the spinach and scallion under running water. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw fish. Run a fingertip along the fillet and pull out any pin bones with tweezers.
Cook the rice in a small pot with one and a half times its volume of water, covered, on low for 15 minutes, until soft and sticky. Keep it covered off the heat.
Whisk the miso and honey into 120 ml of water in a small pan and add the ginger. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the mackerel, skin side up, cover and simmer for 8 to 10 minutes, spooning the glaze over, until it flakes and reaches 70 °C (158 °F). Check for stray bones.
Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 1 minute, until soft, then squeeze it dry, cut it into short lengths and toss with the soy sauce, lemon juice and sesame seeds.
Serve the fish over the rice with the glaze spooned over, the spinach on the side and the scallion on top.
tip: Cook the fish and eat it the same day; do not save it for the next. Use the smallest pot with a tight lid for the rice.
ingredients: fillet, pin bones pulled out; Atlantic, never king

name: Oyakodon, soft chicken and egg over rice
inspiredBy: Inspired by Japanese oyakodon
about: Tender simmered chicken, onion and soft broccoli in a light soy broth, set with beaten egg and spooned over soft rice. It is ready in about 30 minutes, and the **chicken and eggs bring plenty of protein**, in a soft, comforting bowl.
steps: Rinse the onion, broccoli and scallion under running water. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw chicken.
Cook the rice in a small pot with one and a half times its volume of water, covered, on low for 15 minutes, until soft and sticky.

Meanwhile simmer the broth, soy sauce and honey in a small pan, add the onion and chicken, and cook for 6 minutes, until the onion is soft and the chicken reaches 74 °C (165 °F). Add the broccoli for the last 4 minutes, until it is very soft.

Beat the eggs lightly (wash your hands after cracking them) and pour them over the chicken. Cover and cook gently for 2 to 3 minutes, until the egg is set all the way through, with no runny parts, 74 °C (165 °F).
Spoon the rice into a deep bowl, slide the chicken and egg over it with the broth, and scatter with the scallion.
tip: Hold back a little rice and a cup of broth for a thinner, soupier bowl.

name: Maritime haddock and potato chowder
inspiredBy: Inspired by a Canadian Maritime fish chowder
about: Flaky haddock in a creamy chowder of soft potato, fennel, carrot and onion, scented with thyme and bay and brightened with lemon. The **milk brings calcium** and the haddock is a lean, mild protein that flakes with the side of a spoon.
steps: Rinse the potato, fennel, carrot and parsley under running water. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw fish, and feel through the haddock for any bones.
Melt the butter with the olive oil in a pot over medium heat and cook the onion, fennel and carrot until soft, about 8 minutes.
Add the broth, potato, thyme and bay leaf. Simmer for 12 minutes, until the potato is very soft, then crush a few pieces against the side of the pot to thicken the broth.
Add the milk and warm gently; do not boil hard.
Slip in the haddock and simmer for 5 to 6 minutes, until it flakes and reaches 70 °C (158 °F). Take out the bay leaf, then add the lemon juice, parsley and iodized salt.
Eat one portion now. Spoon the second portion into a shallow container and get it into the fridge within 2 hours. It keeps up to 3 days; reheat it once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Best eaten within 2 days; the potato goes grainy when frozen, so don't freeze this one.

name: Sardine, tomato and spinach pasta with lemon
inspiredBy: Inspired by Sicilian pasta con le sarde, kept simple
about: Soft-cooked whole-wheat pasta tossed with canned sardines, tomato, spinach and fennel in lemon and olive oil. The **sardines and their soft bones bring calcium**, plus vitamin D and omega-3.
steps: Rinse the spinach, fennel and parsley under running water.
Boil the pasta in plenty of water for 2 minutes longer than the pack says, until very tender, then drain, keeping a cup of the cooking water.
Meanwhile warm the olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Cook the fennel until soft, about 8 minutes, adding the garlic for the last minute.
Add the tomato and cook 5 minutes, until it thickens into a sauce, then stir in the spinach until it wilts.
Stir in the sardines, breaking them up, with the pasta and a splash of cooking water. Toss for 2 minutes, until hot all the way through.
Finish with the lemon juice and parsley.
tip: Use no-salt-added canned sardines if you can find them.

name: Baked egg custard with nutmeg
inspiredBy: Inspired by the British baked egg custard
about: A small, silky custard of egg and milk baked gently until just set, with a grating of nutmeg. It is soft, and the **milk and egg bring calcium and protein** in a few spoonfuls.
steps: Heat the oven to 160 °C (325 °F). Beat the egg with the honey (wash your hands after cracking it), then whisk in the milk, warmed.
Pour into an ovenproof ramekin and grate a little nutmeg on top.
Stand the ramekin in a dish and pour hot water halfway up its side.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes, until the custard is set with just a slight wobble, and reaches 74 °C (165 °F). Eat warm or chilled.
tip: Bake two ramekins together if the oven is on anyway, and chill the second; it keeps up to 2 days.

name: Greek yogurt with ginger apple, almond butter and walnuts
inspiredBy: Inspired by apple compote
about: Cold Greek yogurt over a small pot of soft apple simmered with fresh ginger, with almond butter swirled in and a few walnuts. The **yogurt brings protein and calcium**, the walnuts add omega-3 and the almond butter vitamin E.
steps: Rinse and peel the apple, and dice it small.
Simmer the apple with 2 tablespoons of water and the ginger, covered, for 8 minutes, until completely soft, then stir in the honey.
Spoon over the yogurt, warm or cooled, swirl in the almond butter and scatter with the walnuts.

name: Soft baked sweet potato with nutmeg and yogurt
about: A sweet potato baked until it collapses, split open and spooned with cool Greek yogurt, a little honey and a grating of nutmeg. It is soft and warming, and the **sweet potato brings vitamin A and fibre**.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Scrub the sweet potato under running water and prick it all over with a fork.
Bake on a tray for 45 to 50 minutes, until it is completely soft and slumps when squeezed. (In the microwave, 6 to 8 minutes, turning once.)
Split it open, spoon in the yogurt and drizzle with honey and grate a little nutmeg over the top.
tip: Bake a few at once and keep them in the fridge up to 3 days; reheat each until steaming hot, 74 °C. The microwave works too.

name: Warm cinnamon apple oatmeal
inspiredBy: Inspired by Canadian stewed apple oatmeal
about: A small bowl of rolled oats cooked with diced apple and cinnamon until soft and spoonable, with a few chopped walnuts. It is cosy, easy to eat, and the **oats bring soluble fibre** and plenty of comfort.
steps: Rinse and peel the apple, and dice it small.
Simmer the oats, apple, cinnamon and a pinch of iodized salt with 200 ml of water for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring, until thick and the apple is completely soft.
Spoon into a bowl and scatter with the walnuts.

name: Warm edamame with lemon and sesame
inspiredBy: Inspired by Japanese edamame
about: Shelled edamame simmered until tender and tossed with lemon, toasted sesame and a little salt. It is a soft, savoury bite with **protein and fibre**.
steps: Simmer the edamame in water for 5 to 6 minutes, until soft enough to squash between your fingers.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan for 1 minute. Drain the edamame and toss with the lemon juice, sesame and iodized salt.

name: Ripe pear with almond butter and honey
about: A ripe, juicy pear sliced and spooned over with smooth almond butter and a drizzle of honey. It is soft, sweet and filling, and the **almond butter brings vitamin E** and a little calcium.
steps: Rinse the pear under running water, then core and slice it into a bowl.
Warm the almond butter for 10 seconds so it runs, spoon it over and drizzle with the honey.

name: Miso soup with tofu and spinach
inspiredBy: Inspired by Japanese miso soup
about: A small bowl of miso broth with cubes of calcium-set tofu, wilted spinach and a little scallion. It is warm and light, and the **tofu brings calcium and protein**.
steps: Rinse the spinach and scallion under running water.
Heat 300 ml of water with the ginger until steaming. Add the tofu and spinach and simmer for 2 minutes, until the spinach is soft.
Turn off the heat, whisk in the miso until smooth, and top with the scallion. Do not boil the soup once the miso is in.

name: Hard-boiled egg with soy, scallion and sesame
inspiredBy: Inspired by Japanese ajitama
about: A firm, creamy-yolked boiled egg halved and dressed with a few drops of soy sauce, scallion and toasted sesame. It is an easy, **savoury egg snack** that is soft to eat.
steps: Rinse the scallion under running water and slice it.
Lower the egg into boiling water and cook for 10 minutes, until the yolk is set all the way through. Wash your hands after handling the raw egg.
Cool the egg under cold water, peel it and halve it. Dress with the soy sauce, scallion and sesame, and eat it the same day.

name: Toasted sesame oats with soy milk and tangerine
inspiredBy: Japanese sesame sweets and porridges
about: Creamy oats cooked in soy milk with a pinch of cinnamon and fresh ginger, topped with toasted sesame, juicy tangerine segments and a drizzle of honey. It tastes nutty and warming, a bit like a Japanese sesame sweet. The **oats and soy milk give slow, steady energy** and a good dose of plant protein.
steps: Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan over medium heat for about 2 minutes, until they smell nutty and start to pop. Crush about half of them with the back of a spoon.
Put the oats, soy milk, cinnamon and ginger in a small pot. Cook over medium heat, stirring, until thick and creamy, about 5 minutes.
Spoon into a bowl and top with the tangerine segments, the whole sesame and a drizzle of honey. Stir the crushed sesame through the top.
tip: Cook a double batch and reheat a portion the next day with a splash of soy milk.

name: Soft egg scramble with shiitake and spinach on toast
inspiredBy: Hong Kong-style scrambled eggs on toast, with mushrooms and spinach
about: Fluffy eggs folded with browned shiitake, wilted spinach and scallion, served on toast with a tangerine. A few drops of soy sauce and sesame oil make it taste rich and savoury with very little salt. **Eggs and mushrooms bring protein and choline** to the start of your day.
steps: Heat the canola oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add the shiitake and cook, stirring only now and then, until browned and shrunk, about 4 minutes.
Add the scallion whites and spinach and stir until the spinach just wilts, about 1 minute.
Pour in the beaten eggs and push them gently around the pan until just set and still glossy, about 1 minute.
Take the pan off the heat and finish with the soy sauce, sesame oil, white pepper and scallion greens. Serve on the toast with the tangerine on the side.
tip: Segment the tangerine the night before to keep the morning quick.
ingredients: sliced, whites and greens kept apart

name: Ginger shiitake brown rice congee with tofu and peanuts
inspiredBy: Chinese jook and Cantonese congee
about: A slow-simmered, silky brown rice porridge with ginger and shiitake, with cubes of tofu stirred in at the end and finished with scallion, toasted sesame oil and crunchy peanuts. It's the weekend breakfast that makes the house smell wonderful. The **whole-grain rice and tofu are filling**, and the ginger and white pepper add warmth instead of salt.
steps: Rinse the rice. Put it in a pot with the broth, the ginger coins, the shiitake and enough water to bring the total liquid, broth included, to about 12 times the weight of the rice. Bring to a boil.
Turn the heat to low, partly cover, and simmer for about 1 hour, stirring now and then, until the rice has burst and the congee is thick and creamy. Add a splash of water if it gets too thick.
Fish out the ginger coins, then stir in the tofu and let it warm through for 2 minutes.
Ladle into a bowl and top with the ginger matchsticks, scallion, peanuts, sesame oil, white pepper and the soy sauce.
tip: Make a double pot and reheat with a splash of water. It keeps 3 days in the fridge.
ingredients: sliced into coins and fine matchsticks

name: Cold soba with edamame and sesame-ginger dressing
inspiredBy: Japanese zaru soba and cold sesame noodles
about: Chewy buckwheat noodles tossed with plenty of edamame and crisp cucumber in a tangy rice vinegar, ginger and toasted sesame dressing. It's cool, crunchy and quick, and a teaspoon of soy sauce carries the flavour. **Edamame brings protein and folate**, so it eats like a full lunch.
steps: Boil the edamame in plenty of unsalted water for 3 minutes, then add the soba for the last 2 to 3 minutes, or as the packet says. Drain and rinse under cold water until cool, then drain well.
Whisk the rice vinegar, soy sauce, canola oil, sesame oil, ginger, lime juice and chili flakes in a large bowl.
Add the noodles, edamame, cucumber and most of the scallion. Toss gently.
Pile into a bowl and top with the sesame seeds and the rest of the scallion.
tip: Make the dressing the night before. The noodles are best tossed just before you eat.
ingredients: fresh, from the refrigerated case; dried works, but check the label for salt

name: Ginger-garlic tofu with broccoli, shiitake and carrot
inspiredBy: Chinese home-style stir-fried tofu with vegetables
about: Golden pan-seared tofu tossed in a light ginger, garlic and rice vinegar glaze with broccoli, shiitake and carrot, served over chewy brown rice and barley. A little reduced-sodium soy sauce does the seasoning, and **garlic, ginger and chili do the rest**. It makes two portions, so tomorrow's lunch is done.
steps: Start the grains: rinse the rice and barley together, then simmer them covered in about two and a half times their volume of water for about 40 minutes, and let them rest off the heat for 10 minutes. Cook enough for both portions.
Whisk the soy sauce, rice vinegar, broth and chili flakes in a small bowl.
Heat half the canola oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Fry the tofu, turning now and then, until golden on most sides, about 8 minutes. Lift it onto a plate.
Add the rest of the oil and the broccoli, carrot and shiitake. Stir-fry for 5 minutes, then add the garlic, ginger and scallion and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the sauce and let it bubble for 3 to 4 minutes into a light glaze. Return the tofu and toss to coat, then finish with the sesame oil and serve over the rice and barley.
Pack the second portion, with its share of the grains, for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: Rice and barley freeze flat in bags and reheat in 2 minutes.
ingredients: calcium-set, check the label; pressed dry and cut into cubes

name: Ginger-scallion salmon with bok choy and brown rice
inspiredBy: Cantonese ginger-scallion sauce, made with far less salt
about: Roasted salmon under a bright pile of fresh ginger and scallion, finished with a hot sizzle of oil and a splash of rice vinegar and soy. Silky bok choy and a chewy brown rice and barley mix soak up the juices. **Salmon is rich in omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the whole plate is built on fresh aromatics instead of salt.
steps: Start the grains: rinse the rice and barley together, then simmer them covered in about two and a half times their volume of water for about 40 minutes and rest them off the heat for 10 minutes.
Heat the oven to 220 C (425 F). Put the salmon on a lined tray, pat it dry and roast for 10 to 12 minutes, until it just flakes.
Meanwhile, steam the bok choy over simmering water for 3 to 4 minutes, until the stems are tender but still bright green. Lay it on a platter.

Mix the soy sauce, rice vinegar and chili flakes. Put the ginger, scallion and garlic in a small heatproof bowl. Heat the canola oil until shimmering and pour it over the aromatics: it will sizzle. Stir in the sesame oil.
Lay the salmon on the bok choy, spoon the sizzled aromatics over it and drizzle with the soy mixture. Serve with the rice and barley.
tip: Rice and barley freeze flat in bags and reheat in 2 minutes.
ingredients: skin on or off, as you like

name: Vietnamese chicken, cabbage and cilantro salad
inspiredBy: Vietnamese goi ga, chicken and cabbage salad
about: Poached chicken, shredded cabbage, carrot and rice vermicelli tossed in a lime, garlic and chili dressing, with cilantro and crushed peanuts on top. It's cool, crunchy and tangy-sweet, with a little fish sauce for depth. The **chicken is lean and high in protein**, and the cilantro and cabbage bring vitamins C and K.
steps: Put the chicken in a small pot with enough cold water to cover. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover, turn off the heat and let it sit for about 15 minutes, until cooked through. Lift it out and shred it with two forks.
Meanwhile, soak or boil the vermicelli in unsalted water until tender, about 4 minutes. Rinse under cold water and drain well.
Whisk the lime juice, fish sauce, honey, sesame oil, garlic and chili flakes until smooth.
Toss the chicken, noodles, cabbage, carrot and cucumber with the dressing. Fold in the cilantro, then top with the peanuts.
tip: Poach two breasts at once. The shredded chicken keeps 3 days in the fridge.

name: Lemongrass-chili shrimp and tofu with broccoli and brown rice
inspiredBy: Vietnamese tom xao sa ot, lemongrass-chili shrimp
about: Plump shrimp and golden tofu stir-fried with lemongrass, garlic and chili, tossed with broccoli and carrot and finished with lime and a little fish sauce. It's fragrant, sharp and fresh, and the brown rice and barley soak up the pan juices. **Shrimp is lean and rich in selenium**, and plain peeled shrimp keeps the sodium in check.
steps: Start the grains: rinse the rice and barley together, then simmer them covered in about two and a half times their volume of water for about 40 minutes and rest them off the heat for 10 minutes. Cook enough for both portions.
Whisk the fish sauce, lime juice, honey and chili flakes in a small bowl.

Heat half the oil in a wide non-stick pan over medium-high heat and fry the tofu until golden, about 6 minutes. Lift it onto a plate. Turn the heat to high, sear the shrimp for 1 to 2 minutes a side, until just pink, and add them to the plate.
Add the rest of the oil, then the broccoli and carrot. Stir-fry for 4 minutes, adding a splash of water if the pan dries, then add the lemongrass and garlic for the last minute.
Return the tofu and shrimp, pour in the sauce and toss for 30 seconds. Serve over the rice and barley, topped with cilantro and peanuts.
Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch and reheat it gently, or eat it at room temperature.
tip: Skip the chili flakes for a milder dish, and add extra lime at the end.
ingredients: calcium-set, pressed dry and cut into cubes

name: Miso-ginger mackerel with sesame spinach and brown rice
inspiredBy: Japanese saba misoyaki (miso-glazed mackerel) and spinach goma-ae
about: Mackerel brushed with a thin miso, honey and ginger glaze, broiled until the edges caramelize, with sesame spinach and a squeeze of lime. A small spoon of miso gives deep savoury flavour, and rice vinegar brightens it. **Mackerel is among the richest sources of omega-3** and also brings vitamin D.
steps: Start the grains: rinse the rice and barley together, then simmer them covered in about two and a half times their volume of water for about 40 minutes and rest them off the heat for 10 minutes.
Whisk the miso, honey, half the ginger and half the rice vinegar into a loose paste.

Heat the broiler to high. Lay the mackerel skin side up on a lined tray and broil about 10 cm from the heat for 4 minutes. Flip it, brush the paste thinly over the flesh and broil 3 minutes more, until the glaze browns in spots and the fish flakes.

Meanwhile, blanch the spinach in boiling water for 40 seconds, then cool it under cold water, squeeze out the water and cut it into short lengths. Toss with the sesame oil, soy sauce, the rest of the rice vinegar and ginger, and half the sesame seeds.
Serve the mackerel on the rice and barley with the spinach alongside. Squeeze the lime over the fish and finish with the scallion and the rest of the sesame.
tip: Atlantic mackerel is easier to find and works just as well. Salmon or trout fillets also take the glaze.

name: Lemongrass pork noodle bowl with cilantro and lime
inspiredBy: Vietnamese bun thit nuong, with a lighter dressing
about: Thinly sliced pork tenderloin seared with lemongrass and garlic, piled over rice vermicelli with cucumber, cabbage and carrot, lots of cilantro and crushed peanuts, with a bright lime and chili dressing. It's fresh, crunchy and bright. **Pork tenderloin is lean, with plenty of thiamin**, and the cilantro and cabbage add vitamin K.
steps: Toss the pork with the lemongrass, half the garlic, the canola oil, half of the fish sauce and half of the honey from the dressing, and let it sit while you prepare everything else.
Soak or boil the vermicelli in unsalted water until tender, about 4 minutes. Rinse under cold water and drain well.
Whisk the lime juice with the rest of the fish sauce, honey and garlic and the chili flakes to make the dressing.
Sear the pork in a hot non-stick pan for 2 to 3 minutes, until browned and cooked through.
Layer the noodles, cucumber, cabbage and carrot in a bowl. Top with the pork, cilantro and peanuts and pour the dressing over.
tip: Slice the pork the night before so it is already marinating when you get home.

name: Korean-style tofu, mushroom and egg stew
inspiredBy: Korean sundubu-jjigae, with firm tofu and less salt
about: A bubbling red stew of tender tofu, shiitake and bok choy with a soft egg in a garlicky chili broth, with a small bowl of brown rice and barley. A little gochujang and gochugaru give it that deep Korean heat, and a splash of toasted sesame oil finishes it. The **tofu and egg carry the protein**, and the shiitake add umami.
steps: Start the grains: rinse the rice and barley together, then simmer them covered in about two and a half times their volume of water for about 40 minutes and rest them off the heat for 10 minutes. Cook enough for both portions.
Warm the canola oil in a pot over medium heat. Add the white parts of the scallion, the garlic and the gochugaru and stir for 2 minutes, until fragrant and the oil turns red.
Stir in the gochujang and fish sauce, then pour in the broth, add the shiitake and bring to a boil. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the tofu and the bok choy. Simmer gently for 5 minutes, then season with the soy sauce.

Crack tonight's share of the eggs into the stew, cover and cook for about 2 minutes, until the whites set and the yolks are still soft. Keep tomorrow's share in the shell and crack it in when you reheat. Finish with the sesame oil and the scallion greens and serve with the rice and barley.
Pack the second portion, with its grains, for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: Add a handful of spinach or napa cabbage at the end for extra greens.
ingredients: calcium-set, broken into large pieces by hand
sliced, whites and greens kept apart

name: Chicken pho with charred ginger, star anise and cilantro
inspiredBy: Vietnamese pho ga, with a lighter broth
about: A fragrant, clear broth built on charred onion and ginger, star anise, cinnamon and coriander seed, with tender chicken, rice noodles, shiitake, bok choy and a handful of cilantro and lime at the table. It's a weekend project that makes two bowls, and tomorrow's lunch tastes even deeper. Because the **spices and charred aromatics make the broth**, it needs only a little fish sauce.
steps: Char the onion halves and the ginger directly on a gas flame, under the broiler or in a dry cast-iron pan for about 10 minutes, turning, until blackened in spots. Peel off the worst of the black skin.

Toast the star anise and coriander seed in a dry pot for 1 minute, until fragrant. Add the cinnamon, the charred onion and ginger, the shiitake, the broth and enough water to make about 450 ml of broth for each bowl. Bring to a boil, then simmer gently, partly covered, for 30 minutes.
Add the chicken and simmer gently for 15 to 18 minutes, until just cooked through. Lift it out, rest it for 5 minutes and slice it thinly.

Line a fine sieve with a damp paper towel and strain the broth through it back into the pot; the towel catches the ground cinnamon and keeps the broth clear. Stir in the fish sauce. Pick the shiitake out of the sieve and return it to the pot. Keep it at a gentle simmer and blanch the bok choy for 1 minute.
Cook the noodles in unsalted water until tender, about 4 minutes, and drain.
Fill one bowl with noodles, chicken, shiitake and bok choy and ladle the hot broth over. Serve with the cabbage, cilantro, scallion, chili flakes and lime at the table.
Keep the second portion's broth separate from its cold noodles and toppings in the fridge. Reheat the broth until steaming and pour it over them tomorrow.
tip: Flat rice noodles (banh pho) are traditional if your store has them. A few torn mint or Thai basil leaves and an extra squeeze of lime at the table are lovely, and add no salt.

name: Thai-style steamed trout with lime, garlic and chili
inspiredBy: Thai steamed fish with lime (pla neung manao)
about: Tender steamed trout spooned with a sharp, hot lime, garlic and chili sauce and a handful of cilantro, with carrot, broccoli and brown rice and barley. It's a fresh, punchy take on Thai pla neung manao that needs only a little fish sauce. **Trout gives you omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the lime sauce does the work salt usually does.
steps: Start the grains: rinse the rice and barley together, then simmer them covered in about two and a half times their volume of water for about 40 minutes and rest them off the heat for 10 minutes.
Mix the lime juice, garlic, chili flakes, fish sauce and honey, stirring until the honey dissolves. Taste: it should be sharp, a little sweet and hot.

Put the lemongrass and ginger in a steamer set over simmering water. Lay the trout on top with the carrot alongside, cover and steam for 7 to 9 minutes, until the fish just flakes. Add the broccoli for the last 5 minutes.
Lift the trout, broccoli and carrot onto a plate and spoon the lime sauce over them. Scatter with the cilantro, scallion and peanuts and serve with the rice and barley.
tip: Use a bamboo steamer, or a heatproof plate set on a rack inside a lidded pot.

name: Chili-lime edamame
inspiredBy: Japanese edamame, with lime and chili in place of salt
about: Warm edamame tossed with lime juice, chili flakes and toasted sesame. It's quick, salt-free and a great little hit of protein. **Edamame is a complete plant protein** with plenty of folate and fibre.
steps: Boil the edamame in unsalted water for 3 to 4 minutes, then drain.
Toss with the lime juice, chili flakes and sesame seeds while still warm.

name: Pineapple with toasted walnuts
inspiredBy: the fruit plate after a Chinese family dinner, with toasted walnuts
about: Juicy pineapple chunks with a small handful of walnuts toasted until fragrant. It's sweet, juicy and crunchy, and it's ready in five minutes. The **walnuts add plant omega-3** and the pineapple adds vitamin C.
steps: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 2 minutes, until fragrant. Serve with the pineapple.

name: Chilled tofu with ginger and scallion
inspiredBy: Japanese hiyayakko
about: A cool slab of tofu topped with grated ginger, scallion, toasted sesame and a few drops of soy sauce. It's clean-tasting and savoury, and it takes two minutes. The **tofu gives protein and calcium**.
steps: Slide the tofu onto a small plate and pat the top dry.
Top with the ginger, scallion and sesame seeds, then drizzle with the soy sauce and sesame oil.
tip: Silken tofu is the classic and softer choice; firm, calcium-set tofu holds its shape and carries more calcium.

name: Pineapple with lime, chili and peanuts
inspiredBy: Southeast Asian fruit with chili and lime
about: Juicy pineapple chunks with a squeeze of lime, a pinch of chili and a small handful of unsalted peanuts. It's sweet, sour, hot and crunchy at once. The **pineapple brings vitamin C** and the peanuts bring protein and vitamin E.
steps: Toss the pineapple with the lime juice and chili flakes.
Sprinkle with the peanuts.

name: Carrot sticks with peanut-lime dip
inspiredBy: Vietnamese peanut dipping sauce
about: Crunchy carrot sticks with a quick dip of ground peanuts, lime, garlic and a few drops of soy sauce. It's a nutty, tangy, garlicky bite in the spirit of a Vietnamese peanut sauce. The **peanuts add protein and vitamin E**.
steps: Mix the ground peanuts, lime juice, garlic, soy sauce, honey and chili flakes with a splash of warm water, until it is a thick, dippable sauce.
Serve with the carrot sticks.

name: Crispy sesame-garlic tofu bites
inspiredBy: Chinese pan-fried tofu with garlic and chili
about: Cubes of tofu pan-fried until golden, then tossed with garlic, chili flakes, a few drops of soy sauce and rice vinegar, and finished with toasted sesame. They're crisp outside, soft inside, and good warm or cold. The **tofu adds protein and calcium**.
steps: Heat the canola oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Fry the tofu, turning, until golden on most sides, about 7 minutes.

Take the pan off the heat and stir in the garlic and chili flakes; the heat of the pan softens the garlic in about 30 seconds. Add the soy sauce and rice vinegar, toss to coat, then scatter with the sesame seeds.
ingredients: calcium-set, pressed dry and cut into cubes

name: Warm walnut soy milk with ginger
inspiredBy: Chinese walnut soy milk
about: Soy milk gently warmed with fresh ginger and a few crushed walnuts, a little sweet and very soothing. It's inspired by the walnut soy milk drinks of northern China. The **soy milk adds protein and calcium** and the walnuts add plant omega-3.
steps: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 2 minutes, then crush them roughly.
Warm the soy milk with the ginger in a small pot over low heat for 5 minutes, without letting it boil. Pour into a mug through a sieve, stir in the honey and top with the walnuts.
tip: Make a double batch and drink the second one cold.

name: Ginger-soy marinated egg
inspiredBy: Japanese ajitsuke tamago and Chinese tea eggs
about: Soft-set boiled egg steeped in a little soy sauce, ginger and star anise. It's savoury, silky and easy to make ahead. The **egg adds protein and choline**.
steps: Lower the eggs into boiling water and cook for 7 minutes. Cool them in cold water, then peel.
Put the soy sauce, ginger, star anise and about 60 ml of water per egg in a small zip bag or a snug jar. Add the eggs and leave for at least 4 hours, or overnight, turning them twice.
tip: Make two at once and double the marinade.

name: Edamame-ginger dip with carrot sticks
inspiredBy: Japanese edamame-zunda flavours
about: A thick, green dip of mashed edamame with lime, ginger and a little sesame oil, scooped up with carrot sticks. It's a bright, nutty take on hummus. The **edamame brings protein, folate and fibre**.
steps: Boil the edamame in unsalted water for 4 minutes and drain, saving a splash of the water.
Mash or blend the edamame with the lime juice, ginger, garlic, sesame oil and enough of the water to make a thick dip.
Scatter with the sesame seeds and serve with the carrot sticks.

name: Quick sesame cucumber and edamame pickle
inspiredBy: Japanese sunomono, with edamame
about: Cucumber and edamame tossed in rice vinegar, honey, ginger and toasted sesame and left to sit for a few minutes. It's cool, crunchy and tangy, a little like a Japanese sunomono. The **edamame adds protein and fibre**.
steps: Boil the edamame in unsalted water for 3 minutes, drain and cool.
Whisk the rice vinegar, honey and ginger. Toss with the cucumber and edamame and let it sit for 5 minutes. Scatter with the sesame seeds.

name: Cucumber and edamame in walnut-miso dressing
inspiredBy: Japanese kurumi-ae (walnut dressing)
about: Crisp cucumber and edamame tossed in a creamy dressing of toasted ground walnuts, a little miso, rice vinegar and honey. It's a snack version of the Japanese kurumi-ae, nutty, savoury and a touch sweet. The **walnuts bring plant omega-3** and the edamame brings protein.
steps: Boil the edamame in unsalted water for 3 minutes, drain and cool.
Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 2 minutes, then grind them to a coarse paste in a mortar. Stir in the miso, rice vinegar, honey and a splash of water.
Toss the cucumber and edamame with the dressing.

name: Blueberry banana overnight oats with walnuts
inspiredBy: Swiss Bircher muesli, by way of the North American overnight-oats jar
about: Rolled oats soaked overnight in milk and Greek yogurt until thick and creamy, then topped with blueberries, sliced banana, a little maple and toasted walnuts. It's a cold, grab-it breakfast made the night before. The **oats and fruit bring fibre and potassium**, and the milk and yogurt cover a good part of your dairy for the day.
steps: The night before, stir the oats, milk, yogurt, cinnamon and vanilla together in a jar or bowl. Cover and chill overnight.
In the morning, give it a good stir. If it's thicker than you like, loosen it with a splash of milk or water.
Toast the walnuts in a dry pan over medium heat until they smell nutty, about 3 minutes.
Top the oats with the blueberries and sliced banana, then add the walnuts and a drizzle of maple.
tip: Frozen blueberries are great here: they thaw overnight in the jar and turn the oats a pretty purple. At Light, if it's loose, stir in a spoonful more oats or use less milk.

name: Blueberry and toasted oat parfait with almond crunch
inspiredBy: the classic diner-counter fruit and yogurt parfait
about: Thick Greek yogurt layered with juicy blueberries, a squeeze of lemon and a quick crunch of toasted oats and almonds, with a drizzle of maple and a pinch of cinnamon. It tastes like blueberry crisp for breakfast and comes together in minutes. The **Greek yogurt carries most of the protein**, and the blueberries bring fibre and vitamin C.
steps: Toast the oats and almonds together in a dry pan over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, until golden and fragrant. Tip onto a plate to cool.
Toss the blueberries with the lemon juice and half the cinnamon.
Stir the maple and the rest of the cinnamon into the yogurt.
Layer half the yogurt into a glass or bowl, then half the blueberries. Repeat, and scatter the crunchy oats and almonds on top just before eating so they stay crisp.
tip: Toast a double batch of the oats and almonds and keep them in a jar for the week.
ingredients: a squeeze, to brighten the berries

name: Western-style veggie scramble with toast and orange
inspiredBy: a Western omelette, scrambled, with no ham
about: Soft scrambled eggs with a splash of milk, sweet red pepper, onion and a big handful of spinach, seasoned with smoked paprika, thyme, garlic and black pepper, served with toast and a fresh orange. It's the diner Western omelette without the ham, and the smoked paprika stands in for its smoky taste. The **orange brings vitamin C** and the eggs bring choline.
steps: Warm the oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat. Cook the onion and pepper until soft, about 5 minutes, then stir in the smoked paprika and thyme for 30 seconds.
Add the spinach and cook until it wilts and the pan looks nearly dry, about 2 minutes.
Beat the eggs with the milk, garlic powder and pepper. Pour over the vegetables and stir gently with a spatula until just set but still glossy.
Toast the bread. Serve the scramble with the toast and the orange wedges alongside.
tip: A little shredded cheddar is classic, but it adds sodium and saturated fat. This week, Tuesday is the morning with room for a small sprinkle.

name: Seared salmon and white bean salad with apple, celery and dill
inspiredBy: a deli-style salmon salad, lightened up
about: A seared salmon fillet flaked over baby spinach with creamy white beans, boiled egg, crisp celery and apple, in a lemony yogurt and Dijon dressing with plenty of dill. It's a quick lunch with crunch in every bite. **Salmon brings omega-3**, and the spinach brings vitamin A and folate.
steps: Lower the egg into a small pot of simmering water and cook for 8 minutes. Cool it under cold water, peel and quarter it.
Whisk the yogurt, lemon juice, Dijon, half the oil, the dill and pepper together in a big bowl until smooth.
Add the celery, apple, onion and white beans and toss to coat.
Warm the rest of the oil in a nonstick pan over medium-high heat and cook the salmon 3 to 4 minutes per side, until it flakes easily.
Pile the spinach on a plate, top with the bean salad and flake the warm salmon over it. Add the egg and eat right away, while the apple is crisp.
tip: Rinse canned beans well: it washes away a good share of the sodium.

name: Smoky turkey and two-bean chili
inspiredBy: classic North American chili, built on beans and lean turkey
about: A big pot of lean turkey, kidney beans and black beans in a thick tomato base with ground ancho chile, cumin, smoked paprika and a good squeeze of lime. The spices are toasted in the pot and the lime lifts everything at the end, so it tastes full with only a pinch of salt. It makes two bowls, so tomorrow's lunch is done, and the beans bring plenty of **fibre and potassium**.
steps: Warm the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and pepper until soft, about 6 minutes, then stir in the garlic for 30 seconds.
Crumble in the turkey and cook, breaking it up, until well browned, about 6 minutes.
Stir in the ground ancho chile, cumin, smoked paprika, cayenne and oregano and cook for 1 minute, until it smells toasty.

Add the tomatoes with their juice, about half a cup of water per portion (more if it gets too thick) and the salt. Bring to a simmer, then cook gently, partly covered, until thick, about 25 minutes. Meanwhile, cook the rice in plenty of simmering water, about 35 minutes, and drain.
Add both beans and simmer 10 minutes more. Take it off the heat and stir in the lime juice.
Ladle over the rice and top with cilantro. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: It freezes beautifully. Double it and freeze single portions for busy nights. Cook a little extra rice too: it keeps 4 to 5 days in the fridge, ready for Thursday's bean bowl.
ingredients: cooked ahead, or cook it while the chili simmers

name: Sheet-pan lemon-herb chicken with potatoes and broccoli
inspiredBy: everyday American sheet-pan suppers
about: Chicken thighs, potato wedges, carrots and broccoli roasted together with garlic, lemon, rosemary and thyme until browned at the edges. A little Dijon in the marinade gives it a tangy crust. It makes two portions, and the potatoes and broccoli bring **potassium** and vitamin C.
