Scatter over the toasted oats and walnuts, drizzle with the maple syrup and finish with a pinch of cinnamon.

name: Tuscan tuna and white bean salad with garlic toast
inspiredBy: Inspired by Tuscan tonno e fagioli
about: A classic Tuscan pairing: tender white beans, flaked tuna, baby spinach and sweet tomatoes in a lemony olive oil dressing, with garlic-rubbed toast on the side. It needs no cooking and is **packed with protein, fibre and folate**.
steps: Slice the red onion very thin and let it sit in the lemon juice while you get everything else ready. It softens and loses its bite.
Drain and rinse the beans and tip them into a bowl with the olive oil, halved tomatoes, diced avocado, chopped parsley, pepper and the salt, then season to taste.
Drain the tuna, flake it in with the onion and its lemony juices, and fold everything together gently.
Toast the bread and rub it with the cut side of the garlic clove. Serve the salad over the spinach with the toast on the side.

name: Chicken and egg rice bowl with spinach and scallion
inspiredBy: Inspired by Japanese oyakodon, with chicken breast and maple in place of thigh and mirin
about: A quick, savoury Japanese-style donburi: chicken and onion simmered in a gingery soy broth, set with a soft egg and piled over rice with wilted spinach. It is cosy and fast, and the chicken and egg together give you **plenty of protein** in one bowl.
steps: Rinse the rice and cook it in a covered pot with about one and a half times its volume of water until tender, about 15 minutes. Start this first.

Slice the onion thin and the chicken into thin strips. Stir the soy sauce, maple syrup, grated ginger and about 1/3 cup (80 mL) of water, a little more at bigger sizes, together in a wide frying pan with a lid and bring it to a simmer.
Add the onion and chicken and cook gently for about 6 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and the onion is soft.
Add the spinach and let it wilt. Beat the eggs and egg whites lightly and pour them over in a thin stream, then cover and cook for about a minute, until just set and still a bit soft.
Spoon the rice into a bowl, slide the chicken and egg on top with all the juices, and finish with the sliced scallion.
tip: Cook the rice a night ahead and the bowl takes 15 minutes.

name: Turkey, black bean and egg brunch burritos
inspiredBy: Inspired by a Tex-Mex breakfast burrito, with turkey instead of chorizo
about: Smoky, spiced ground turkey with black beans, spinach and soft scrambled eggs, rolled into warm flour tortillas with a little melted cheddar. It is a proper weekend brunch with **eggs, turkey and beans in every bite**, and it goes together in about 25 minutes.
steps: Warm the tortillas wrapped in a damp towel in the microwave, then keep them covered.
Soften the finely chopped onion in the oil for 3 minutes. Add the turkey, smoked paprika and cumin and cook, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it smells toasty.
Stir in the black beans, halved tomatoes and spinach and cook until the spinach wilts.
Pour in the beaten eggs and egg whites and stir gently until just set.

Fill two small tortillas loosely with the eggs, cheddar, cilantro and sliced avocado, fold in the sides and roll up. Spoon any extra filling beside them. For a crisp outside, toast the burritos seam-side down in the pan for a minute or two.
tip: To get ahead, cook a double batch of the turkey and bean filling and freeze half. Add the eggs, cheddar and avocado fresh.

name: Chicken tinga rice bowls with black beans and avocado
inspiredBy: Inspired by Mexican tinga de pollo
about: Shredded chicken simmered in smoky chipotle tomato sauce, served over rice and black beans with creamy avocado and lime. It is smoky, a little spicy and tangy, and it **makes two portions**, so tomorrow's lunch is ready. The chicken and beans together carry a big protein load.
steps: Rinse the rice and cook it in a covered pot with about one and a half times its volume of water until tender, about 15 minutes. Cook enough for both portions.
Meanwhile, simmer the chicken breasts in lightly salted water for 15 to 18 minutes, until cooked through. Lift out and shred with two forks. Keep a mug of the poaching water.
Soften the chopped onion in the oil for about 6 minutes, until golden. Add the garlic, cumin and oregano and stir for a minute.

Pour in the crushed tomatoes and finely chopped chipotle with a spoonful of its sauce. Simmer for 8 minutes, until thick, then stir in the chicken with a good splash of the poaching water, more at bigger sizes, so the sauce stays saucy.
Warm the black beans in a small pan. Build bowls with rice, beans and tinga, then top with sliced avocado, cilantro and a squeeze of lime.
Pack the second portion, kept separate from the avocado, for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: Reheat day 2 with a splash of water.

name: Maple Dijon sockeye salmon with roasted sweet potatoes and garlic spinach
inspiredBy: Inspired by West Coast maple-glazed salmon
about: Sockeye is the deep red salmon of the Pacific coast, lean and full-flavoured, and it loves a sweet and tangy maple Dijon glaze. Caramelized roasted sweet potatoes and garlicky spinach make it a full plate. It is a great source of **omega-3 and vitamin D**.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Toss the sweet potatoes with half the olive oil and a pinch of the salt, and roast on a tray for about 25 minutes.
Whisk the Dijon, maple syrup, lemon juice and pepper together.

Push the sweet potatoes over, add the salmon to the tray, season it with the rest of the salt, brush it with the glaze and roast for 8 to 10 minutes, until it just flakes. Sockeye is lean, so do not overcook it.
Meanwhile, warm the rest of the oil in a pan with the sliced garlic until it smells sweet, then add the spinach and cook for about 2 minutes, until wilted.
Scatter the parsley over everything and squeeze over any leftover lemon.

name: Lean beef and kidney bean chili over a baked sweet potato
inspiredBy: Inspired by American beef and bean chili
about: A thick, smoky chili with lean beef, kidney beans and sweet red pepper, spooned over a split baked sweet potato with a squeeze of lime. It is the kind of bowl that **makes a perfect next-day lunch**, because the flavour deepens overnight. Beans and beef give you iron, zinc and fibre in one pot, and the sweet potato adds vitamin A.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Prick the sweet potatoes and bake them for 45 to 50 minutes, until soft all the way through.
Warm the oil in a heavy pot and soften the chopped onion, grated carrot and pepper for 6 minutes. Add the garlic and cook for a minute.
Add the beef and break it up, cooking until no pink remains. Stir in the chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika and oregano for a minute so they bloom in the fat.
Add the crushed tomatoes and a splash of water, then the beans. Simmer for 20 to 25 minutes, until thick, and season with the salt.
Split the sweet potatoes, spoon the chili over and finish with cilantro and lime. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: Microwave the sweet potatoes for 8 minutes, then crisp them in the oven for 10.

name: Turkey and white bean ragù with rigatoni
inspiredBy: Inspired by Bolognese ragù
about: A simmered Italian-style ragù made with very lean turkey and creamy white beans, with finely chopped carrot and onion and plenty of garlic. Tossed with chewy rigatoni and finished with parmesan and parsley, it is real comfort food with **a big dose of protein and fibre** on every plate.
steps: Finely chop the carrot and onion. Soften them in the olive oil over medium heat for about 8 minutes, until sweet and golden. Add the garlic for the last minute.
Add the turkey, let it sit for 3 to 4 minutes so it browns, then break it up and cook until no pink remains. Stir in the fennel seed and oregano and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the crushed tomatoes, the beans and a splash of water. Simmer gently for 25 minutes, stirring now and then and crushing a few of the beans against the side, until thick and glossy.
Boil enough rigatoni for both portions in salted water until just al dente, reserving a cup of the cooking water, then drain.
Toss the pasta with the ragù, loosening with a splash of the pasta water, and finish with the grated parmesan and chopped parsley.
Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: Reheat the leftover with a splash of water or pasta water.

name: Ginger soy salmon rice bowl with spinach and quick pickles
inspiredBy: Inspired by Japanese salmon teriyaki, with little sugar
about: Pan-seared salmon glazed with ginger and soy, over rice with wilted spinach and cucumber and carrot pickled in rice vinegar. Savoury, sharp and rich in all the right places, it is a Friday-night bowl with **omega-3 and plenty of protein**.
steps: Rinse the rice and cook it in a covered pot with about one and a half times its volume of water until tender, about 15 minutes, then keep it warm.
Slice the cucumber and carrot very thin and toss with the rice vinegar, a pinch of salt and a pinch of ginger. Leave them for 10 minutes, then squeeze them dry.

Mix the soy sauce, maple syrup and the rest of the finely grated ginger. Sear the salmon in a hot non-stick pan for 3 minutes, flip, then pour in the glaze off the heat, return the pan and cook for another 2 to 3 minutes, spooning it over and watching it so it does not scorch, until the fish just flakes.
Wilt the spinach in the same pan with a splash of water and a drop of soy sauce, about 1 minute.
Build bowls with rice, salmon, spinach, sliced avocado and the pickles, and scatter with sliced scallion.

name: Chicken souvlaki wraps with lemon potatoes and skyr tzatziki
inspiredBy: Inspired by Greek souvlaki
about: Lemony, garlicky chicken skewers with oregano, roasted lemon potatoes, a cool cucumber tzatziki made with skyr, and warm wraps. It is a relaxed weekend cook, and the second portion makes **a very good wrap** the next day.
steps: Cut the chicken into chunks. Mix half the lemon juice with half the oil, half the garlic and the oregano, and toss the chicken in it. Marinate for 1 to 4 hours, no longer.
Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Cut the potatoes into wedges, toss with the rest of the oil, lemon juice and a little salt, and roast for 35 to 40 minutes, turning once, until golden at the edges.
For the tzatziki, grate the cucumber and squeeze out the water. Stir it into the skyr with the rest of the garlic, chopped parsley and a pinch of salt.
Thread the chicken on skewers and grill or broil for 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through.
Halve the tomatoes and slice the red onion for a quick salad. Warm the wraps and fill them with chicken, tzatziki and salad, with the potatoes on the side.
Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch, with the tzatziki kept separate. Eat it cold, sliced into the wrap, or warm it for 30 seconds.

name: Lean beef cottage pie with olive oil mash, spinach and carrots
inspiredBy: Inspired by British cottage pie and Québec pâté chinois
about: A proper weekend comfort dish: lean beef, carrots, red pepper, kidney beans and spinach in a rich tomato gravy, under a golden olive oil mash with no butter or cream needed. It is hearty, deeply savoury and **packed with iron, zinc and protein**.
steps: Peel the potatoes if you like, cut them into chunks and boil in water until a knife slips in easily, about 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, warm half the olive oil in a wide pan and soften the chopped onion, diced carrot and pepper for about 8 minutes. Add the garlic and thyme for the last minute.

Add the beef and break it up, cooking until no pink remains. Stir in the crushed tomatoes, the beans and a splash of water and simmer for 12 minutes, until thick, and season with two thirds of the salt. Stir in the spinach until it wilts, then tip the filling into a baking dish.
Drain the potatoes and mash them with the rest of the olive oil, the pepper, the rest of the salt and a splash of the cooking water until smooth and creamy.
Heat the broiler. Spoon the mash over the filling in the baking dish, rough it up with a fork so the peaks catch, and broil for 5 to 8 minutes, until golden at the edges.
tip: Double it and freeze the second pie. It reheats well in the oven.

name: Blueberry maple skyr with walnuts
about: Thick skyr with blueberries, a drizzle of maple syrup and a few crunchy walnuts. It is cool, a little sweet and **a serious protein hit** for a few minutes of effort.
steps: Spoon the skyr into a bowl and top with the blueberries, chopped walnuts and maple syrup.

name: Spinach and cheddar egg white cups
about: Little baked egg cups made mostly with egg whites, spinach, tomato and a bit of sharp cheddar. They are fluffy, savoury and **very lean protein**, and they reheat in the microwave in under a minute.
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F) and use a silicone muffin tin or line a few cups with parchment cases.
Beat the egg whites and egg with the pepper and salt, and season to taste. Divide the chopped spinach, tomatoes and scallion between the cups, pour in the eggs and top with the cheddar.
Bake for about 15 minutes, until puffed and set in the middle.
tip: Bake a fresh tin on Wednesday night for Thursday, and another on Saturday for Sunday.

name: Tuna and white bean toast with cucumber
about: Crisp toast piled with a lemony Dijon tuna and white bean mash and cool cucumber slices. It is light, crunchy and gives you **protein and fibre** for few calories.
steps: Toast the bread. Mash the tuna and beans together with the lemon juice, Dijon, pepper and salt, and season to taste.
Spread over the toast and top with thin cucumber slices.

name: Cottage cheese, tomato and parsley toast
inspiredBy: Inspired by Italian bruschetta
about: Creamy cottage cheese on toast with sweet cherry tomatoes, fresh parsley and a thread of olive oil, like a bruschetta that actually fills you up. It brings **a good dose of protein**.
steps: Toast the bread and rub it with the cut side of the garlic. Halve the tomatoes and toss with the olive oil, chopped parsley and pepper.
Spread the cottage cheese on the toast and pile the tomatoes on top. At bigger sizes, serve the cottage cheese in a bowl with the toast on the side.

name: Skyr herb dip with crunchy vegetables
about: A cool, garlicky dip of skyr, lemon and parsley with carrot, cucumber and sweet pepper sticks. It is crisp and fresh, and **very high in protein for the calories**.
steps: Stir the skyr with the lemon juice, chopped parsley, finely grated garlic and the salt, and season to taste.
Cut the carrot, cucumber and pepper into sticks and serve with the dip.

name: Lemon Dijon chicken salad cucumber boats
about: Shredded poached chicken folded with Dijon, lemon, olive oil and parsley, spooned into crisp cucumber halves. It is fresh and zingy, and **lean protein with almost no starch**.
steps: Simmer the chicken in lightly salted water for 12 to 15 minutes, until cooked through. Cool a little and shred.
Stir the Dijon, lemon juice, olive oil and chopped parsley together and fold in the chicken.
Halve the cucumber lengthwise, scoop out the seeds with a spoon and fill the hollows with the chicken salad.
tip: Poach the chicken when you cook dinner and the snack takes 5 minutes.

name: Mini turkey meatballs with tomato dip
inspiredBy: Inspired by Italian polpette
about: Little baked meatballs of lean turkey with parmesan, parsley and garlic, served with warm crushed tomato for dipping. They are tender, savoury and **a lean protein snack that reheats well**.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Soak the oats in half the crushed tomato for 5 minutes, then mix in the turkey, parmesan, chopped parsley, finely grated garlic, oregano and salt, and roll into small balls.
Bake on a lined tray for 12 to 14 minutes, until browned and cooked through.
Warm the rest of the crushed tomato with the olive oil in a small pan and serve alongside for dipping.
tip: Ground turkey breast (99% lean) or extra lean ground turkey both work. Bake a double batch and they keep for 4 days.

name: Black bean and cheddar tortilla wedges with fresh tomato salsa
inspiredBy: Inspired by Mexican quesadillas
about: Crisp pan-toasted tortilla folded around black beans and melted cheddar, cut into wedges and served with a quick lime and cilantro tomato salsa. It is **a filling snack with protein and fibre**.
steps: Mash the beans roughly with a fork. Spread them over one half of the tortilla (at bigger sizes use a large tortilla, or two small ones), scatter over the cheddar and fold it over.
Toast in a dry pan over medium heat for 2 minutes a side, until golden and the cheese has melted. Cut into wedges.
Chop the tomatoes and toss with the lime juice and cilantro for a quick salsa to spoon over.

name: Mexican shrimp cocktail with lime and avocado
inspiredBy: Inspired by Mexican coctel de camarón
about: Chilled poached shrimp with tomato, cucumber, red onion, lime and cilantro, in the style of a coctel de camarón. It is bright and refreshing and **one of the leanest protein snacks there is**.
steps: Simmer the shrimp in lightly salted water for 2 to 3 minutes, until pink and curled. Drain, rinse in cold water and chill.
Dice the tomatoes, cucumber and red onion and toss with the lime juice, cilantro and a pinch of salt.
Fold in the shrimp so it picks up all the lime and tomato juices in the bowl, then top with diced avocado.

name: Huevos rancheros with pinto beans and avocado
inspiredBy: Mexican huevos rancheros
about: Fried eggs on warm corn tortillas, under a spicy tomato and jalapeño sauce, with garlicky mashed pinto beans, a little crumbled queso fresco and slices of avocado. The eggs and beans together bring **plenty of protein and fibre** to the first meal of the day.
steps: Warm half the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion, jalapeño and half the garlic for 3 minutes until soft and fragrant.

Stir in the cumin, then the tomato with a splash of water. Simmer 8 minutes, pressing it down with a spoon, until it thickens into a spoonable sauce. Season with part of the salt and half the lime juice.
Meanwhile, warm the pinto beans in a small pot with the rest of the garlic and a splash of water, mashing them roughly until creamy. Season with a pinch of salt.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan until they have a few toasty spots, then lay them on the plate.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil in a nonstick pan until the whites are set and the yolks still soft.

Spoon the beans onto the tortillas, set the eggs on top, and ladle the sauce over the whites. Taste the sauce and beans and add a pinch more salt if they need it. Stir the rest of the lime juice into the yogurt, and finish with a spoonful of that crema, the avocado, queso fresco and cilantro.
tip: Make the sauce on Sunday and it keeps four days in the fridge, so breakfast takes about 10 minutes.

name: Huevos pericos with a cheese arepa and beans
inspiredBy: Colombian huevos pericos and arepa con queso
about: Colombia's morning scramble with tomato and onion (the colours of the parrot, perico), served with a griddled corn arepa stuffed with a little queso fresco and a spoonful of warm beans. Extra egg whites keep the plate **high in protein** without making it heavy.
steps: Stir the corn flour with a pinch of the salt and enough warm water to make a soft, smooth dough. Rest it 5 minutes, then shape into a thick patty and press the queso fresco into the middle, closing the dough around it.
Cook the arepa in a lightly oiled nonstick skillet over medium heat, about 5 minutes a side, until golden outside and firm when tapped.

Warm a little oil in a pan and cook the onion, garlic and tomato with the cumin for 4 minutes, until the tomato is soft and saucy. Spoon a quarter of it into a small pot with the pinto beans and a splash of water and warm through.
Beat the whole eggs with the egg whites and a pinch of salt, pour them into the tomato pan and stir gently over medium-low heat until just set and creamy, about 2 minutes.
Season the beans and eggs to taste, then serve the eggs beside the arepa and the beans.
tip: On a weekday, griddle the arepa the night before and warm it in a dry pan while the eggs cook, so breakfast is quick. Split it and pile the eggs inside to eat on the go.

name: Yogurt bowl with mango, toasted oats and pepitas
inspiredBy: a tropical-fruit yogurt breakfast, with Brazilian and Mexican touches
about: Thick yogurt with ripe mango and lime, topped with oats toasted in a dry pan and a spoonful of toasted pepitas. The yogurt does the heavy lifting here: a big bowl of it carries **more than 25 g of protein** before you add the oats and seeds.
steps: Toast the oats and pepitas in a dry skillet over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until they smell nutty. Tip them onto a plate to cool.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl and top with the mango. Squeeze over the lime juice, which brings out the mango's sweetness.
Scatter on the toasted oats and pepitas and finish with a pinch of cinnamon.
tip: Toast a big batch of oats and pepitas on Sunday and keep them in a jar. At larger sizes use a deep bowl.

name: Turkey burrito bowl with black beans and lime rice
inspiredBy: the Tex-Mex burrito bowl
about: Taco-spiced turkey over lime-cilantro rice with black beans, charred corn, crunchy cucumber, tomato, avocado and a spoonful of chipotle crema. It is a Tex-Mex lunch bowl, built to be big: **lean turkey and beans** carry the protein and the rice carries your training.
steps: Rinse the rice, then cook it in a covered pot with a little under twice its volume of water and a pinch of salt for about 15 minutes, until tender. Fluff it with half the lime juice and half the cilantro.
Warm the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the onion and garlic for 2 minutes, then add the turkey and break it up as it browns, about 6 minutes.
Stir in the chili powder, cumin, oregano and the rest of the salt with a splash of water, and cook 2 more minutes until the turkey is coated and a little saucy.
Warm the black beans in a small pot, and char the corn in a hot dry pan for 3 to 4 minutes until it has brown spots.
Stir the yogurt with the chipotle, a squeeze of lime and a pinch of salt to make the crema.
Build the bowls with rice, turkey, beans, corn, cucumber, tomato and avocado. Spoon on the crema and the rest of the cilantro.
tip: Cook a double batch of rice and turkey on Monday and chill half in a covered container. Thursday's bowl then takes 5 minutes; cooked rice and meat keep 3 days in the fridge.

name: Lomo saltado with crisp potatoes and rice
inspiredBy: Peruvian lomo saltado
about: Peru's famous stir-fry, born where Chinese and Peruvian cooking meet: strips of beef seared hot with red onion and tomato, splashed with soy sauce and vinegar and tossed with golden potatoes, served over rice. Lean sirloin and a mound of potatoes make it **high in protein and in training carbs**. It makes two portions.
steps: Cover the potato wedges with cold water in a pot, bring to a boil and simmer 8 minutes until just tender. Drain well and let them steam dry.
Cook the rice in a covered pot with a little under twice its volume of water for about 15 minutes, until tender.

Toss the beef with the garlic, cumin, pepper and the soy sauce. Heat half the oil in a large skillet over high heat and crisp the potatoes until golden, 6 to 8 minutes, in two batches if they crowd the pan. Set them aside on a plate.

Add the remaining oil to the very hot pan and sear the beef in a single layer, in batches, for 1 to 2 minutes, until browned but still pink inside. A crowded pan steams the beef instead of searing it.
Add the onion and tomato wedges and toss over high heat for 2 minutes, so they stay a little firm. Stir in the ají amarillo paste, the vinegar and the salt.
Fold the potatoes back in, scatter on the cilantro and serve over the rice. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: For a crisper potato, reheat leftovers in a hot dry pan, not the microwave.

name: Peruvian green arroz con pollo with corn
inspiredBy: Peruvian arroz con pollo
about: Chicken and rice cooked in a blended cilantro and ají sauce until the grains turn vivid green and fragrant, with sweet corn and red pepper stirred in. It is a pot you make once and reheat well, with **lean chicken breast** for protein and the rice for energy. It makes two portions.
steps: Blend the cilantro and ají amarillo paste with water, a few spoonfuls at a time, until smooth, pourable and bright green, about a third of a cup at Standard and Big and a little more at XL.
Warm the oil in a wide, heavy pot over medium-high heat and brown the chicken for 4 to 5 minutes. Lift it onto a plate.
In the same pot, cook the onion, garlic, cumin and oregano for 4 minutes until soft and golden. Stir in the green purée and cook 3 minutes, until it darkens and smells herby.

Add the rice, red pepper and salt with a little under twice the rice's volume of water. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook on low for 10 minutes, then nestle the chicken back in, scatter the corn on top and cover again.
Cook 10 minutes more, until the rice is tender and the chicken is cooked through, then rest off the heat for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork and finish with the lime juice.
Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: Reheat leftovers with a splash of water so the chicken stays moist.

name: Trout ceviche with sweet potato, corn and toasted corn
inspiredBy: Peruvian ceviche de trucha, as it is made around Lake Titicaca, with camote and choclo
about: Fresh trout cured briefly in lime juice with red onion, chili and cilantro, served the Peruvian way with boiled sweet potato and sweet corn, and a handful of pan-toasted corn for a nutty bite. Trout is a **fatty fish rich in omega-3**, and the sweet potato brings the carbs.
steps: Rinse the onion slices in cold water for a minute, then drain; this softens their bite and keeps them crisp.

Cover the sweet potato with water, bring to a boil and cook about 12 minutes until tender but not mushy. Lift it out with a slotted spoon, then simmer most of the corn in the same water for 4 minutes and drain.
Pat the rest of the corn very dry and toast it in a dry skillet over medium heat, shaking the pan, until golden and nutty in spots, 6 to 8 minutes. It will be chewy rather than crunchy.

Stir the lime juice with the ají amarillo paste, garlic and salt. Toss the trout with this leche de tigre and the onion, and leave it for 3 to 5 minutes, until the edges just turn opaque and the centre is still glossy.
Fold in the cilantro. Serve the ceviche right away with its juices, the warm sweet potato and boiled corn alongside, and the toasted corn on top.
tip: Ask your fishmonger for trout that is safe to eat raw, and keep it cold until you cut it. If you are pregnant or have a weakened immune system, skip the raw version: cook the trout cubes in a hot pan until opaque all the way through, 3 to 4 minutes, then dress them. Ceviche is always made fresh and is not a leftover.
ingredients: safe to eat raw, skinned and cut into 2 cm cubes
peeled and cut into thick rounds

name: Arroz, feijão and grilled lime chicken with collards and vinagrete
inspiredBy: Brazilian prato feito
about: The everyday Brazilian plate: garlicky grilled chicken, white rice, pinto beans simmered with onion and bay, quick sautéed collards (couve) and a fresh tomato vinagrete, with orange slices to finish. It is **big on protein**, and the orange's vitamin C helps your body absorb the iron from the beans and collards. It makes two portions.
steps: Marinate the chicken in the lime juice, half the garlic, the paprika and a pinch of salt for 15 minutes while you start the rice.
Cook the rice with a little under twice its volume of water and a pinch of salt in a covered pot, about 15 minutes. Fluff with a fork.

Warm a third of the oil in a pot and cook half the onion and the remaining garlic for 3 minutes. Add the beans, bay leaf and enough water to just cover them, and simmer 15 minutes, mashing a few beans against the side to thicken the broth. Season with a pinch of salt.
Stir the tomato, the remaining raw onion, the cilantro and the vinegar with a pinch of salt for the vinagrete.
Sear the chicken in the second third of the oil in a very hot pan, in batches if it crowds, for 4 to 5 minutes a side, until browned and cooked through. Rest it for 3 minutes, then slice.
Cook the collards in the last third of the oil in a wide pan over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes, until bright green and just tender.
Plate the rice, beans, chicken, collards and vinagrete with orange slices on the side. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: Slice the chicken before packing the leftover so it reheats evenly.
ingredients: butterflied or sliced into thin cutlets
stems removed, sliced into thin ribbons

name: Cuban picadillo with black beans, rice and sweet plantain
inspiredBy: Cuban picadillo a la habanera
about: Lean beef simmered in a sofrito of onion, sweet pepper and garlic with tomato, olives and a splash of vinegar, with black beans stirred in and spooned over rice with sweet fried plantain. The plantain and beans bring the **energy for training**, and the beef the protein. It makes two portions.
steps: Cook the rice in a covered pot with a little under twice its volume of water and a pinch of salt, about 15 minutes.
Warm two thirds of the oil in a wide skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion, pepper and garlic with the cumin and oregano for 6 minutes, until soft and sweet. This is the sofrito.
Add the beef and break it up, cooking 6 minutes until no longer pink. Stir in the tomato, bay leaf, vinegar, a splash of water and the rest of the salt, and simmer 12 minutes until saucy.
Stir in the black beans and the olives and simmer 3 minutes more.
Fry the plantain in the remaining oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes a side, until deeply golden and caramelized at the edges.
Serve the picadillo over the rice with the plantain alongside. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: Add a spoonful of raisins with the olives if you like the sweet and salty Cuban way.

name: Lighter feijoada with pork, black beans, collards and orange
inspiredBy: Brazilian feijoada completa, lightened
about: Brazil's Saturday pot, lightened: lean pork tenderloin simmered until tender, then black beans, garlic, bay and a little chicken linguiça for smoke, served over rice with sautéed collards and orange slices. It is a **weekend project** that fills the house with its smell and makes two portions, one for Sunday's lunch.
steps: Put the pork in a heavy pot with the bay leaf, a pinch of the salt and enough water to cover by 5 cm. Bring to a boil and skim off the foam, then turn it down to a few lazy bubbles, partly cover and cook for 40 minutes, until the pork is nearly tender. A hard boil makes lean pork stringy.
In a skillet, warm half the oil and cook the onion and garlic with the smoked paprika for 6 minutes until golden and sweet.

Stir the sofrito, the black beans and the linguiça slices into the pot. Simmer, uncovered, 20 to 25 minutes, until the broth is thick and glossy. Mash a ladleful of beans against the side of the pot to thicken it more, and season with the rest of the salt.
Cook the rice in a covered pot with a little under twice its volume of water, about 15 minutes.
Sauté the collards in the remaining oil in a wide pan over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes, until bright green.
Serve the feijoada over rice, with the collards and orange slices, which cut the richness. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: A pressure cooker does the pork in 10 minutes at high pressure. Release it, add the sofrito, beans and linguiça, and simmer 15 minutes, uncovered.
ingredients: stems removed, sliced into thin ribbons

name: Salmon moqueca with coconut, tomato and rice
inspiredBy: Brazilian moqueca baiana, with colorau in place of dendê oil
about: A Bahian-style fish stew: salmon simmered gently with tomato, peppers, onion, cilantro and a little coconut milk, golden with urucum, and spooned over fluffy rice. Salmon brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the coconut milk is just a splash, enough for silkiness without much saturated fat.
steps: Marinate the salmon with the lime juice, half the garlic and a pinch of the salt while you start the rice.
Rinse the rice, then cook it in a covered pot with a little under twice its volume of water and a pinch of salt for about 15 minutes, until tender.
Warm the oil in a wide, shallow pan. Layer in half the onion, tomato and red pepper, then the salmon, then the rest of the vegetables. Scatter on the remaining garlic and the colorau.

Pour the coconut milk, loosened with a splash of water, around the edges. Cover and simmer gently for 12 to 15 minutes, until the salmon flakes and the sauce has thickened. Do not stir; spoon the liquid over the fish instead.
Season with the remaining salt, scatter on the cilantro and serve over the rice, with plenty of sauce.
tip: In Bahia, moqueca comes with rice and pirão, the broth thickened with cassava flour. If you have some, whisk a spoonful into a ladle of the sauce and simmer for a minute.
ingredients: skin removed, cut into large chunks

name: Chile-lime boiled eggs with cucumber
inspiredBy: Mexican street snacks of cucumber with chile and lime
about: Boiled eggs with crunchy cucumber sticks, dressed the Mexican street way with lime, chili and salt. The eggs give you **high-quality protein and choline**, and the crunch makes it feel like a snack.
steps: Lower the eggs into a pot of boiling water and cook 9 minutes. Cool them under cold water, peel and halve.
Toss the cucumber with the lime juice, chili and half the salt.
Sprinkle the remaining salt over the eggs and serve them with the cucumber.
tip: Boil a batch of eggs on Sunday; they keep five days in the shell.

name: Chicken tostadas with cucumber, lime and chipotle crema
inspiredBy: Mexican tostadas de pollo, with a nod to tinga
about: Poached shredded chicken tossed in a smoky chipotle crema and piled on crisp baked tostadas with lime-dressed cucumber and avocado. A **high-protein snack** without the frying, with the chipotle as a nod to tinga.
steps: Heat the oven to 200C and bake the tortillas on a tray for 8 to 10 minutes until crisp.
Stir the yogurt with the chipotle and half the lime juice for the crema. Toss the cucumber with the rest of the lime juice and a pinch of salt.
Simmer the chicken in a small pot of lightly salted water with the cilantro stems for 12 to 14 minutes, until cooked through. Cool slightly, shred with two forks, and toss with half the crema.
Pile the chicken on the tostadas, top with cucumber, avocado, the rest of the crema and the cilantro leaves.
tip: Poach double the chicken when you are cooking dinner and the tostadas take 5 minutes.
ingredients: cut into wedges or left whole
stems for the pot, leaves chopped

name: Requesón-style cottage cheese with pineapple and cinnamon
inspiredBy: Mexican requesón with fruit
about: Soft, creamy cottage cheese, close to Mexico's requesón, with sweet pineapple, lime and cinnamon. A **cool, high-protein snack** that takes two minutes.
steps: Spoon the cottage cheese into a bowl and top with the pineapple.
Grate over a little lime zest, squeeze on the juice, and dust with cinnamon.
Scatter on the pepitas.

name: Cottage cheese with pico de gallo and baked totopos
inspiredBy: Mexican pico de gallo
about: Creamy cottage cheese topped with a fresh pico de gallo of tomato, onion, jalapeño and cilantro, with crisp baked corn totopos for scooping. **Cool, tangy and high in protein**, it is a savoury answer to a sweet snack.
steps: Heat the oven to 200C. Lay the tortilla wedges on a tray and bake 8 to 10 minutes until crisp and lightly golden.
Stir the tomato, onion, jalapeño, cilantro, lime juice and salt together for the pico de gallo.
Spoon the cottage cheese into a bowl, top with the pico and serve with the totopos.

name: Pineapple yogurt with chile, lime and pepitas
inspiredBy: Mexican fruit with chile and lime
about: Thick yogurt with sweet pineapple, a squeeze of lime, a pinch of chili and toasted pepitas, the way fruit is eaten with chile and lime across Mexico. The yogurt keeps it **protein-forward**, the pineapple keeps it a treat.
steps: Spoon the yogurt into a bowl and top with the pineapple.
Squeeze on the lime and sprinkle with a pinch of chili.
Finish with the toasted pepitas.

name: Sardine tostadas with cucumber, lime and avocado
inspiredBy: Mexican tostadas de sardina
about: Canned sardines, with their soft bones, mashed gently onto crisp corn tostadas with cucumber, red onion, avocado and a squeeze of lime. Sardines bring **omega-3, calcium and vitamin D** in one snack, and tostadas de sardina are a real Mexican favourite.
steps: Heat the oven to 200C and bake the tortillas on a tray for 8 to 10 minutes until crisp.
Toss the cucumber, red onion, jalapeño and cilantro with half the lime juice.
Mash the sardines lightly with the rest of the lime, then spread over the tostadas and top with the cucumber mix and avocado.
tip: If there is sardine left in the can, keep it covered in the fridge and eat it within 2 days, mashed with lime on a tostada.
ingredients: cut into wedges or left whole

name: Black bean and egg white tostadas with salsa
inspiredBy: Mexican tostadas with frijoles
about: Crisp corn tostadas topped with mashed black beans, soft-scrambled egg whites and a quick fresh salsa. A savoury, **high-protein snack** with the beans for fibre.
steps: Heat the oven to 200C and bake the tortillas on a tray for 8 to 10 minutes until crisp.
Toss the tomato, onion, jalapeño and cilantro with the lime juice and a pinch of salt to make the salsa.
Warm the beans in a small pot with a splash of water, mashing them until spreadable.
Scramble the egg whites in the oil in a nonstick pan over medium-low heat until just set, about 2 minutes, and season with a pinch of salt.
Spread the beans over the tostadas, top with the eggs and finish with the salsa.
ingredients: cut into wedges or left whole

name: Egg white tacos with tomato, onion and chile
inspiredBy: Mexican huevos a la mexicana
about: Egg whites scrambled the way Mexico does huevos a la mexicana, with tomato, onion and jalapeño, folded into warm corn tortillas with a squeeze of lime. A **light, very high-protein snack** that is quick and lean.
steps: Warm a little oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat and cook the onion and jalapeño for 2 minutes, until soft.
Add the tomato and cook 2 minutes more, until it has softened and lost its raw edge.
Pour in the egg whites with a pinch of salt and stir gently over medium-low heat, taking the pan off the heat while they are still glossy; the pan finishes them. Overcooked whites go rubbery.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan, fill them with the eggs and finish with cilantro and a squeeze of lime.
tip: Buy egg whites by the carton. This week uses a lot of them, and you won't be left with a bowl of yolks.

name: Griddled arepa with soft egg whites and tomato hogao
inspiredBy: Colombian arepa with hogao
about: A golden Colombian arepa split open and filled with soft-scrambled egg whites and a warm tomato and onion hogao. The corn arepa gives you **carbs for training** and the egg whites add protein without much fat.
steps: Stir the corn flour with a pinch of the salt and enough warm water to make a soft dough. Rest it 5 minutes, then shape into a thick patty.
Cook the arepa in a lightly oiled nonstick skillet over medium heat, about 5 minutes a side, until golden and firm when tapped.
In a small pan, soften the onion and garlic in a little oil for 2 minutes. Add the tomato and cumin and cook 4 minutes into a thick hogao. Spoon a little out for the top.
Pour the egg whites into the rest of the hogao with the rest of the salt and stir gently until just set, about 2 minutes.
Split the arepa, fill it with the eggs and spoon the saved hogao on top.

name: Ful medames with boiled eggs, tomato and warm pita
inspiredBy: Egyptian ful medames
about: Egypt's breakfast of creamy fava beans, warmed with garlic and cumin, mashed a little and finished with lemon, a spoonful of tahini and a little olive oil. Boiled eggs and warm pita make it a proper plate. The beans and eggs together give you **plenty of protein and fibre** before the day starts.
steps: Lower the eggs into a small pot of boiling water and simmer for 8 minutes, then cool them under cold water and peel.
Warm the olive oil in a saucepan, add the garlic and cumin and stir for 30 seconds until it smells toasty.

Tip in the fava beans with a splash of water (or their cooking liquid, if you cooked them from dried), add the salt and simmer for 5 minutes, mashing about a third of the beans with a fork so it goes thick and creamy. Stir in the tahini and half the lemon juice.
Toss the tomato and parsley with the rest of the lemon juice and a pinch of Aleppo pepper.
Spoon the ful into a bowl, top with the halved eggs and the tomato salad, and serve with warm pita.
tip: Canned ful medames is what many Egyptian homes use: rinse it very well and taste before you salt, as it usually needs little or none. Boil the eggs the night before and breakfast takes about 6 minutes.
ingredients: small brown ful beans, canned and well rinsed, or cooked from dried

name: Shakshuka with chickpeas and warm pita
inspiredBy: Egyptian and Levantine shakshuka
about: Eggs baked in a bubbling pan of tomato, red pepper and cumin, with chickpeas for body and warm pita for scooping up every last bit. The peppers and tomato bring plenty of vitamin C, and the eggs and chickpeas give it **a solid dose of protein** before the day gets going.
steps: Warm the oil in a wide, deep pan over medium heat and cook the onion and pepper until soft, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, paprika, cumin and Aleppo pepper and cook for a minute until fragrant.
Add the grated tomatoes, chickpeas and salt and simmer for 12 to 15 minutes, until the sauce is thick enough to hold a dent.
Make little wells with a spoon, crack the eggs in, cover and cook on low for 5 to 6 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks still wobble.
Scatter the parsley over the top and eat straight from the pan with warm pita.
tip: Make the sauce the night before and keep it 2 days. Warm it, then crack in the eggs.

name: Thick yogurt bowl with dates, walnuts and toasted oats
inspiredBy: Gulf and Levantine yogurt with dates
about: Thick, tangy yogurt topped with chewy chopped dates, toasted walnuts and oats, with a hint of cardamom. Dates, yogurt and walnuts are an old Levantine and Gulf combination. The yogurt brings **a big dose of protein and calcium**, and the walnuts add omega-3.
steps: Toast the oats and walnuts in a dry pan over medium heat for 3 minutes, until they smell nutty. Tip them onto a plate to cool.
Mash the dates into the yogurt with the cardamom so the sweetness runs through, then spoon it into a bowl.
Top with the toasted oats and walnuts and a pinch of cinnamon.
tip: At larger sizes, use a deep bowl. Toast a few days' worth of oats and walnuts at once and keep them in a jar.

name: Chicken and chickpea fatteh with garlic yogurt
inspiredBy: Syrian and Lebanese fatteh
about: A Levantine layered dish: crisp toasted pita, warm spiced chickpeas and shredded chicken, all under a cool garlicky yogurt and tahini sauce with toasted almonds. It is crunchy, creamy and lemony all at once. The chicken and yogurt give you **plenty of protein for the afternoon**.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 C. Tear the pita into bite-size pieces, toss with half the oil and bake for 8 minutes, until golden and crisp.
Cover the chicken with water in a small pot, add a pinch of salt and simmer gently for 14 minutes, until cooked through. Lift it out and shred it with two forks.
Warm the chickpeas in a little of the chicken cooking water with the cumin, cinnamon and paprika until hot.
Stir the yogurt with the tahini, garlic, lemon juice and a pinch of salt.

Toast the almonds in the rest of the oil in a small pan until golden. Pile the crisp pita in a shallow bowl, top with the chickpeas and chicken, spoon over the yogurt and finish with the almonds and parsley.
tip: Bake the pita bits ahead and assemble just before eating, so they stay crisp.

name: Shish tawook with garlicky rice and tomato cucumber salad
inspiredBy: Lebanese and Turkish chicken skewers
about: Chicken breast marinated in lemon, garlic, tomato paste and warm spices, grilled until browned at the edges, with fluffy garlicky rice and a crisp tomato, cucumber and carrot salad. A little olive oil and a good marinade keep lean chicken juicy. It makes **two big, high-protein portions**, so tomorrow's lunch is done.
steps: Mix the tomato paste, half the lemon juice, half the garlic, the paprika, baharat, pepper, a little salt and half the oil in a bowl. Add the chicken, turn to coat and marinate for at least 30 minutes.

Rinse the rice. Warm the remaining oil in a pot, stir in the rest of the garlic for 30 seconds, add the rice, a pinch of salt and a little less than twice its volume of water. Bring to a boil, cover and simmer on low for about 15 minutes, until the water is absorbed. Rest it, covered, for 5 minutes.
Thread the chicken onto skewers, or spread it on a tray. Grill or broil on high for 12 to 14 minutes, turning once, until browned in places and cooked through.
Toss the tomato, cucumber, carrot, onion and parsley with the remaining lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Serve the chicken over the rice with the salad. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: Marinate 30 minutes to 8 hours. Longer and the lemon turns breast chalky. Cook enough rice for two portions and the leftover lunch is ready.

name: Lean beef and lamb kofta in tomato and pepper sauce with pita
inspiredBy: Egyptian kofta bil salsa and Lebanese kafta bi banadoura
about: Little kofta made with lean beef and a smaller share of lean lamb, grated onion, parsley and baharat, simmered in a garlicky tomato and pepper sauce and served with warm pita. Mixing the two meats keeps the flavour but **keeps saturated fat low**. It makes two portions, so tomorrow's lunch is done.
steps: Squeeze the grated onion over a bowl and keep the juice. Mix the beef, lamb, squeezed onion, half the parsley, half the garlic, the baharat, cinnamon, a little salt and a spoonful of the onion juice with your hands, squeezing until it holds together. Shape into small ovals and chill them for 20 minutes so they hold.
Warm the oil in a wide, deep pan and brown the kofta for about 6 minutes, turning, then lift them out.
In the same pan, soften the diced onion and pepper for 6 minutes. Stir in the rest of the garlic, the cumin and the tomato paste for a minute.

Add the grated tomatoes and a pinch of salt, return the kofta and simmer gently for 15 to 20 minutes, until the sauce is thick and the kofta are cooked through. Add a splash of water only if the sauce catches.
Scatter the sumac and the rest of the parsley over the top and serve with warm pita. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: Shape the kofta the night before. They hold together better after a night in the fridge.
ingredients: ask the butcher to mince lean leg, or use the leanest ground lamb

name: Grilled mackerel with sumac onions and herby bulgur pilaf
inspiredBy: Turkish uskumru izgara with pilav
about: Rich, oily mackerel fillets, broiled until the skin crackles, with a sharp pile of sumac onions and a Turkish-style bulgur pilaf with chickpeas, lots of parsley and a squeeze of lemon. The acid cuts the richness beautifully. Mackerel is a big source of **omega-3 and vitamin D**.
steps: Toss the red onion with the sumac, a squeeze of the lemon juice, half the parsley and a pinch of salt. Set it aside so it softens.
Warm half the oil in a pot and cook the diced onion until soft and golden, about 6 minutes. Stir in the cinnamon and Aleppo pepper for 30 seconds.

Add the bulgur, chickpeas, salt and a little over its volume of water, bring to a boil, cover and simmer on low for 12 minutes. Rest, covered, for 5 minutes, then fluff and fold in the rest of the parsley.
Heat the broiler to high. Rub the mackerel with the rest of the oil and a pinch of salt, lay it skin side up on a tray and broil for 5 to 6 minutes, until the skin blisters and the flesh flakes.
Serve the fish over the pilaf with the sumac onions and the rest of the lemon juice squeezed over.
tip: Ask the fishmonger to fillet the mackerel and pull out the pin bones.

name: Turkish tuna and white bean piyaz with boiled egg
inspiredBy: Turkish piyaz, with tuna
about: A cool Turkish bean salad with sumac-bright red onion, grated carrot, tomato, plenty of parsley and chunks of tuna and boiled egg, dressed with lemon and olive oil. Warm pita is on the side. It is easy, filling and **high in protein and fibre** with nothing to cook but an egg.
steps: Boil the egg, or eggs, for 8 minutes, cool under cold water and peel.
Rub the red onion with the sumac and a pinch of salt for a minute to soften and sharpen it.
Toss the beans with the onion, carrot, parsley, tomato, lemon juice, olive oil and Aleppo pepper, and season to taste.
Flake the tuna over the top, add the egg, cut into quarters, and eat with warm pita.
tip: Boil the egg, or eggs, the night before and the whole lunch comes together in 5 minutes.

name: Beef and okra stew (bamia) with rice
inspiredBy: Egyptian bamia
about: A tomatoey Egyptian and Levantine stew of tender lean beef and okra with garlic and parsley, spooned over rice. Lemon at the end keeps it bright. Beef and okra together bring **iron, magnesium and a lot of fibre**, and it tastes even better the next day.
steps: Warm most of the oil in a heavy pot and brown the beef in two batches, about 5 minutes a batch. Lift it out.
Cook the onion in the same pot until soft and golden, about 6 minutes. Stir in half the garlic, the allspice, cinnamon and tomato paste for a minute.
Return the beef, add the passata, some water to just cover, the salt and pepper. Cover and simmer gently for 45 minutes, until the beef is nearly tender.
Add the okra whole, cover again and cook for 15 minutes more, until the okra is soft but not falling apart. Stir as little as you can.
Meanwhile, cook the rice with a pinch of salt and a little less than twice its volume of water, covered, on low for 15 minutes.

Warm the last of the oil in a small pan and fry the rest of the garlic with the ground coriander for a minute, until fragrant. Stir this ta'leya into the stew with the lemon juice and parsley, and serve over the rice. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: Frozen whole okra works, straight from the freezer. A pressure cooker does the beef in 20 minutes; add the okra after pressure is released.
ingredients: passata or crushed tomatoes, no salt added (not paste)

name: Baharat salmon with saffron rice, roasted cauliflower and carrots, and lemon tahini
inspiredBy: Gulf spiced fish and rice
about: Salmon rubbed with baharat and roasted until just flaking, on saffron-scented rice with charred cauliflower, carrots and tomatoes and a lemony tahini drizzle. It borrows the spices and the fish-and-rice idea of Gulf kitchens. Salmon delivers **omega-3, vitamin D and B12**.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 C. Toss the cauliflower, carrots and tomatoes with half the oil, the cumin and a pinch of salt on a tray and roast for 15 minutes.

Steep the saffron in a few spoonfuls of hot water. Warm the rest of the oil in a pot and soften the onion for 5 minutes. Add the rinsed rice, stir for a minute, then pour in a little less than twice its volume of water with the saffron and a pinch of salt. Cover and cook on low for 15 minutes, then rest for 5.
Rub the salmon with the baharat and ground dried lime. Nestle it among the vegetables and roast for 10 to 12 minutes more, until it just flakes.
Whisk the tahini with half the lemon juice, the garlic and a pinch of salt, adding only a spoonful of cold water until it pours like thick cream. Squeeze the rest of the lemon over the salmon.
Toast the almonds in a dry pan. Fluff the rice, fold in the parsley, and serve with the salmon, vegetables, the almonds and a big drizzle of tahini.
tip: If you can't find dried lime, use a little extra lemon and a pinch of sumac.

name: Hummus with warm spiced beef and almonds
inspiredBy: Lebanese hummus bil lahme
about: A big swoop of creamy, lemony hummus topped with sizzling lean beef spiced with allspice and cinnamon, toasted almonds and parsley, with pita and cucumber to scoop. It is a Levantine mezze turned into a proper lunch. The beef and chickpeas together give you **protein and iron**.
steps: Blend the chickpeas with the tahini, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, a pinch of salt and 3 or 4 spoonfuls of ice-cold water until smooth and fluffy. Taste and add more lemon or salt if it needs it.
Toast the almonds in a dry pan until golden, then set them aside.

Warm the oil in the same pan and cook the onion for 3 minutes. Add the beef, allspice, cinnamon and a pinch of salt and cook for 6 to 7 minutes, breaking it up, until browned and crumbly. Add a splash of water and let it bubble for a minute so the beef stays juicy.
Swoop the hummus into a wide bowl, pile the warm beef on top and scatter the almonds and parsley.
Serve with warm pita and cucumber.
tip: Hummus is best made fresh, but it keeps 3 days in a covered container in the fridge.

name: Maqluba-style chicken and rice with cauliflower and eggplant
inspiredBy: Palestinian and Syrian maqluba
about: The upside-down pot of Palestine, Jordan and Syria: spiced chicken, roasted eggplant, cauliflower, carrot and tomato layered under rice, then turned out like a cake. It is the weekend project, with a cool cucumber yogurt on the side. The chicken and yogurt carry **plenty of protein**, and it makes two portions.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 C. Toss the eggplant, cauliflower and carrot coins with half the oil and a pinch of salt on a tray and roast for 20 minutes, until browned at the edges.

Rub the chicken with the baharat, turmeric, cinnamon, allspice and a little salt. Brown it in the rest of the oil in a wide, heavy pot for 3 to 4 minutes a side, then lift it out. Soften the onion and garlic in the same pot for 3 minutes and scoop them onto a plate.

Rinse the rice until the water runs clear. Layer the tomato slices and the softened onion on the bottom of the pot, then the chicken, then the roasted vegetables and the bay leaf. Pour the rice over the top and press it down.
Pour in enough hot water to cover the rice by about a finger's width, add a pinch of salt, bring to a boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 30 minutes. Rest for 10 minutes, covered.
Toast the almonds in a dry pan. Run a knife around the pot, put a large plate on top and flip it in one confident move. Scatter with almonds.
Stir the yogurt with the cucumber and a pinch of salt and serve alongside. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: Cut the chicken in thick pieces and tuck it under the vegetables so it stays moist. If flipping the pot feels scary, serve it straight from the pot.

name: Lean lamb and white bean stew (kuru fasulye) with bulgur pilaf
inspiredBy: Turkish kuru fasulye with pilav
about: A Turkish favourite: creamy white beans simmered with lean lamb, tomato and a spoonful of paprika-spiked tomato paste, served over a bulgur pilaf with a sharp parsley and onion salad. The beans and lamb give you **iron, zinc and slow-burning fuel** for training.
steps: Warm half the oil in a pot and brown the lamb for about 5 minutes. Add the onion and cook until soft, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, tomato paste, paprika and Aleppo pepper for a minute, then add the passata, salt, pepper and enough water to just cover.
Cover and simmer for 40 minutes, until the lamb is tender. Add the beans and cook for 10 more minutes so the sauce goes thick.
Meanwhile, warm the rest of the oil in a small pot, stir in the bulgur for a minute, then add a little over its volume of water and a pinch of salt. Cover and simmer for 12 minutes, then rest for 5.
Toss the red onion with the sumac and parsley.
Spoon the stew over the bulgur and pile the onion salad on top.
tip: Canned beans keep this quick. Make a double pot and freeze the second portion; it keeps 3 months.
ingredients: passata or crushed tomatoes, no salt added (not paste)

name: Lupini beans with lemon, cumin and tomato
inspiredBy: Egyptian termis
about: Egypt's street snack: firm, nutty lupini beans tossed with lemon, cumin and olive oil, with juicy tomato wedges. Squeeze each bean out of its thin skin, as people do in Egypt. They are a surprisingly **high-protein, high-fibre** bean you can eat with your fingers.
steps: Rinse the lupini beans well under cold water, because they are salty.
Toss them with the lemon juice, olive oil, cumin and Aleppo pepper.
Serve with the tomato wedges. Squeeze each bean out of its thin skin and eat the inside.

name: Thick yogurt with walnuts, pomegranate and mint
inspiredBy: Levantine yogurt
about: Cool, thick yogurt scattered with juicy pomegranate seeds, toasted walnuts and a pinch of dried mint. Sweet, sharp and crunchy, and **a quick hit of protein and calcium**.
steps: Spoon the yogurt into a bowl.
Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 2 minutes until they smell nutty.
Scatter the pomegranate seeds and walnuts over the yogurt and finish with the dried mint.

name: Boiled eggs with dukkah, tomato and warm pita
inspiredBy: Egyptian eggs and dukkah
about: Jammy boiled eggs, split and dusted with dukkah, with sweet ripe tomato, a squeeze of lemon and a little warm pita. The nuts and spices make plain eggs taste like an Egyptian breakfast mezze, and it is **an easy, high-protein snack**.
steps: Lower the eggs into boiling water and simmer for 7 minutes, then cool under cold water and peel.
Arrange the tomato wedges on a plate, squeeze over the lemon and drizzle with the olive oil.
Halve the eggs, dip the cut sides in the dukkah and eat with the tomato and warm pita.

name: Hummus with garlic lemon chicken strips and carrot sticks
inspiredBy: Levantine hummus with shawarma-style chicken
about: Quick hummus with strips of garlicky, lemony chicken breast seared in a hot pan, and crunchy carrot sticks to scoop. It is like a shawarma plate in snack form, and **keeps your protein topped up through the afternoon**.
steps: Blend the chickpeas with the tahini, half the lemon juice, half the garlic, half the cumin, a pinch of salt and a few spoonfuls of cold water until smooth, using a stick blender in a tall jar, or mash very well with a fork for a rustic hummus.
Toss the chicken with the rest of the garlic and cumin, the paprika and a pinch of salt.
Heat the oil in a pan over high heat and sear the chicken for 4 to 5 minutes, until golden and cooked through. Squeeze over the rest of the lemon.
Spoon the hummus into a bowl, lay the chicken on top and serve with the carrot sticks.

name: Labneh with za'atar, cucumber, mint and carrot sticks
inspiredBy: Levantine labneh and za'atar
about: Thick, tangy labneh swirled with olive oil and za'atar, with cool cucumber, mint and carrot sticks to scoop it up. A classic Levantine breakfast, brought in as a snack, with **protein and a little calcium** in a few minutes.
steps: Spread the labneh in a shallow bowl and make a swirl with the back of a spoon.
Drizzle with the olive oil and sprinkle with the za'atar.
Scatter the cucumber and mint over the top and scoop it up with the carrot sticks.

name: White cheese with tomato, olives and mint
inspiredBy: Egyptian gebna beida
about: Salty, creamy Egyptian-style white cheese with ripe tomato, a few olives and fresh mint. It is the sort of plate you'd find on the table at any meal, and it gives you **protein and calcium** with very little effort.
steps: Slice the cheese and lay it on a plate with the tomato.
Scatter the olives and mint over the top and eat with a fork.
tip: No gebna beida nearby? Any mild white brined cheese works, such as Bulgarian white cheese or a mild feta. Rinse it if it tastes very salty.

name: Smashed sardines on toasted pita with sumac onion and tomato
inspiredBy: Egyptian sardine sandwich
about: Oily sardines smashed with lemon and sumac onto crisp toasted pita, with sweet tomato and a pile of fresh parsley. It is a classic Egyptian and Mediterranean quick bite, sharp and crunchy. Sardines bring **omega-3 and calcium from the soft bones**.
steps: Toast the pita until crisp and golden. Rub the red onion with the sumac and a squeeze of the lemon juice and let it sit for a few minutes.
Mash the sardines roughly with the rest of the lemon juice and the olive oil.
Pile the tomato and the sardines on the pita and top with the sumac onion, the parsley and a pinch of Aleppo pepper.
tip: Opened sardines keep 2 days in a covered container in the fridge. Mash the rest with lemon and parsley for tomorrow's toast.

name: Tuna, red pepper and parsley pita pocket
inspiredBy: Egyptian and Levantine tuna sandwich
about: Flaked tuna with crunchy red pepper, tomato, parsley, lemon and cumin stuffed into a warm pita pocket. It is a light bite you can eat on the go, with **lean protein** and not much else to wash up.
steps: Flake the tuna into a bowl with the lemon juice, olive oil and cumin.
Warm the pita and open the pocket.
Stuff it with the red pepper, tomato, parsley and tuna.

name: Thick cacik with cucumber, garlic and mint
inspiredBy: Turkish cacik
about: Turkish cacik made thick enough to eat with a spoon: strained-style Greek yogurt with grated cucumber, garlic, mint and a thread of olive oil. It is cool and sharp, and a big bowl is **a lean, calcium-rich hit of protein**.
steps: Squeeze the grated cucumber in your hands to get rid of the extra water.
Stir it into the yogurt with the garlic, fresh mint, lemon juice and salt.
Spoon into a bowl, drizzle with the olive oil and rub the dried mint over the top.

name: Herb eggah with extra egg whites, tomato and pita
inspiredBy: Egyptian eggah and Levantine ijjeh
about: Eggah, called ijjeh in Lebanon and Syria, is a thick, herby omelette cut into wedges. This one leans on egg whites so it stays light and high in protein, with a whole egg for flavour and colour. Parsley, onion and a pinch of baharat do the work, and it gives you **over 30 g of protein**, warm or cold.
steps: Warm the oil in a small non-stick pan over medium heat and soften the onion for 3 minutes.
Beat the whole egg and the egg whites with the parsley, baharat, pepper and salt.
Pour the eggs into the pan, cover and cook on low for 6 to 7 minutes, until the top is just set. Slide it onto a plate and cut into wedges.
Serve warm or cold with the tomato and warm pita.

name: Shakshuka masri, eggs in garlicky tomato and red pepper with baladi bread
inspiredBy: Egyptian shakshuka, the home version with plenty of sweet red pepper, garlic and cumin
about: Two eggs set in a thick, garlicky tomato sauce with soft sweet red pepper and a pinch of chili, finished with a spoonful of nutty dukkah and served with warm bread for scooping. The eggs bring **protein and choline**, and the dukkah brings vitamin E.
steps: Warm the olive oil in a small, wide pan. Cook the onion and red pepper over medium heat until the onion is soft and just golden, about 6 minutes.
Add the garlic, cumin, paprika and chili and stir for 30 seconds, until it smells toasty.
Pour in the passata with the salt and a splash of water. Simmer, stirring now and then, until it turns thick and jammy, about 8 minutes.
Make two little wells with the back of a spoon and crack an egg into each. Cover and cook on low for 4 to 5 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks are still soft.
Scatter with the parsley and finish with a spoonful of dukkah, the way Egyptians do with eggs. Warm the bread in a dry pan, tear it up and scoop.
tip: Make the tomato sauce the night before and keep it in the fridge. In the morning, heat it, crack in the eggs and breakfast is ready in 8 minutes.
ingredients: passata or tomato sauce, no salt added

name: Ful medames with tinned sardines, tahini, lemon and cucumber
inspiredBy: Cairo and Alexandria ful, with the tinned sardines many Egyptians keep in the cupboard for a quick plate
about: Warm, creamy fava beans mashed with garlic, cumin and lemon, with tinned sardines broken over the top, a drizzle of tahini and a pile of cucumber, onion and parsley. The beans bring **fibre, folate and iron**, and the sardines add omega-3, B12 and calcium from their soft bones.
steps: Mash the garlic with the salt into a paste. Warm the beans with a splash of water in a small pot with the garlic and cumin, stirring now and then, until steaming hot, about 5 minutes.
Mash roughly with a fork, leaving some whole beans. Stir in the lemon juice and most of the olive oil.
Stir the tahini with a spoonful of water until it pours like thin cream.
Spoon the ful into a shallow bowl. Break the sardines over the top, drizzle with the tahini and the rest of the oil, and pile on the cucumber, onion and parsley. Add the shatta on the side.
Warm the bread in a dry pan or the toaster, tear it up and scoop.
tip: Cook a big batch of dried fava, or open a tin with no salt added and drain it, and keep the rest for the next ful morning. Dried fava turns creamy in a slow cooker or a pressure cooker.
ingredients: cooked from dried, or a tin with no salt added, drained
tinned in water or brine, drained

name: Ful medames with tahini, lemon and a boiled egg
inspiredBy: the Cairo breakfast ful, the way a home cook finishes it with tahini, lemon and an egg
about: Warm, creamy fava beans mashed with garlic, cumin and lemon, with a boiled egg, a drizzle of tahini and a pile of tomato, onion and parsley. The beans bring **fibre, folate and iron**, and the egg adds choline.
steps: Use an egg boiled the night before, or lower one into boiling water for 8 minutes, then cool it under cold water and peel.
Mash the garlic with the salt into a paste. Warm the beans with a splash of water in a small pot with the garlic and cumin, stirring now and then, until steaming hot, about 5 minutes.
Mash roughly with a fork, leaving some whole beans. Stir in the lemon juice and most of the olive oil.
Stir the tahini with a spoonful of water until it pours like thin cream.
Spoon the ful into a shallow bowl. Drizzle with the tahini and the rest of the oil, pile on the tomato, onion and parsley, and set the halved egg on top. Add the shatta on the side.
Warm the bread in a dry pan or the toaster, tear it up and scoop.
tip: Boil Thursday's and Friday's eggs together on Wednesday night. They keep 4 days in the fridge.
ingredients: cooked from dried, or a tin with no salt added, drained

name: Eggs with basterma-style pastrami and tomato, with olives and baladi bread
inspiredBy: the Cairo breakfast of eggs fried with basterma, made here with beef pastrami as the nearest widely sold cured beef
about: Peppery, smoky cured beef crisped in the pan, then softened tomato and red pepper with two eggs cooked right on top and a spoonful of dukkah to finish. Salty and rich, so a little goes a long way. The eggs and beef bring **protein, choline and B12**.
steps: Warm the olive oil in a small pan. Add the pastrami strips and fry for about 2 minutes, until the edges are crisp and it smells peppery and smoky.
Add the tomato and red pepper and cook until they soften, about 4 minutes.

Crack the eggs over the top, sprinkle with the cumin and pepper, cover and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks still soft. The pastrami is salty, so you should not need extra salt.
Scatter with parsley and finish with a spoonful of dukkah. Serve with the olives and warm bread.
tip: Real basterma has a fenugreek and garlic crust. If you find it at a Middle Eastern shop or an Armenian deli, use it the same way.
ingredients: sliced thin, then cut in strips
black olives, rinsed, on the side

name: Sudanese-style ful with egg, white cheese, tomato, sesame and rocket
inspiredBy: the Sudanese breakfast ful, finished with white cheese, sesame and plenty of raw rocket
about: Fava beans mashed with garlic, lemon and chili, with a boiled egg, crumbled white cheese, tomato, onion, toasted sesame and a big handful of peppery rocket. It is a different mood from Egyptian ful. The beans and rocket bring **iron, folate and vitamin K**, and the egg and cheese add choline and calcium.
steps: Use an egg boiled the night before, or lower one into boiling water for 8 minutes, then cool it under cold water and peel.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan until golden and nutty, about 2 minutes.
Mash the garlic with the salt into a paste. Warm the beans with a splash of water, the garlic, cumin and the shatta, stirring, until steaming hot, about 5 minutes.
Mash with a fork until mostly creamy. Stir in the lemon juice and half the olive oil.
Spoon into a shallow bowl. Pour the rest of the olive oil over the middle and scatter on the white cheese, tomato, onion, sesame and rocket. Halve the egg and set it on top.
Warm the bread and tear it up to scoop.
tip: In Sudan the oil is often toasted sesame oil. A teaspoon in place of half the olive oil is lovely. Gebna beida is salty, so a little goes a long way.
ingredients: cooked from dried, or a tin with no salt added, drained

name: Baked green ta'meya with cucumber and rocket salad, tahini and olives
inspiredBy: Egyptian ta'meya, the fava falafel of Cairo and Alexandria, baked instead of deep-fried
about: Green fava patties packed with parsley and dill, crusted in sesame and baked until crisp, with a peppery cucumber and rocket salad, a lemony tahini sauce and a few black olives. The fava and herbs bring **protein, folate, iron and vitamin K**. This makes two portions, so Sunday's breakfast is done.
steps: The night before, cover the fava with plenty of cold water and soak for at least 12 hours. Drain well. Do not cook them first, they should be raw and just soft.
Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Line a tray with parchment and brush it with a little of the oil.
Pulse the fava, parsley, dill, onion, garlic, half the sesame, cumin and salt in a food processor until it looks like coarse green crumbs. It should hold together when you squeeze a handful.
Shape into small flattened patties, about 6 per portion. Press the edges into the rest of the sesame seeds, set them on the tray and brush with the remaining oil.
Bake for 12 minutes, flip, and bake another 10 to 12 minutes until deep golden and crisp outside, still green inside.
While they bake, stir the tahini with half the lemon juice, a pinch of salt and enough water to make a pourable sauce. Toss the cucumber and rocket with the rest of the lemon.

Serve the ta'meya with the salad, the tahini sauce, the olives and warm bread, with a little dukkah for dipping. Keep the second portion for tomorrow's breakfast and re-crisp it in a hot oven or toaster oven for 8 minutes.
tip: Peeled split dried fava from a Middle Eastern grocer gives the greenest, lightest ta'meya. Whole dried fava from the supermarket works too, but peel the skins after soaking. Canned fava will not work, the raw soaked fava is what holds the patties together.
ingredients: dried, soaked overnight, peeled and split if you can find them
half in the mix, half to coat
black olives, rinsed, on the side

name: Sardine, tomato and rocket in baladi bread with tahini and lemon
inspiredBy: the Egyptian tinned sardine sandwich, a lunch-hour classic in Cairo
about: Mashed tinned sardines with onion, cumin and lemon, stuffed into a toasted pocket with tomato, rocket and a tahini and lemon sauce with a pinch of dried mint. The soft sardine bones bring **calcium and omega-3**, and it comes together in ten minutes.
steps: Mash the sardines roughly with a fork with half the lemon juice, the cumin, the chili and the onion.
Stir the tahini with the olive oil, the dried mint, the salt and a spoonful of water to make a thick sauce.
Split the pita and toast it for a minute in a dry pan or toaster.
Spread the sauce inside, then fill with the sardines, tomato, rocket and parsley. Squeeze the rest of the lemon over the top and eat it right away.
tip: Pack the pita, filling and salad separately if you are taking it to work and assemble at lunch so the bread stays crisp.
ingredients: tinned in water or brine, drained

name: Tinned mackerel in garlicky tomato with salata baladi and baladi bread
inspiredBy: a cheap, quick Cairo supper of tinned fish warmed in tomato and scooped up with bread, with the everyday salad on the side
about: Tinned mackerel warmed through in a garlicky, cumin-scented tomato sauce, scooped up with warm bread, with a crunchy salata baladi of cucumber, tomato, onion and parsley on the side. The mackerel brings **omega-3, B12 and vitamin D**, and the cooked tomato brings lycopene and vitamin C.
steps: Warm the olive oil with the crushed garlic in a small pan over low heat for 1 minute, without letting it brown.
Add the passata, cumin, chili, half the lemon juice and half the salt. Simmer for about 4 minutes, until it thickens.
Flake in the mackerel and warm it through for 2 minutes. Do not stir too hard, you want big flakes.
Toss the cucumber, fresh tomato, onion and parsley with the rest of the lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Warm the bread in a dry pan. Scoop the mackerel and sauce up with the bread and eat the salad alongside.
tip: Tinned sardines work the same way. Mash the soft bones in with a fork for extra calcium.
ingredients: passata or tomato sauce, no salt added

name: Molokhia with chicken and brown rice, with garlic and coriander taqliya
inspiredBy: Cairo molokhia, the green jute leaf soup, served over brown rice rather than white
about: Silky, deep green jute leaves in chicken broth, finished with a sizzle of garlic and coriander, spooned over brown rice and tender chicken, with sharp onion in vinegar on the side. The jute brings **vitamins A and K, folate and calcium**, and the chicken and rice make it a full meal.
steps: Start the brown rice first, in a pot with twice its volume of water. It needs about 40 minutes.

Put the chicken, the quartered onion, bay leaf, cardamom, pepper and half the salt in another pot with enough water to cover, about 700 ml for two portions. Simmer, covered, until the chicken is just tender, 18 to 20 minutes.
Lift out the chicken and keep it warm. Strain the broth back into the pot and bring it to a gentle simmer.
Stir in the molokhia, still frozen is fine, and the rest of the salt. Bring back to a gentle simmer, not a hard boil, and cook for 5 minutes. It should be glossy and fall off the spoon in ribbons.

Make the taqliya. Warm the olive oil in a small pan and fry the garlic with the ground coriander for 1 to 2 minutes, until the garlic is just golden. Do not let it brown. Tip it sizzling into the pot and stir once.
Toss a few thin slices of raw onion with the vinegar and a pinch of salt.

Serve the rice with the molokhia ladled over and the chicken on top, with the onions and lemon wedges on the side. Squeeze the lemon over at the table, since it dulls the green if it cooks. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch, with the rice in a separate container.
tip: Ghee is the traditional fat for the taqliya, and a teaspoon of it is delicious here if you have some. Molokhia freezes well, so a double batch makes a quick dinner later.
ingredients: frozen minced molokhia, or fresh, or dried
quartered, plus a little thinly sliced

name: Koshari with lentils, chickpeas and a little pasta
inspiredBy: Cairo koshari, reimagined with brown rice and lentils doing most of the work, and a small handful of whole-wheat pasta
about: The Cairo street classic: lentils, rice, pasta and chickpeas under a spiced tomato sauce, crisp onions and a sharp garlic and vinegar splash. Here it leans on lentils and chickpeas for **fibre, iron and slow carbs**, with less rice and pasta than the street version.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Toss the sliced onions with most of the oil and a pinch of salt and spread them in a single layer over two trays. Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, flipping once, until deep golden. They crisp up as they cool.
Simmer the brown rice alone in plenty of water for 10 minutes. Add the lentils and half the cumin and simmer for about 22 minutes more, until both are tender. Drain and season with a pinch of salt.
Cook the pasta in boiling salted water until just al dente, then drain.

For the sauce, warm the rest of the oil and half the garlic (finely chopped) over low heat for 1 minute. Stir in the tomato paste, the passata, the rest of the cumin, the coriander, cinnamon and salt. Simmer for 12 minutes until thick, then stir in the chickpeas to warm through.
Crush the remaining garlic and stir it into the vinegar with a splash of water. This is the daqqa.

Pile the lentils and rice into bowls, top with the pasta, the saucy chickpeas and the crispy onions. Spoon over the garlic vinegar, scatter with parsley and add a spoonful of shatta at the table. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch, with the onions in a separate container.
tip: Cook the lentil and rice base on Sunday and keep it in the fridge, then koshari is a 25-minute job. Re-crisp the leftover onions in a dry pan before you eat them.
ingredients: passata or tomato sauce, no salt added

name: Alexandrian grilled sardines with cumin and lemon, tahini sauce and baladi salad
inspiredBy: the grilled sardines of Alexandria's fish markets, rubbed with cumin and garlic
about: Fresh sardines rubbed with garlic, cumin and lemon, grilled until the skin blisters, with a lemony tahini sauce, a crunchy tomato, cucumber, carrot and parsley salad and warm bread. The sardines bring **omega-3, vitamin D, B12 and calcium**.
steps: Mash half the garlic with the salt, then stir in the cumin, paprika, chili, half the oil and half the lemon juice. Rub this all over the sardines, inside and out, and leave them for 15 minutes.
Heat the broiler (or a grill pan or barbecue) as hot as it goes. Cook the sardines for 3 to 4 minutes on each side, until the skin is blistered and the flesh flakes off the bone.
Make the tahini sauce. Mash the rest of the garlic, stir in the tahini and half the remaining lemon juice, and thin with water until it pours like cream.
Toss the tomato, cucumber, carrot, onion and parsley with the rest of the lemon juice and oil and a pinch of salt.
Serve the sardines hot with the salad, the tahini sauce and warm bread.
tip: Ask the fishmonger to gut and scale the sardines. If you cannot find fresh ones, mackerel fillets work the same way.

name: Bamia bil lahma, okra and beef in garlicky tomato, with brown rice
inspiredBy: Egyptian bamia, the okra and meat stew every Cairo family makes, with a garlic and coriander taqliya
about: Tender okra and small chunks of beef simmered in a thick tomato sauce, finished with a sizzle of garlic and coriander, over brown rice. Okra is **rich in fibre, folate and vitamin K**, and the garlic and tomato make it taste like Friday lunch.
steps: Brown the beef in half the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat, about 5 minutes. Add the onion and cook until golden, about 5 minutes.
Add the tomato paste, the passata, the bay leaf, the pepper, half the salt and 250 ml of water. Cover and simmer gently for about 55 minutes, until the beef is nearly tender.
Start the rice in a separate pot with twice its volume of water about 35 minutes before the end, and cook until fluffy.
Add the okra whole, trimming only the stems, and simmer for another 15 minutes, until tender. Do not stir too much, it will turn slimy. Shake the pot instead.
Fry the sliced garlic with the ground coriander in the rest of the oil until golden, about 1 minute, then tip the sizzling taqliya into the pot with the lemon juice.
