name: Mast-o-khiar, cucumber yogurt with dill and mint
inspiredBy: Persian mast-o-khiar, with a little lavash to scoop
about: Cool, thick yogurt with grated cucumber, fresh dill and mint, with torn lavash for scooping. It is the Iranian answer to a hot afternoon. The yogurt brings **calcium and protein**, and the cucumber keeps it light.
steps: Squeeze the grated cucumber lightly. Stir it into the yogurt with the dill, mint and salt, and loosen with a spoonful of cold water.
Serve in a bowl with the torn lavash for scooping.

name: Yogurt with pekmez and dried figs
inspiredBy: Pekmezli yoğurt, the Turkish afternoon bowl, with Aegean dried figs
about: Thick yogurt with a drizzle of dark grape molasses (pekmez) and chopped dried figs, a simple Turkish afternoon treat. The yogurt brings **calcium and protein**, and the figs add fibre.
steps: Spoon the yogurt into a bowl, drizzle with the pekmez and scatter over the chopped figs.

name: Roasted chickpeas, leblebi style
inspiredBy: Turkish leblebi, the roasted chickpeas sold at every market, made from tinned chickpeas in the oven
about: Crunchy oven-roasted chickpeas with cumin, Aleppo pepper and lemon, in the style of the leblebi sold at Turkish nut shops. They bring **plant protein, fibre and folate**.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 C. Pat the chickpeas very dry and toss with the oil, cumin, Aleppo pepper and salt on a tray.
Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, shaking the tray halfway, until golden and crunchy. Squeeze over the lemon while they are hot. They crisp further as they cool.
tip: Roast a fresh tray on the day. They lose their crunch after 3 days in a jar.

name: Dried figs with hazelnuts
about: Aegean dried figs with hazelnuts from the Black Sea coast, a sweet and nutty Turkish tea-time plate. The hazelnuts bring **vitamin E and magnesium**, and the figs bring fibre and a little calcium.
steps: Serve the figs and hazelnuts together on a small plate. Toast the hazelnuts in a dry pan for 3 minutes first if you like.

name: Orange slices with cinnamon
about: Sliced orange with a pinch of cinnamon, a Persian-style fruit plate. The orange brings **vitamin C and folate**.
steps: Peel the orange and slice it into rounds. Sprinkle with the cinnamon and chill for 10 minutes if you have time.

name: Tahini and pekmez on warm lavash
inspiredBy: Turkish tahin-pekmez, tahini swirled with grape molasses
about: A thick swirl of tahini and pekmez (grape molasses) on warm whole-wheat lavash, a very Turkish sweet snack. The tahini brings **calcium, copper and healthy fats**.
steps: Warm the lavash. Spread the tahini over it, then drizzle with the pekmez and swirl them together with a knife. Fold and eat.

name: Dried figs with walnuts and hazelnuts
inspiredBy: Turkish incir ve ceviz, the classic pairing, with a few Black Sea hazelnuts
about: Chewy dried figs with walnut halves and a few hazelnuts, a classic Turkish and Persian pairing. The figs bring **fibre and a little calcium**, the walnuts bring plant omega-3, and the hazelnuts bring vitamin E.
steps: Tuck a walnut half into each fig, or serve them side by side on a plate with the hazelnuts.

name: Pomegranate seeds with walnuts
inspiredBy: the pomegranate and walnut pairing of fesenjan, as a snack
about: Ruby pomegranate seeds with a handful of walnut halves, the sweet-tart and rich pairing that Persian cooks love. The walnuts bring **plant omega-3 and magnesium**, and the pomegranate brings vitamin C.
steps: Tip the pomegranate seeds into a bowl and eat them with the walnut halves, a spoonful of each at a time.

name: Orange with toasted hazelnuts
about: Mediterranean oranges with toasted Black Sea hazelnuts, a simple Turkish pairing. The hazelnuts bring **vitamin E and magnesium** and the orange brings vitamin C.
steps: Toast the hazelnuts in a dry pan for 3 minutes, until fragrant. Peel and slice the orange and eat it with the nuts.

name: Overnight oats with Greek yogurt, figs and almonds
inspiredBy: Greek yogurt with dried fruit and nuts, turned into make-ahead oats
about:
Rolled oats soaked overnight in thick Greek yogurt with chopped dried figs and a pinch of cinnamon, finished with chopped almonds. It is **ready when you wake up**, creamy and a little sweet, with a crunch on top.

The oats bring fibre, the yogurt brings calcium and protein, and the almonds bring vitamin E.
steps: The night before, stir the oats, yogurt, chopped figs and cinnamon together in a jar with a splash of milk or water. It should look a little too loose, since the oats will drink it up.
Cover and chill overnight, and eat within 2 days. The figs soften and sweeten the oats as they sit.
In the morning, give it a good stir. It should be thick and spoonable. A splash more milk or water loosens it if it has gone stiff.
Scatter the chopped almonds on top just before eating, so they stay crunchy.
tip: Mix two jars at a time to save effort; they keep up to 2 days in the fridge. A chopped orange works in place of the figs in season.

name: Baked eggs in tomato and pepper with toast
inspiredBy: Spanish huevos a la flamenca, without the chorizo and with a smoky paprika base
about: Eggs set in a bubbling sofrito of sweet pepper, onion, tomato and a handful of spinach, with smoky paprika standing in for chorizo. Eat it with toast to mop up the sauce. It is a **proper hot breakfast**, rich in eggs for choline, with vitamin C from the pepper and tomato.
steps: Rinse the pepper, then dice it. Warm the olive oil in a small non-stick frying pan over medium heat and cook the onion and pepper with a pinch of the salt until soft, about 6 minutes.
Add the garlic and smoked paprika and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant. The paprika blooms in the hot oil, so don't let it scorch.
Tip in the tomatoes, breaking them up with a spoon. Simmer until the sauce is thick and jammy, about 8 minutes, then stir in the spinach until it wilts.
Make two wells in the sauce and crack in the eggs. Cover and cook over low heat until the whites are set and the yolks are firm, about 7 minutes.
Scatter with parsley and serve with the toast. Wash your hands after cracking the eggs.
tip: A pinch of chili flakes with the paprika gives it a gentle kick.

name: Ricotta toast with apple, walnuts and honey
inspiredBy: Italian ricotta and honey on toast
about: Thick whole-wheat toast spread with creamy ricotta, topped with sliced crisp apple, toasted walnuts and a drizzle of honey. It takes **five minutes** and feels like a treat. Ricotta brings calcium and protein, and the walnuts bring omega-3 and vitamin E.
steps: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan over medium heat until they smell nutty, about 3 minutes, then chop them roughly.
Toast the bread until golden and crisp. Spread the ricotta over it right away.
Lay the apple slices on top, scatter with the walnuts and a pinch of cinnamon, and finish with a drizzle of honey.
tip: A ripe pear or a few fresh figs in season work just as well as the apple. Little ones under 4 do better with the walnuts finely chopped. Do not give honey to a child under 1 year.

name: Shrimp saganaki with feta, tomato and crusty bread
inspiredBy: Greek shrimp saganaki, with a little less feta and a cucumber salad on the side
about: Plump shrimp in a quick tomato sauce with garlic, oregano and a hint of chili, topped with a crumble of salty feta and served with whole-wheat bread and a crisp cucumber salad. It's a **quick lunch**, on the table in about 25 minutes. The shrimp bring selenium and iodine and the tomato brings vitamin C.
steps: If the shrimp are frozen, thaw them overnight in the fridge and cook them within 2 days. Rinse them and pat them dry. Keep them in the fridge until the sauce is ready, and wash your hands and the board after handling them.
Warm the olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Cook the onion until soft and glossy, about 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic, oregano and chili for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, breaking them up with a spoon, with the salt. Simmer until the sauce is thick, about 8 minutes.
Nestle the shrimp into the sauce and cook, turning once, until they are pink, curled and opaque all the way through (74 °C), about 3 to 4 minutes. Don't overcook them, or they turn rubbery.
Take the pan off the heat, crumble the feta over the top and let it soften for a minute. Finish with the parsley and lemon juice.
Serve with the bread for mopping and the cucumber dressed with lemon, a pinch of oregano and a few drops of the olive oil.
tip: If you like it hot, add more chili at the table, not in the pot.

name: Pasta e fagioli with kale and a little anchovy
inspiredBy: Italian pasta e fagioli, with whole-wheat pasta and a melted anchovy in the soffritto
about: A thick, comforting Italian bean and pasta soup built on a soffritto of onion and carrot, with white beans, tomato, rosemary and kale. A single anchovy melts into the oil and adds **deep savoury flavour** without tasting fishy. Beans and kale bring iron and folate, and the tomato and lemon help you absorb it.
steps: Warm the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and carrot with a pinch of the salt until soft and sweet, about 8 minutes. Add the garlic, anchovy, rosemary and bay and stir until the anchovy melts away, about 2 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes, until it darkens a shade. Add the tomatoes and break them up with a spoon.
Add the white beans and enough water to cover everything by about 3 cm. Bring to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes. Mash a few spoonfuls of the beans against the side of the pot to thicken the broth.

Add the pasta (short tubes like ditalini, or broken spaghetti) and the kale with a little more water if it looks dry. Cook until the pasta is tender, about 10 minutes, stirring often so it doesn't catch. It should be thick enough to hold a spoon upright.
Season with the remaining salt, a squeeze of lemon and plenty of black pepper. Serve in wide bowls with a thread of olive oil.

Pasta is a cooked grain, so cool the second portion in a shallow container and refrigerate within 1 hour. Tomorrow, loosen it with a splash of water, since the pasta drinks the broth, and reheat it to 74 °C.
tip: Leave the anchovy out and add an extra squeeze of lemon for a fish-free version. New to this many beans? Build up over the week and drink plenty of water.

name: Grilled sardines with lemon potatoes and wild greens
inspiredBy: Greek and Portuguese grilled sardines, with horta-style greens
about: Whole sardines grilled until the skin blisters, served with tender lemony potatoes and a pile of olive-oil-dressed spinach, the way you'd eat horta by the sea. Sardines are one of the **best fish sources of omega-3 and vitamin D**, and their soft bones add calcium.
steps: Put the potatoes in a pot of cold water with a pinch of the salt. Bring to a boil and cook until just tender, about 15 minutes. Drain and let the steam escape.
Rinse the sardines and pat them dry. Brush with a little of the olive oil and sprinkle with salt and pepper. Wash your hands, the board and the plate after handling raw fish.
Heat a grill or a cast-iron pan until very hot. Grill the sardines about 3 to 4 minutes a side, until the skin is blistered and the flesh is opaque and flakes at the spine (70 °C inside).
While the fish cooks, boil the spinach in salted water for 2 minutes, until tender. Drain well and dress with olive oil, the garlic and a squeeze of lemon.
Toss the warm potatoes with the oregano, remaining olive oil and most of the lemon juice. Slice the tomato and onion into a quick salad with the parsley.
Serve the sardines with a squeeze of lemon over the top, alongside the potatoes, greens and salad.
tip: No grill? Roast the sardines on a very hot tray, 8 minutes, until opaque. Ask the fishmonger to clean them, or use a pan and open the window.
ingredients: cleaned and gutted, heads on or off

name: Smoky lentils with Swiss chard and a spoon of yogurt
inspiredBy: Spanish lentejas, with smoked paprika and no chorizo
about: A cosy Spanish-style pot of green lentils with potato, carrot and plenty of smoked paprika, which gives the chorizo flavour without any meat. Swiss chard goes in at the end and a spoon of cool yogurt balances the smoke. **Lentils bring a big share of your iron**, and the vinegar at the end helps you absorb it.
steps: Rinse the lentils and pick through for any stones. Warm the olive oil in a heavy pot over medium heat and soften the onion and carrot for 8 minutes.
Add the garlic and tomato paste and stir for a minute. Add the smoked paprika and stir for 20 seconds, until it smells deeply smoky. It scorches fast, so keep the heat gentle.

Add the lentils, potato, bay leaf and enough water to cover by about 3 cm. Bring to a boil, then simmer gently until the lentils and potato are tender, about 30 minutes. Top up with water if it gets dry.
Stir in the salt and the chard and cook until tender, 4 minutes. Remove the bay leaf and finish with the vinegar. Taste, since it should be smoky, savoury and a little sharp.
Serve in bowls with a spoon of yogurt and the parsley. Cool the second portion within 1 hour in a shallow container, refrigerate within 2 hours and reheat to 74 °C tomorrow.
tip: Stir a spoon of the pot into a little yogurt for the kids. It freezes well in single portions.

name: Portuguese chickpea and tuna salad with tomato and parsley
inspiredBy: Portuguese salada de grao com atum
about: A bright Portuguese-style salad of chickpeas, flaked light tuna, ripe tomato, onion and lots of parsley, dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar. It's a **quick lunch** that tastes better after the chickpeas soak up the dressing. Chickpeas bring iron and zinc, the tuna brings protein, niacin and B12, and the tomato helps you absorb the iron.
steps: Rinse the tomato, cucumber and parsley, then dice the tomato and cucumber. Soak the sliced onion in cold water for 5 minutes to soften its bite, then drain well.
Whisk the olive oil, vinegar, garlic and salt in a bowl. Add the chickpeas, tuna, onion, tomato, cucumber and olives and toss.
Let the salad sit for 5 minutes so the chickpeas drink in the dressing. Stir in most of the parsley.
Scatter with the remaining parsley and serve.
tip: Make the salad without the tomato the night before and add it fresh. Keep it cold and eat it within 1 day. Keep the rest of the opened tin in a lidded container in the fridge and use it within 2 days, flaked into a sandwich or on toast.

name: Baked cod with chickpeas, spinach and tomato
inspiredBy: Portuguese and Spanish baked cod and chickpeas, with fresh cod in place of salt cod
about: Fresh cod baked on a bed of chickpeas, spinach and tomato, scented with smoked paprika, lemon and olives. The chickpeas soak up the juices and the cod stays tender on top. It's a **one-dish dinner that makes tomorrow's lunch**. Cod is a lean protein with iodine, and the chickpeas add fibre, iron and zinc.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Warm half of the olive oil in an ovenproof skillet or wide pan and cook the onion with a pinch of salt until softened, about 6 minutes. Add the garlic and smoked paprika and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, breaking them up, then the chickpeas and olives. Simmer for 5 minutes, then stir in the spinach until it wilts.

Rinse the cod, pat it dry, and season with salt and a little pepper. Wash your hands and the board after handling raw fish. Nestle the fillets into the chickpeas and drizzle with the remaining olive oil.
Bake until the cod is opaque and flakes easily, about 12 to 15 minutes, with an internal temperature of 70 °C (158 °F).
Finish with the lemon juice and parsley and serve in wide bowls. Cool the second portion quickly, refrigerate within 2 hours, and reheat it tomorrow until steaming hot (74 °C).
tip: Hake or pollock work the same way. If your fillets are thin, add them for the last 8 minutes. Frozen fillets are fine: thaw them in the fridge overnight and cook them within 2 days.

name: Greek briam with white beans and feta
inspiredBy: Greek briam, the roasted summer vegetable tray, with white beans for a full dinner
about: A tray of potatoes, zucchini, eggplant, red pepper and tomatoes roasted slowly in olive oil and oregano, with white beans tucked in and a little feta on top. It's **meat-free comfort food** that tastes even better the next day. Beans bring iron and fibre, and the feta brings calcium.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Wash all the vegetables before cutting them.
Toss the potatoes, zucchini, eggplant, red pepper, onion and garlic in a roasting dish with the olive oil, oregano and salt. Pour the tomatoes and their juice over the top and add a splash of water.
Roast, stirring once, for 35 minutes, until the potatoes are nearly tender and the juices have thickened.
Tuck the white beans into the vegetables, crumble the feta over the top and roast for 10 minutes more, until the edges are caramelized and the potatoes are completely soft.
Finish with the parsley and a squeeze of lemon, and add a spoonful of yogurt to each bowl. Refrigerate the second portion within 2 hours and reheat it to 74 °C tomorrow.
tip: It roasts hands-off while you do other things, and takes closer to 45 minutes if you slice the potatoes thin. Cut the vegetables in similar sizes so everything is tender together. Add a handful of olives if you like.

name: Portuguese fish and shellfish stew with potatoes and peppers
inspiredBy: Portuguese caldeirada, lightened with more vegetables and less oil
about: A big, fragrant Portuguese-style fish stew of cod, salmon, mussels, clams and shrimp on a base of potatoes, red pepper, tomato and onion, with paprika, saffron and a bay leaf. It's the **weekend project**: layer the pot, simmer gently and eat it from deep bowls. The seafood brings iron, zinc and B12, and the salmon brings omega-3.
steps: Soak the clams in a bowl of cold water with about 2 tbsp of salt per litre for 20 minutes, then lift them out and rinse. Scrub the mussels and clams under cold running water, and pull the beards off the mussels just before cooking. Throw out any with cracked shells, and tap any that are open: if they stay open, throw them out.

Until you cook them, keep the shellfish in the fridge in an open bowl under a damp cloth, never in a sealed bag or fresh water, and cook them the day you buy them. If the shrimp are frozen, thaw them overnight in the fridge. Wash your hands, boards and knives well after handling raw fish and shellfish.

Warm the olive oil in a wide, heavy pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrot and red pepper with a pinch of salt for 8 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic, paprika and saffron and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, bay leaf and the potatoes with enough water to nearly cover them. Bring to a simmer and cook until the potatoes are just tender, about 15 minutes.
Lay the cod and salmon on top of the potatoes and season with the remaining salt. Cover and simmer gently for 5 minutes.

Scatter the mussels and clams over the fish, cover tightly and cook until the shells open, about 5 minutes. Add the shrimp for the last 3 minutes, until pink and opaque. The fish should flake easily and be 70 °C (158 °F) inside, and the shellfish steaming hot right through (74 °C).
Throw away any mussels or clams that haven't opened after cooking. Stir in the parsley and lemon juice and serve in deep bowls.
For tomorrow's lunch, take the shellfish out of their shells, cool the second portion in a shallow container, refrigerate within 2 hours, eat it tomorrow and reheat it once to 74 °C.
tip: A splash of fish stock in place of some of the water gives a deeper broth. Hake, pollock or haddock work in place of the cod. Mussels and clams are weighed without their shells, so shop for roughly four times that weight of mussels and five times that of clams in the shell.
ingredients: weighed without shells, so buy about four times as much in the shell
weighed without shells, so buy about five times as much in the shell

name: Zucchini, potato and ricotta frittata with a tomato salad
inspiredBy: Italian frittata, with potato and zucchini and a little ricotta for softness
about: A thick, golden Italian frittata of sweet onion, tender potato, zucchini and ricotta, set gently and finished under the grill, served with a juicy tomato and oregano salad. It's an **easy, satisfying meat-free dinner** that's also lovely cold. Eggs bring protein and choline, and the potato brings potassium.
steps: Wash the zucchini and potato. Warm half of the olive oil in an ovenproof non-stick pan over medium-low heat. Cook the potato and onion with a pinch of salt, covered, stirring now and then, until the potato is tender, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the grated zucchini for the last 3 minutes. Tip the vegetables into a bowl and let them cool for a few minutes.
Beat the eggs with the ricotta, parsley and the remaining salt, then fold in the vegetables.
Heat the remaining oil in the pan, pour in the mixture and cook over low heat until the edges are set, about 8 minutes. Meanwhile, heat the grill.
Finish under the grill until the top is set and lightly golden and the centre is firm, about 3 minutes (the centre reads 74 °C, or 165 °F).
Toss the tomatoes with the oregano, vinegar and a pinch of salt. Serve the frittata in wedges with the tomato salad.
tip: It's lovely cold too: make it in a bigger pan, refrigerate the extra wedges within 2 hours and pack one in tomorrow's sandwich. Wash your hands after cracking eggs.

name: Greek yogurt with dried figs and walnuts
about: Thick Greek yogurt with chopped dried figs and toasted walnuts. It's a **calcium and omega-3 snack** that feels like dessert.
steps: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan until fragrant, about 3 minutes, then chop them.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl and top with the figs and walnuts.

name: Orange and almonds
about: A juicy orange with a small handful of almonds. The orange brings **vitamin C** and the almonds bring vitamin E and magnesium.
steps: Wash the orange before peeling it. Peel and segment it, and eat with the almonds.
tip: Chop the almonds for children under 4.

name: Smoky roasted chickpeas
inspiredBy: Spanish-style smoked paprika chickpeas
about: Crunchy oven-roasted chickpeas tossed with smoked paprika. A **crisp, high-fibre snack** that also brings plant protein and iron.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Dry the chickpeas very well with a towel, since dry means crisp.
Toss with the olive oil, smoked paprika and salt on a tray. Roast for 25 minutes, shaking the tray halfway, until golden and crunchy.
Toss with a squeeze of lemon. Eat the same day, since they soften as they sit.

name: Sardines on toast with tomato and lemon
inspiredBy: Portuguese tosta de sardinhas
about: Canned sardines mashed onto crisp whole-wheat toast with sliced tomato and lemon. A **small fish snack** with omega-3, vitamin D and calcium from the soft bones.
steps: Toast the bread until crisp.
Lay the tomato slices on the toast and top with the sardines, mashing them gently with a fork.
Finish with lemon juice, parsley and a grind of pepper.
tip: Keep the rest of the opened tin in a lidded container in the fridge and use it within 2 days.

name: Tuscan white bean dip with carrot and cucumber
inspiredBy: Tuscan cannellini bean dip with rosemary
about: A quick garlicky white bean dip with rosemary and lemon, served with crunchy carrot and cucumber sticks. A **fibre-rich snack** with plant protein and iron.
steps: Wash the carrot and cucumber, then cut into sticks.
Blitz the beans, olive oil, garlic, lemon, rosemary and salt with a splash of water until smooth.
Serve the dip with the sticks. Keep leftover dip in the fridge up to 3 days.

name: Apple with walnuts and cinnamon
about: Crisp apple slices with toasted walnuts and a pinch of cinnamon. A **crunchy snack** with fibre and a little omega-3.
steps: Wash and slice the apple.
Toast the walnuts in a dry pan until fragrant, about 3 minutes.
Serve together with a dusting of cinnamon.
tip: Chop the walnuts for children under 4.

name: Medjool dates stuffed with almonds
about: Soft dates stuffed with whole almonds. A **sweet, quick snack** with potassium and vitamin E.
steps: Slit the dates open, pull out the pits, and tuck an almond into each.
tip: Chop the almonds for young children.

name: Tzatziki with cucumber and toasted bread
inspiredBy: Greek tzatziki
about: Cool garlicky Greek yogurt with grated cucumber, lemon and a little olive oil, scooped up with cucumber slices and a piece of toasted whole-wheat bread. A **cooling, high-protein snack**.
steps: Wash the cucumber. Grate half of it and squeeze it dry in a clean towel, then slice the rest.
Stir the grated cucumber into the yogurt with the garlic, lemon, olive oil and salt.
Serve with the cucumber slices and toast. It keeps in the fridge up to 3 days.
ingredients: half grated and squeezed dry, half sliced

name: Boiled egg with tomato and oregano
about: A boiled egg with sliced tomato, olive oil and a dusting of oregano. A **simple protein snack** with choline and vitamin C.
steps: Put the egg in a small pot of cold water, bring to a boil, then simmer 10 minutes, until the yolk is firm. Cool under cold water and peel.
Slice the egg and tomato, drizzle with olive oil and dust with oregano, black pepper and salt.

name: Tuscan white bean toast with tomato
inspiredBy: Tuscan fettunta with beans
about: Crisp whole-wheat toast piled with mashed white beans, sliced tomato, a little garlic and olive oil. A **filling snack** with plant protein, fibre and iron.
steps: Toast the bread and rub it with the cut side of the garlic.
Mash the beans with a fork, olive oil and salt, and spread over the toast.
Top with the tomato and parsley.

name: Chickpea, tomato and cucumber cup
inspiredBy: Greek and Portuguese chickpea salads
about: A small cup of chickpeas with chopped tomato, cucumber, oregano, lemon and olive oil. A **fresh, filling snack** with plant protein, fibre and iron.
steps: Wash the tomato and cucumber, then dice them.
Toss everything together in a small bowl.
Let it sit for 5 minutes so the chickpeas soak up the dressing.

name: Black sesame and almond oat porridge with banana
inspiredBy: Chinese black sesame porridge (zhi ma hu), made with oats for a quicker morning
about: Creamy oats cooked in milk with a little fresh ginger, then topped with toasted black sesame, almonds, walnuts and banana. It is a warm, nutty bowl that comes together in ten minutes. The **almonds and milk bring vitamin E and calcium**, alongside the oats' fibre.
steps: Toast the black sesame seeds and almonds in a dry pan over medium heat for about 2 minutes, until they smell nutty. Tip them onto a board and crush the sesame lightly.
Put the oats, milk, ginger, cinnamon and salt in a small pot. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, stirring often so the milk doesn't catch.
Cook for about 5 minutes, until the porridge is thick and creamy, then stir in the mashed banana.
Spoon into a bowl and top with the sliced banana, the toasted sesame and almonds, and the walnuts.
tip: Toast and crush a jar of black sesame and almonds ahead of time and spoon it on straight from the jar.
ingredients: ripe, half mashed and half sliced

name: Korean steamed egg custard with rice, shiitake and spinach
inspiredBy: Korean gyeran-jjim, eaten the way it is at a family table, next to a bowl of rice
about: A silky, savoury egg custard steamed gently until completely set, served with warm rice and a quick sauté of shiitake and spinach. It is soft, easy food for a slow morning. The **eggs bring choline and B12**, and the spinach brings folate.
steps: Wash the spinach and mushrooms. Beat the eggs well with the salt and about the same volume of water, until no streaks of white remain. Pour the mixture into a heatproof bowl through a small sieve, then stir in half of the scallion.
Set a rack or a small upturned bowl in a pot with about 2 cm of water and bring it to a gentle simmer. Cover the custard bowl loosely with foil and set it on the rack. Put the lid on the pot.

Steam on low heat for 12 to 15 minutes, until the custard is completely set: the centre should not wobble, a knife should come out clean, and the centre should reach 74 °C (165 °F). Never serve it soft or runny.

While it steams, reheat the rice (thawed in the fridge overnight if it was frozen) with a splash of water and a lid, in the microwave or a pot, until it is steaming hot (74 °C). Warm the canola oil in a pan and cook the shiitake for 3 minutes, until browned. Add the spinach and cook for 1 minute, until just wilted.

Toss the spinach with the perilla oil. Drizzle the custard with the soy sauce and sesame oil, and scatter over the rest of the scallion and the sesame seeds. Serve with the rice, shiitake and spinach.
tip: On Sunday, cook enough brown basmati for the three custard mornings (a generous ½ cup raw, or about ¾ cup at Big), chill it within 1 hour, keep Monday's portion in the fridge and freeze the other two. Thaw one in the fridge the night before, use within 2 days and reheat until steaming. A pouch of cooked brown rice works too. Keep perilla oil in the fridge, use it within 2 months and never heat it. No perilla? Use sesame oil.
ingredients: brown basmati from your Sunday batch

name: Ginger congee with tofu, spinach and egg
inspiredBy: Chinese rice porridge (zhou), the everyday food of zuo yuezi, with no wine or herbs
about: Rice simmered until it falls apart into a soft, steaming porridge with fresh ginger, tofu, shiitake and spinach, with egg stirred in and crushed walnuts on top. Congee is the classic first food of a Chinese confinement month, and this pot makes two bowls so the next morning is ready. The **egg and tofu make it a protein breakfast**.
steps: Wash the spinach and mushrooms. Put the rinsed rice and the ginger in a large pot with about 8 parts water to 1 part rice by volume. Bring to a boil, then turn the heat down to a steady, gentle simmer.

Simmer partly covered for about 50 minutes, stirring every so often and scraping the bottom, until the grains have burst and the congee is thick and creamy. Add a splash of hot water if it gets too thick.
Stir in the shiitake and tofu and cook for 5 minutes, until the mushrooms are soft and the tofu is hot through.
Stir in the soy sauce, salt and spinach. Pour in the beaten egg in a thin stream, stirring gently, and cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until the egg has set into soft ribbons with no runny bits.
Ladle into bowls and finish with the sesame oil, scallion, white pepper and walnuts.
Divide into shallow containers, chill within 2 hours, eat tomorrow or freeze, and reheat once until steaming hot (74 °C).
tip: Use a cooker's keep-warm setting only if it holds above 60 °C. Otherwise cook the base the evening before, chill it in shallow containers and bring it to a boil in the morning before adding the tofu, mushrooms, spinach and egg.

name: Sesame-ginger greens with seared tofu and rice
inspiredBy: Cantonese ginger greens and Korean sigeumchi namul, on a rice bowl
about: Tender water spinach dressed in a warm ginger, garlic and toasted sesame dressing, with golden tofu and steamed brown rice. It is a quick, bright plate. The **greens and tofu bring calcium** and folate, and the sesame adds its nutty flavour.
steps: Cook the rice in plenty of simmering water for about 30 minutes, until tender, then drain well and keep it covered.

Wash the water spinach well, since grit hides between the stems. Cut the tofu into thick slabs. Warm the canola oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat and sear the tofu for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until golden and crisp at the edges.
Boil the water spinach in a pot of water for 1 minute, until the stems are just tender and the leaves are bright green. Drain well.

Warm the sesame oil in a small pan over low heat. Add the ginger and garlic and stir for about 30 seconds, until fragrant but not browned. Take off the heat and stir in the soy sauce, lemon juice and salt.
Toss the greens with the warm dressing. Serve on top of the rice with the tofu, scattered with the scallion and sesame seeds.
tip: Swap in bok choy, spinach or broccoli. Whatever is crisp and green works with this dressing.
ingredients: cut into short lengths and washed

name: Ginger and sesame chicken soup
inspiredBy: Chinese sesame oil chicken (ma you ji), made as a soup with no rice wine
about: A warm, fragrant pot of chicken simmered with plenty of fresh ginger, toasted sesame oil, shiitake, carrot and bok choy. The traditional confinement chicken uses rice wine; this one leaves it out, and you won't miss it, because the **ginger and sesame oil carry the aroma**. It makes two bowls and freezes well.
steps: Wash all the vegetables. Warm the sesame oil and canola oil in a soup pot over medium-low heat. Add the ginger and stir for 2 to 3 minutes, until it is fragrant and just starting to turn golden at the edges. Don't let it scorch.
Add the chicken and stir for about 3 minutes, until the outside is pale. Add the shiitake, carrot and soy sauce, then enough water to cover everything by about 3 cm.

Bring to a boil, skim off any foam, then turn down to a gentle simmer. Cover and cook for 25 minutes, until the carrot is tender and the chicken reaches 74 °C (165 °F) in the thickest piece, with no pink inside.
Cook the rice in plenty of simmering water for about 30 minutes, until tender, then drain well and keep it covered.
Add the bok choy and the salt to the soup and simmer for 3 minutes, until the greens are soft. Ladle the soup over or beside the rice and finish with the white pepper and scallion.
Divide into shallow containers, chill within 2 hours, eat tomorrow or freeze, and reheat once until steaming hot (74 °C). The soup freezes on its own for up to 3 months.
tip: Add more ginger if you love it. For the freezer, freeze the soup without the rice and cook fresh rice on the day.

name: Salmon and ginger congee with water spinach
inspiredBy: Cantonese fish congee (yu pin zhou), with salmon for its omega-3 fat
about: Soft, savoury congee topped with tender flakes of salmon, fresh ginger, water spinach (ong choy) and scallion. Fish congee is a home favourite in southern China, and the salmon gives it **omega-3 fat (DHA) and vitamin D**. It makes two bowls, so tomorrow's lunch is ready.
steps: Wash the water spinach well. Put the rinsed rice and the sliced ginger in a large pot with about 8 parts water to 1 part rice by volume. Bring to a boil, then turn down to a steady simmer.
Simmer partly covered for about 50 minutes, stirring now and then, until the grains have burst and the congee is thick and creamy. Add a splash of hot water if it tightens.
Toss the salmon with the soy sauce, the ginger matchsticks and the white pepper.
Stir the salt and water spinach into the congee and cook for 2 minutes. Lay the salmon on top, cover and simmer for 4 to 5 minutes, until the fish is opaque, flakes easily and reaches 70 °C (158 °F).
Break the salmon into large flakes, ladle into bowls and finish with the sesame oil, scallion and sesame seeds.
Divide into shallow containers, chill within 2 hours, eat tomorrow or freeze, and reheat once until steaming hot (74 °C).
tip: Chill the base within 2 hours and bring it to a boil before adding the fish. No water spinach? Use bok choy or spinach.
ingredients: skin removed, cut into thick slices
half thinly sliced and half cut into fine matchsticks

name: Miyeok-guk, Korean seaweed soup with beef and tofu
inspiredBy: Korean miyeok-guk, the seaweed soup eaten after a birth and on birthdays
about: A clear, savoury soup of tender beef, tofu, garlic and a small amount of wakame, deepened with toasted sesame oil, with sesame spinach and rice alongside. Seaweed is very rich in iodine, so it's kept to a few grams: enough for flavour and some **iodine**, without overdoing it. It makes two bowls and freezes well.
steps: Wash the spinach well. Soak the wakame in cold water for 10 minutes, until soft and swollen to many times its size. Drain, squeeze out the water and cut it into short lengths.
Cook the rice in plenty of simmering water for about 30 minutes, until tender, then drain well and keep it covered.
Warm the sesame oil and canola oil in a soup pot over medium heat. Add the beef and half of the garlic and stir for 3 to 4 minutes, until the beef is browned and no pink remains.

Add the wakame and stir for 1 minute. Add the soy sauce and about 1½ cups of water for each serving. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 25 to 30 minutes, until the beef is very tender and the broth tastes rich.

Add the tofu for the last 5 minutes. Season with the salt and stir in the rest of the garlic. Meanwhile, blanch the spinach in boiling water for 1 minute, drain, squeeze and toss with the perilla oil and sesame seeds, the way Korean namul is dressed.

Serve the soup with the rice and the spinach. Divide into shallow containers, chill within 2 hours, eat tomorrow or freeze, and reheat once until steaming hot (74 °C). Freeze the soup without the rice and spinach.
tip: Weigh 3 g dry per serving, not a pinch. It swells a lot in the pot. Use wakame (miyeok) only: kelp, kombu and dashima carry far more iodine. Lovely as it is, keep this soup to a couple of bowls a week. Keep perilla oil in the fridge, use it within 2 months and never heat it. No perilla? Use sesame oil.
ingredients: very thinly sliced against the grain
weighed dry, soaked and drained, soaking water discarded

name: Red lentil, spinach and carrot dal with ginger-cumin tadka and brown rice
inspiredBy: North Indian masoor dal with a ghee tadka
about: Soft red lentils simmered with turmeric, tomato, carrot and spinach, then finished with a sizzling ghee, cumin, garlic and ginger tadka and a squeeze of lemon. Served with brown basmati rice and a spoonful of yogurt, it is comforting food that freezes beautifully. The **lentils bring iron, folate and protein**, and the lemon helps with iron.
steps: Cook the rice in plenty of simmering water for about 30 minutes, until tender, then drain well and keep it covered.

Wash the vegetables. Put the lentils, carrot, onion, tomato, turmeric and about 3 times the lentils' volume of water in a pot. Bring to a boil, skim off any foam, then simmer for about 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until the lentils have collapsed into a soft, thick dal.
Stir in the spinach and the salt and cook for 3 minutes, until the spinach has wilted. Add a splash of hot water if the dal is too thick.

For the tadka, heat the ghee and canola oil in a small pan until shimmering. Add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle for about 20 seconds, then add the garlic and ginger and cook for 30 seconds, until golden but not brown.
Pour the sizzling tadka over the dal and stir in the garam masala and lemon juice.
Serve with the rice and the yogurt. Divide into shallow containers, chill within 2 hours, eat tomorrow or freeze, and reheat once until steaming hot (74 °C). The dal freezes for up to 3 months.
tip: Make the tadka fresh each time. It is what makes leftover dal taste new.
ingredients: rinsed until the water runs clear

name: Braised mackerel with daikon and bok choy
inspiredBy: Korean godeungeo-jorim, braised mackerel with radish, with less salt and heat
about: Meaty mackerel simmered with sweet daikon, onion, ginger and a little soy and chili until the sauce clings, with bok choy laid over to steam at the end. The sauce is sweetened with grated apple instead of sugar. **Mackerel is a low-mercury oily fish**, a good source of omega-3 fat (DHA), B12 and vitamin D.
steps: Cook the rice in plenty of simmering water for about 30 minutes, until tender, then drain well and keep it covered.

Wash the vegetables. Spread the daikon, carrot and onion in a wide pot. Add the ginger, garlic, soy sauce, gochugaru, grated apple and about half a cup of water. Bring to a boil, cover and simmer for 12 minutes, until the daikon and carrot are nearly tender.
Nestle the mackerel pieces on top and spoon the sauce over them. Cover and simmer for 10 to 12 minutes, until the fish is opaque, flakes easily with a fork and reaches 70 °C (158 °F).
Lay the bok choy over the fish for the last 3 minutes, just until it turns bright green and tender.

Drizzle with the sesame oil and scatter with the scallion. Serve with the rice. If there are any leftovers, refrigerate them within 2 hours, eat them the next day and reheat until steaming hot (74 °C).
tip: Buy Atlantic mackerel or saba, never king mackerel (high mercury). Thaw frozen fillets in the fridge and cook them within 2 days.
ingredients: peeled, thick half-moons; simmers in the sauce, no pre-boil

name: Chicken and egg rice bowl (oyakodon)
inspiredBy: Japanese oyakodon, with the egg cooked through and no mirin or sake
about: Tender chicken, onion and edamame simmered in a gently sweet, savoury broth, then topped with egg cooked until set and spooned over rice. Grated apple does the work of mirin here. It is a quick lunch with plenty of **protein and choline**.
steps: Cook the rice in plenty of simmering water for about 30 minutes, until tender, then drain well and keep it covered.

Wash the vegetables. Warm the canola oil in a small, wide pan over medium heat and cook the onion, shiitake and ginger for 3 minutes, until soft. Add about half a cup of water, the soy sauce and the grated apple and bring to a simmer.
Add the chicken, spreading it out in a single layer, and simmer for 5 to 6 minutes, until it reaches 74 °C (165 °F) in the thickest piece, with no pink. Stir in the edamame for the last 2 minutes.
Pour the beaten egg over in a thin stream, cover and cook gently for 2 to 3 minutes, until the egg is fully set with no runny parts.
Slide everything over the rice and finish with the scallion and sesame seeds.
tip: Eat it straight away. It's the one dish here that doesn't want to wait.

name: Pork rib and daikon soup
inspiredBy: Cantonese lou fo tong, the slow-simmered soup of the home kitchen
about: A clear, comforting Cantonese-style soup of pork rib meat, sweet daikon, carrot, sweet corn and ginger, simmered slowly until the pork is tender, with bok choy stirred in at the end and rice on the side. It is hands-off cooking, and the soup freezes well. The **pork adds thiamin and zinc**, and the daikon keeps the broth clean and sweet.
steps: Wash the vegetables. Put the pork in a pot of cold water, bring to a boil and cook for 3 minutes, until foam rises. Drain, rinse the foam off the blanched pork and out of the pot, then wipe down the sink.
Return the pork to the clean pot with the daikon, carrot, sweet corn and ginger. Add enough water to cover by about 4 cm and bring to a boil, then skim.

Turn the heat down to a very gentle simmer, partly cover and cook for about 1½ hours, until the pork is very tender, reaches 71 °C (160 °F) and the daikon is soft. In a pressure cooker, cook for about 25 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook the rice in plenty of simmering water for about 30 minutes, until tender, then drain well and keep it covered.
Skim off any fat from the surface. Add the bok choy and the salt and simmer for 3 minutes. Finish with the sesame oil, white pepper and scallion, and serve with the rice.
Divide into shallow containers, chill within 2 hours, eat tomorrow or freeze, and reheat once until steaming hot (74 °C). The soup freezes on its own for up to 3 months.
tip: Found lotus root? Use 100 g instead of the daikon.
ingredients: peeled, thick coins; goes in raw, no pre-boil
kernels cut off the cob, or frozen

name: Beef and potato simmer (nikujaga)
inspiredBy: Japanese nikujaga, home-style simmered beef and potatoes
about: Thin slices of beef with potato, carrot, onion and spinach, simmered in a light soy broth sweetened with grated apple. Home-style nikujaga is made with mirin and sake; this one uses neither. The **beef brings iron, zinc and B12**, and the potato makes it a full, filling bowl.
steps: Cook the rice in plenty of simmering water for about 30 minutes, until tender, then drain well and keep it covered.
Wash the vegetables. Warm the canola oil in a wide pot over medium heat. Add the beef and ginger and stir for 2 to 3 minutes, until the beef has lost its pink colour.
Add the potato, carrot and onion and stir for 1 minute. Add the grated apple, the soy sauce and about 1 cup of water, then bring to a boil.
Turn the heat down, cover and simmer for 20 to 25 minutes, until the potato is tender and the beef is cooked through. Stir in the spinach for the last 2 minutes, until wilted.
Uncover and cook for 2 minutes more to thicken the broth a little. Serve in a bowl beside the rice, with any broth spooned over.
tip: Cooked a double batch? Chill it in a shallow container within 2 hours. It's even better the next day, and keeps up to 3 days or a month in the freezer. Reheat until steaming hot (74 °C).

name: Sesame, date and almond bites
about: Soft medjool dates mashed with almonds and rolled oats into sticky little balls rolled in black sesame. They are one-hand food you can eat while holding a baby. The **dates, almonds and sesame** add iron, calcium and vitamin E.
steps: Mash the dates with a fork in a bowl until you have a sticky paste.
Stir in the almonds, oats and cinnamon.
Roll into small balls with damp hands, then roll them in the black sesame and chill for 15 minutes. They keep in the fridge for 4 days.
tip: Make a batch of a dozen on Sunday and keep them in a jar in the fridge.

name: Warm tofu with ginger honey syrup
inspiredBy: Chinese tofu pudding (dou hua), made with a quick ginger syrup
about: Warm cubes of tofu spooned over with a little ginger-honey syrup, black sesame and walnuts, a gentle snack in the spirit of Chinese tofu pudding (dou hua). It takes five minutes. The **tofu brings protein and calcium**.
steps: Simmer the honey, ginger and a splash of water in a small pot for 2 minutes to make a syrup.
Warm the tofu in a bowl in the microwave for about 1 minute, or in a pot of hot water, until steaming hot all the way through.
Spoon the syrup over the tofu and scatter with the sesame and walnuts. Let it cool a minute before eating.

name: Soy-simmered egg with edamame
inspiredBy: Chinese soy-braised egg (lu dan), simplified
about: A hard-cooked egg steeped in a light soy and ginger broth until it takes on a savoury, golden-brown edge, with a handful of warm shelled edamame. It's a protein-rich bite you can eat standing up. The **egg brings choline and B12**, and the edamame add folate.
steps: Bring a small pot of water to a boil. Lower the egg in gently (add a second for later in the week if you like) and boil for 10 to 12 minutes, until the yolk is completely set.
Cool in cold water, then peel.
Simmer the soy sauce, ginger and a few tablespoons of water for 2 minutes. Add the egg and turn it for 2 minutes, until glazed.

Warm the edamame in the microwave for about 1 minute and serve beside the egg. If you boiled a second egg, keep it in its shell in the fridge, glaze it on the day you eat it, and eat it within 3 days.

name: Warm almond and black sesame milk
inspiredBy: Chinese almond and sesame drinks (xing ren zhi ma lu)
about: Milk warmed and blended with ground almonds, black sesame and a little honey, a cozy mug for when baby is down. It is inspired by the almond and sesame drinks of Chinese breakfast stalls, with **calcium from the milk** and vitamin E from the almonds.
steps: Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan for about 1 minute, until they smell nutty, then grind them finely with the almonds.
Warm the milk in a pot until steaming, but not boiling, then let it cool a few minutes until warm, not hot.
Whisk in the almond and sesame mixture and the honey, and sip from a lidded mug with baby set down.

name: Warm walnut and black sesame milk
inspiredBy: Chinese walnut and sesame sweet soups (he tao zhi ma hu)
about: Milk warmed and blended with ground walnuts, black sesame and a little honey, a cozy mug for when baby is down. It is inspired by the walnut and sesame sweet soups of southern China. The **walnuts bring plant omega-3 fat (ALA)**, and the milk brings calcium.
steps: Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan for about 1 minute, until they smell nutty, then grind them finely with the walnuts.
Warm the milk in a pot until steaming, but not boiling, then let it cool a few minutes until warm, not hot.
Whisk in the walnut and sesame mixture and the honey, and sip from a lidded mug with baby set down.

name: Mandarin with walnuts and almonds
about: A juicy mandarin with a handful of walnuts and almonds, a no-cook snack you can eat in the car or on the sofa. The **walnuts bring plant omega-3 fat (ALA)**, the almonds bring vitamin E, and the mandarin brings vitamin C.
steps: Wash the mandarin, then peel it and eat it with the nuts.

name: Warm edamame with sesame
about: Shelled edamame warmed through and tossed with a pinch of salt and toasted sesame. Easy finger food that takes two minutes. The **soy beans bring protein, folate and iron**.
steps: Warm the edamame in the microwave or in a pot of hot water until steaming hot, about 2 minutes, then let them cool for a minute.
Toss with the salt and sesame seeds.

name: Mango almond lassi
inspiredBy: North Indian mango lassi, made lighter with Greek yogurt
about: Greek yogurt and milk blended with ripe mango, ground almonds and a pinch of cardamom into a cool, creamy drink. It's one-hand food in a glass, with **protein and calcium** from the yogurt and milk and vitamin E from the almonds.
steps: Blend the yogurt, milk, mango, almonds and cardamom until smooth.
Pour into a glass and drink right away, or chill for up to a day.
ingredients: ripe, fresh or thawed from frozen

name: Masala chickpeas and almonds
inspiredBy: Inspired by Indian chana snacks and masala nuts
about: Chickpeas roasted until crisp with cumin, garam masala and lemon, tossed with a few almonds, a crunchy, savoury snack for the handbag or the nursing chair. The **chickpeas bring protein, fibre and folate**.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Toss the chickpeas with the oil, cumin, garam masala and salt on a tray.
Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, shaking the tray halfway, until golden and crisp.
Toss with the almonds and the lemon juice and let cool for 5 minutes. They are best the day they're made.

name: Apple with walnuts and almonds
about: A crisp apple with a small handful of walnuts and almonds, sweet, juicy and crunchy. It is a no-cook snack that eats well with one hand. The **walnuts bring plant omega-3 fat (ALA)**, the almonds bring vitamin E, and the apple brings fibre.
steps: Wash the apple, slice it if you like and eat it with the nuts.

name: Banana walnut smoothie with black sesame
about: Milk blended with banana, walnuts and a spoonful of black sesame into a thick, creamy drink. It is easy to sip one-handed, with **calcium from the milk**, plant omega-3 fat from the walnuts and potassium from the banana.
steps: Blend everything until smooth and creamy. Black sesame can leave a few specks, which is fine.
Drink right away or chill for a few hours.

name: Yogurt with mandarin and toasted almonds
about: Thick Greek yogurt topped with juicy mandarin segments and crunchy toasted almonds. It's cool, tangy and takes a minute. The **mandarin brings vitamin C**, the almonds bring vitamin E, and the yogurt brings protein and calcium.
steps: Toast the almonds in a dry pan for about 2 minutes, until golden and fragrant. Wash the mandarin before peeling and splitting it into segments.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl and top with the mandarin and almonds.

name: Berry and walnut overnight oats
about: Rolled oats soaked overnight in milk and yogurt, thick and cold, with blueberries, walnuts and a few pumpkin seeds for crunch. It is **ready the second you wake up**, and you can eat it one-handed from the jar. The yogurt and milk bring calcium and iodine, and the pumpkin seeds bring zinc.
steps: Stir the oats, milk, yogurt, cinnamon and maple syrup together in a jar until there are no dry pockets.
Fold in half the blueberries, put the lid on and chill overnight, or at least 4 hours.
In the morning, loosen with a splash of milk if it has set firm, then top with the rest of the blueberries, the walnuts and the pumpkin seeds.
tip: Mix the jar the night before and eat it within 2 days. Mix a second jar for another morning only if you will eat it within that time.

name: Carrot cake baked oat squares with yogurt
about: Soft, spiced oat squares with grated carrot, dates and walnuts, baked in one dish and cut cold from the fridge. They taste like carrot cake and eat like a bar, so one hand is plenty. The carrot and egg bring **vitamin A and choline**.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and grease a small baking dish with a little canola oil.
Stir the oats, cinnamon and baking powder together, then stir in the beaten eggs, milk and maple syrup until evenly wet.
Fold in the grated carrot, dates and walnuts and spread the mix in the dish.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until the middle is set, the top is golden and a knife comes out clean, so the egg is fully cooked (74°C or 165°F in the centre).
Cool, cover and chill in an airtight container. Cut into squares and serve cold or warmed, with the yogurt and blueberries on the side or spooned on top.
tip: Bake Sunday. Keep day 2's square in the fridge in an airtight container and freeze day 5's wrapped alone. Thaw it in the fridge overnight and eat within 2 days.
ingredients: fresh, or thawed if frozen, to serve

name: Egg muffin breakfast wrap with avocado and clementine
about: A baked spinach and cheddar egg muffin tucked into a warm tortilla with sliced avocado, with a clementine on the side. The muffins are baked ahead, so breakfast is a minute of assembly and one hand. The eggs bring **choline and protein**, cooked all the way through.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and grease a muffin tin well.
Whisk the eggs, milk, salt and pepper, then stir in the spinach and cheddar.
Pour into the tin, about three-quarters full. Bake for 18 to 22 minutes, until puffed and completely set in the middle, with no wet egg, and the centre reaches 74°C (165°F).
Cool, then chill within 2 hours. Keep tomorrow's muffins in the fridge and freeze the rest in single portions.
To serve, reheat the muffins to 74°C (165°F), steaming hot all the way through. Warm the tortilla, lay on the avocado and the muffins, fold and eat. Peel the clementine on the side.
tip: Bake 3 breakfasts on Sunday: day 1 from the fridge, days 4 and 7 from the freezer. Thaw overnight in the fridge, then reheat to 74°C (165°F).

name: Beef and bean chili with tortilla for scooping
inspiredBy: classic North American chili con carne
about: A thick, smoky chili with lean beef, kidney and black beans, carrot and tomato, topped with creamy avocado. Cook it on **Sunday and freeze portions**, so a hot, hearty meal is only a reheat away. The beef brings iron, zinc and B12, and the beans add fibre.
steps: Warm the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and carrot for 6 to 8 minutes, until soft and starting to colour. Add the garlic and cook 1 minute.
Add the ground beef and break it up with a spoon. Cook for 6 to 8 minutes, until no pink remains, it is browned all over and it reaches 71°C (160°F).
Stir in the chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika and oregano and cook for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, beans, salt and a splash of water. Simmer gently for 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick and the flavours have come together.

Divide into shallow containers so it cools fast, and chill within 2 hours. Keep one portion in the fridge for up to 3 days and freeze the rest in single portions. Reheat to 74°C (165°F), steaming hot all the way through.
Serve in a bowl with the diced avocado on top and the warm tortilla for scooping.
tip: This pot covers day 1's lunch and day 7's dinner. Double it if you want spare freezer meals. Thaw overnight in the fridge, use within 2 days and never refreeze.

name: Red lentil, carrot and tomato soup with cheddar quesadilla wedges
inspiredBy: Middle Eastern shorbat adas
about: A silky orange soup of red lentils, carrots and tomato with warm cumin and a squeeze of lemon, served with crisp cheddar quesadilla wedges for dunking. It is a **freezer-friendly one-pot soup** that blends up thick and creamy. The carrots and spinach bring vitamin A and the lentils bring folate.
steps: Warm the oil in a pot over medium heat and cook the onion and carrot for 8 minutes, until the onion is soft.
Add the garlic, cumin and tomatoes and stir for 1 minute.
Rinse the lentils and add them with the broth and a cup of water. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 20 minutes, until the lentils and carrots are completely soft.
Blend with an immersion blender until smooth, or leave it a little chunky. Stir in the washed spinach until it wilts, then the salt and lemon juice.
For the quesadilla, scatter the cheddar over half the tortilla, fold it over and toast in a dry pan for 2 minutes a side, until golden and the cheese has melted. Cut into wedges.
Divide into shallow containers so it cools fast, and chill within 2 hours. Keep one portion in the fridge for up to 3 days and freeze the rest in single portions. Reheat to 74°C (165°F).
tip: Make it Sunday and freeze in single portions with a little room at the top. Thaw overnight in the fridge, use within 2 days and never refreeze. Make the quesadilla fresh each time.

name: Sheet-pan salmon with sweet potato, broccoli and lemon-dill yogurt
about: A whole dinner on one tray: salmon roasted over wedges of sweet potato and broccoli, spooned with a cool lemon-dill yogurt. Salmon is the DHA dinner of the week, and the sweet potato brings **plenty of vitamin A**. There is one pan to wash and nothing to stir.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Toss the sweet potato wedges with half the oil, half the salt and the pepper on a large tray and roast for 15 minutes.
Add the broccoli to the tray with the rest of the oil and toss. Make room for the salmon in the middle.

Season the salmon with a pinch of salt and lay it on the tray. Roast for 10 to 12 minutes more, until the salmon flakes easily with a fork, reaches 70°C (158°F) inside, and the sweet potato is tender.
Stir the yogurt, lemon juice, garlic and dill together in a small bowl.
Serve the salmon and vegetables with the yogurt sauce spooned over.
tip: Salmon is best eaten fresh, so cook only what you will eat tonight.

name: Chicken tinga bowl with sweet potato, black beans and avocado
inspiredBy: Pueblan tinga de pollo
about: Tender shredded chicken in a smoky tomato and chipotle sauce with sweet potato cooked right in, over a little brown rice and black beans with avocado and a squeeze of lemon. It makes **two portions**, and tomorrow's lunch is better for the night in the fridge. The chicken brings protein and choline, the sweet potato brings vitamin A.
steps: Cook the rice in plenty of water or per the packet until tender, then drain. Warm the black beans through in a small pot.
Warm the oil in a wide pan over medium heat and cook the onion for 6 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic, cumin and oregano and cook 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, chipotle, salt and a splash of water and bring to a simmer. Add the chicken and cover. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the sweet potato cubes, cover again and simmer 15 minutes more, until the sweet potato is tender and the chicken reaches 74°C (165°F) on a thermometer, with no pink and the juices running clear.
Shred the chicken with two forks right in the sauce and simmer a few minutes, until thick.
Spoon the chicken and sweet potato over the rice and beans. Top with avocado and a squeeze of lemon.
Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch, spreading any leftover rice thin in a shallow container so it cools fast. Chill within 2 hours and reheat once to 74°C (165°F), steaming hot.
tip: Use less chipotle for a milder sauce. The tinga freezes well without the avocado. Thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days and never refreeze.

name: Turkey meatball and spinach soup with little pasta
inspiredBy: Italian wedding soup
about: A brothy soup of tender baked turkey meatballs, carrot, chickpeas, spinach and a small handful of pasta, with lemon at the end. It is warm, mostly water and easy to eat with a spoon. It makes **tomorrow's lunch**, and freezes well without the pasta.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F) and line a tray with parchment. Beat the egg in a large bowl (if the list shows part of an egg, beat a whole one, use about half, and cover, chill and cook the rest within 2 days). Mix in the turkey, oats, half the garlic, half the oregano and a pinch of the salt with your hands. If the mix is too soft to roll, chill it for 10 minutes, then roll into small balls with wet hands and set them on the tray.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes, until browned and cooked through, with no pink inside and 74°C (165°F) on a thermometer.
Meanwhile, warm the oil in a pot and cook the onion and carrot for 6 minutes, until soft. Add the rest of the garlic and oregano, then the tomatoes, broth, chickpeas and a cup of water.
Bring to a simmer, add the broken spaghetti and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, until tender.
Add the meatballs and the washed spinach and simmer 3 minutes, until the spinach wilts and the meatballs are hot all the way through. Stir in the lemon juice and the rest of the salt.
Pack the second portion in a shallow container and chill within 2 hours. Reheat to 74°C (165°F), steaming hot, with a splash of water if the pasta has soaked up the broth.
tip: To freeze, leave out the pasta and add fresh spaghetti when you reheat it. Thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days and never refreeze.

name: Haddock and sweet corn chowder
inspiredBy: Maritime fish chowder
about: A creamy, comforting chowder of flaky haddock, potato, carrot and sweet corn in a milky broth with thyme and a handful of spinach stirred in. It is **a good iodine dinner**, since haddock and milk are two of the best food sources, and it reheats well for the next day's lunch. Soft, warm and easy to eat with a spoon.
steps: Warm the oil in a pot over medium heat and cook the onion and carrot for 6 minutes, until soft but not browned.
Add the potato, broth and thyme with a cup of water. Simmer for 10 minutes, until the potato is nearly tender.
Pour in the milk and add the corn. Warm gently, without letting it boil hard.

Cut the haddock into big pieces and lay them in. Cover and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, until the fish turns opaque, flakes easily and reaches 70°C (158°F). Stir in the washed spinach until it wilts and season with the salt and pepper.
Crush a few potato pieces against the side of the pot to thicken the chowder.
Pack the second portion in a shallow container and chill within 2 hours. Eat it within 3 days, stir and reheat to 74°C (165°F), steaming hot all the way through.
tip: Cod or pollock work too. Do not freeze the chowder, as the fish and milk turn soft and grainy.

name: Maple-ginger salmon rice bowl with broccoli and cucumber
inspiredBy: a Japanese-style salmon bowl, with Canadian maple
about: Salmon brushed with maple, ginger and a little soy sauce, roasted until just flaky, on brown rice with steamed broccoli, crunchy cucumber and carrot. It is sweet, salty and fresh, and everything comes together in one bowl. The salmon brings **DHA and B12**, and the broccoli brings vitamin C and folate.
steps: Cook the rice in plenty of water or per the packet until tender, then drain and keep warm.
Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Stir the maple syrup, soy sauce and ginger together and brush it over the salmon on a lined tray.
Roast for 10 to 12 minutes, until the salmon flakes easily, is opaque all the way through and reaches 70°C (158°F) inside.
Steam the broccoli for 4 to 5 minutes, until bright green and just tender. Toss the cucumber and carrot with the lemon juice and the oil.
Pile the rice in a bowl, add the broccoli and the cucumber-carrot salad and set the salmon on top.
tip: Cook the rice fresh, or cool extra rice fast in a shallow container, use it within 2 days and reheat once to 74°C (165°F).

name: Lemon-herb chicken tray bake with potatoes, carrots and chickpeas
inspiredBy: Greek-style lemon chicken and potatoes
about: Juicy chicken thighs roasted over potatoes, carrots, chickpeas and onion with lemon, garlic and thyme, finished with wilted spinach. It goes in the oven and you leave it alone, and the second portion is **tomorrow's lunch**, eaten cold from the fridge or reheated until steaming. A simple roast dinner without the Sunday effort.
steps: Heat the oven to 210°C (410°F). Toss the potato and carrot with half the oil, half the salt and the thyme on a large tray and roast for 15 minutes.
Toss the chicken with the rest of the oil, the garlic, smoked paprika, lemon juice and the remaining salt.

Add the chicken, chickpeas and onion to the tray and roast for 25 minutes more, until the chicken reaches 74°C (165°F) on a thermometer in the thickest piece, with no pink and the juices clear, and the potatoes are golden.
Pile the washed spinach onto the hot tray and toss for a minute, until it wilts, and serve.
Pack the second portion and chill it within 2 hours. Reheat to 74°C (165°F), or eat it cold from the fridge.
tip: Cut the potatoes and carrots the night before and keep them covered in cold water in the fridge. Making Big? Use two trays so it roasts instead of steaming.

name: Almond and date oat bars
about: Chewy bars of rolled oats, dates and chopped almonds pressed into a pan and cut into squares. They are sweet without being sugary and you can eat one in your other hand. They bring **slow-burning oats and vitamin E**.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C (325°F). Soak the dates in hot water for 5 minutes, then drain and mash them with a fork or blitz into a paste.
Mix the date paste with the maple syrup, a splash of water, cinnamon and salt, then stir in the oats and almonds until sticky.
Press firmly into a lined small pan. Bake for 15 to 18 minutes, until lightly golden around the edges.
Cool completely in the pan, cut into bars and keep in an airtight container in the fridge up to 4 days, or freeze wrapped one by one.
tip: Bars you will not eat within 4 days go in the freezer, wrapped one by one. Move one to the fridge the night before and eat it within 2 days of thawing.

name: Smashed chickpea and cucumber wrap
about: Mashed chickpeas with yogurt and lemon in a soft whole-wheat tortilla with crunchy cucumber and baby spinach. It is cold, crisp and juicy, and you can hold it in one hand. The chickpeas and spinach bring **iron, zinc and folate**.
steps: Mash the chickpeas roughly with a fork, then stir in the yogurt, lemon juice and pepper.
Lay the tortilla flat and spread the chickpea mix over it, leaving a border.
Pile the spinach and cucumber down the middle, fold in the sides and roll up tightly.
Wrap in parchment or foil so you can eat it one-handed. It keeps in the fridge until the next day.
tip: Roll it in foil and peel as you eat, so nothing falls out while the baby feeds.

name: Canned salmon and cucumber wrap
about: Flaked canned salmon, mashed with its soft bones, with creamy yogurt, lemon and dill in a whole-wheat wrap with cucumber and spinach. It tastes like a fresh salmon salad sandwich. Canned salmon with the bones carries **DHA and calcium**.
steps: Drain the salmon and flake it into a bowl, mashing in the soft bones.
Stir in the yogurt, lemon juice, dill and pepper.
Spread on the tortilla, add the cucumber and spinach, fold in the sides and roll tightly.
Eat right away or chill, wrapped, until later in the day.
tip: Open a can once and make two wraps. Keep the extra salmon mixture covered in the fridge up to 2 days.

name: Mango and banana yogurt smoothie
about: A cold, thick smoothie of frozen mango, banana, yogurt and milk that you can drink straight from a water bottle or a tall travel cup. It is sweet, easy and mostly water. Yogurt and milk bring **calcium and iodine**, and the mango adds vitamin A.
steps: Add the milk, yogurt, banana and frozen mango to a blender in that order.
Blend for about a minute, until completely smooth.
Drink right away, or pour into a lidded cup or water bottle (never a baby bottle), keep it cold and drink within a day.
tip: Peel and freeze ripe bananas in chunks so the smoothie is thick and cold without ice.

name: Cottage cheese with mango and almonds
about: Creamy cottage cheese with juicy thawed mango and a few chopped almonds, eaten with a spoon from a cup. It is sweet and savoury, cool and hydrating. It brings **protein, iodine and vitamin E** with plenty of water.
steps: Thaw the mango in the fridge overnight or for a few minutes in a bowl of cold water.
Spoon the cottage cheese into a cup or small bowl and top with the mango and almonds.
Eat it cold with a spoon, or keep it in the fridge until you want it.

name: Smoky roasted chickpeas
about: Crunchy chickpeas roasted until crisp with smoked paprika, cumin and lemon. They are a handful-at-a-time snack you can eat from a bowl on your lap. They bring **plant protein, fibre and zinc**.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Pat the chickpeas very dry with a clean towel.
Toss with the oil, smoked paprika, cumin and salt on a tray.
Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, shaking the tray halfway, until deep golden and crunchy.
Let them cool on the tray, as they crisp up as they cool. Squeeze the lemon over just the portion you are eating. Keep the rest plain in a jar for 3 days at most.
tip: Makes two portions. Keep the second plain and add its lemon when you eat it, so it stays crunchy.

name: Clementines with almonds and walnuts
about: Easy-peel clementines with a small handful of almonds and walnuts, juicy and crunchy together. There is no prep and no mess. Together they bring **vitamin C, vitamin E and plant omega-3**.
steps: Peel the clementines and split into segments.
Eat with a small handful of the almonds and walnuts.

name: Carrot sticks with garlicky yogurt dip
about: Crunchy carrot sticks with a cool, garlicky lemon yogurt dip, easy to dunk and eat with one hand. Mostly water, with a little protein. The carrots bring **vitamin A**.
steps: Stir the yogurt, grated garlic, lemon juice, salt and pepper together in a small bowl.
Wash and cut the carrots into sticks and dunk them in the dip.
Keep the dip covered in the fridge for up to 2 days.
tip: Makes enough dip for two snacks. Eat the second portion within 2 days.

name: Paprika yogurt eggs
about: Hard-boiled egg halves filled with a creamy yogurt, lemon and smoked paprika mix, easy to eat in two bites. Make them ahead and keep them in the fridge. The eggs bring **choline and protein**, boiled until the yolks are fully set.
steps: Lower the eggs into a pot of simmering water and boil for 10 minutes, so the yolks are fully set. Cool under cold running water, then peel.
Halve the eggs and scoop the yolks into a bowl. Mash with the yogurt, lemon juice, salt and pepper until creamy.
Spoon the filling back into the whites and dust with the smoked paprika.
Eat them the day you fill them.
tip: Hard-boil the eggs up to a week ahead and keep them in the shell, in the fridge. Fill them the day you eat them.

name: Banana and almond yogurt cup
about: Thick Greek yogurt with sliced banana, a few chopped almonds and a dusting of cinnamon, spooned from a cup. It is cool and creamy with a little crunch. The yogurt brings **calcium and iodine**, and the almonds bring vitamin E.
steps: Spoon the yogurt into a cup or small bowl.
Top with the banana slices, almonds and cinnamon.
Eat right away, so the banana stays fresh.

name: Blueberry yogurt bowl with walnuts and maple
about: Thick Greek yogurt with juicy blueberries, chopped walnuts and a drizzle of maple syrup, eaten with a spoon. It is cool, creamy and mostly water. It brings **calcium, protein and plant omega-3**, with very little iron, so it suits the bigger sizes.
steps: Spoon the yogurt into a bowl or cup.
Top with the blueberries and walnuts and drizzle with the maple syrup.
Eat it cold, right away.

name: Cheddar and clementine plate
about: A small plate of sharp cheddar cubes, clementine segments and a few almonds, all finger food. It is sweet, salty and juicy, and easy to eat one-handed. The cheddar brings **calcium and protein**, and the clementines bring vitamin C.
steps: Peel the clementines and split into segments.
Cut the cheddar into small cubes.
Arrange everything on a plate and eat with your fingers.

name: Creamy oatmeal with blueberries and walnuts
inspiredBy: Inspired by a Canadian bowl of porridge with maple and berries
about: Rolled oats and a spoonful of iron-fortified instant oats simmered in milk until creamy, topped with blueberries, chopped walnuts and a little maple syrup. It is **plain, warm and easy on a queasy morning**, and the oats bring fibre and iron.
steps: Stir both oats, the milk, a splash of water, cinnamon and a pinch of the iodized salt together in a small pot.
Bring to a gentle bubble over medium heat, then turn it down and cook, stirring often, until thick and creamy, about 5 minutes.
Rinse the blueberries under cold running water. Spoon the oatmeal into a bowl and top with the blueberries, chopped walnuts and a drizzle of maple syrup.
tip: Too much for a sleepy stomach? Leave off the walnuts and let the oatmeal cool a little. A ripe banana is a good swap for the blueberries.
ingredients: Plain instant oats with iron on the label, such as Quaker Instant Oatmeal, Original. Iron varies by brand, so do not stack other iron-fortified cereal on the same day

name: Firm scrambled eggs and spinach on toast with an orange
inspiredBy: Inspired by a Canadian diner breakfast of eggs and toast
about: Eggs scrambled slowly until fully set, with a handful of wilted spinach, on whole-wheat toast with orange wedges and a glass of milk. It is **simple and filling**, and eggs bring choline, milk brings calcium, and the orange's vitamin C helps your body take up plant iron.
steps: Wash the spinach well and shake it dry. Beat the eggs with the iodized salt and a little pepper, then wash your hands.
Warm the oil in a nonstick pan over medium-low heat. Add the spinach and stir for a minute, until it wilts.
Pour in the eggs and stir gently with a spatula. Keep cooking until no liquid egg is left and the eggs are set and fully firm, about 3 minutes.
Toast the bread. Pile the eggs on top and serve with the orange, washed and cut into wedges, and a glass of milk.
tip: Not up for much? Skip the spinach and just have eggs on toast.

name: Yogurt bowl with fruit and toasted oats
inspiredBy: Inspired by a Canadian yogurt parfait
about: Thick Greek yogurt topped with sliced banana, blueberries and a handful of rolled oats toasted with maple and cinnamon. It is **cool, light and easy to eat** when mornings are queasy, and the yogurt brings calcium and iodine.
steps: Warm a dry small pan over medium heat. Add the oats, sunflower seeds and cinnamon and toast, stirring, until they smell nutty, about 3 minutes.
Stir in the maple syrup for 30 seconds, then tip the oats onto a plate to cool and crisp up.
Rinse the blueberries and slice the banana.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl, add the fruit and scatter the crunchy oats on top.
tip: Toast a double batch of the oats and keep them in a jar for the next breakfast.

name: Mexican-style tomato eggs with black beans and corn tortillas
inspiredBy: Inspired by Mexican huevos a la mexicana, with the chili kept mild
about: Eggs scrambled firm with tomato, onion, wilted spinach and a little chili powder, served with warm corn tortillas, black beans and avocado. It is **a bright, savoury breakfast** with folate and iron from the beans, and the eggs bring choline.
steps: Heat the oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat. Rinse the tomato and dice it. Soften the onion with the chili powder for 2 minutes.
Add the tomato and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until it breaks down into a thick, saucy mixture. Stir in the spinach until it wilts.
Wash your hands after cracking the eggs. Add the beaten eggs and the iodized salt and stir gently. Keep cooking until no liquid egg is left and the eggs are set and fully firm, about 3 minutes.
Warm the beans in a small pot and warm the tortillas in a dry pan, about 30 seconds a side.
Serve the eggs with the tortillas, beans and the avocado, its skin rinsed before you slice it.
tip: Want it livelier? Add a pinch of red pepper flakes with the chili powder.

name: Potato, pepper and spinach hash with firm eggs
inspiredBy: Inspired by a Canadian diner breakfast hash
about: Crisp-edged potatoes with sweet red pepper, onion and wilted spinach, topped with eggs cooked until the yolks are set, with a glass of milk. A slow, **weekend diner-style breakfast** with choline from the eggs, calcium from the milk and vitamin C from the pepper.
steps: Wash the potato, pepper and spinach. Cover the diced potato with water in a small pot, bring to a boil and simmer for 5 minutes, until just tender. Drain well.
Heat the oil in a large nonstick pan over medium-high heat. Add the potato and cook, turning only now and then, until golden and crisp at the edges, about 8 minutes.
Add the onion and pepper with the smoked paprika, iodized salt and pepper and cook 4 minutes, until soft. Stir in the spinach until it wilts.

Make two wells in the hash and crack in the eggs, then wash your hands. Break each yolk gently with the tip of a spatula. Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 minutes, until the whites and yolks are fully set and no liquid egg is left. Serve with a glass of milk.
tip: A set yolk feels firm. If it jiggles, cook it longer.

name: Lemon-herb chicken traybake with potatoes, chickpeas and broccoli
inspiredBy: Inspired by a Canadian Sunday roast chicken, simplified onto one tray
about: Chicken thighs roasted on one tray with potatoes, chickpeas, carrots and broccoli, with lemon, garlic and oregano. It is **one tray and very little washing up**, and the chickpeas add folate and iron. It makes two portions, so tomorrow's lunch is done.
steps: Heat the oven to 425 F (220 C). Toss the potatoes, carrots and chickpeas on a large tray with half the oil, the oregano, iodized salt and pepper. Roast for 15 minutes.
Scrub the lemon under running water, then zest and juice it. Mix the garlic, lemon zest and juice with the remaining oil and rub it over the chicken.

Push the vegetables aside and nestle the chicken in the middle. Wash your hands, the board and the knife with hot soapy water after handling the raw chicken. Roast for 10 minutes, then scatter the washed broccoli florets around it.

Roast 15 to 20 minutes more, until the potatoes are golden and the chicken is cooked through, with no pink left and the juices running clear. A thermometer should read 165 F (74 C) in the thickest part.

Cool the second portion quickly, pack it into a shallow container and get it into the fridge within 2 hours. Tomorrow, reheat it until it reaches 165 F (74 C) and is steaming hot all the way through. Eat it within 2 days.
tip: Save a pinch of the zest in step 2 and scatter it over the finished tray for a fresh, bright finish. Reheat the leftover tray in a 350 F (180 C) oven or a pan, not the microwave, so the broccoli stays firm.
ingredients: from a lemon; zest it first

name: Maple-mustard salmon with brown rice and broccoli
inspiredBy: Inspired by Canadian maple-glazed salmon
about: Salmon fillets baked with a glaze of maple, Dijon and dill, served with nutty brown rice and garlicky lemon broccoli. It is **quick and fresh**, and salmon brings omega-3 DHA, one of the low-mercury fatty fish.
steps: Heat the oven to 400 F (200 C). Rinse the rice, then simmer it in plenty of water until tender, about 25 minutes, and drain.
