Stir the maple syrup, Dijon, dill and half the garlic together. Place the salmon on a lined tray and spoon the glaze on top with a clean spoon. Wash your hands after touching the raw fish.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes, until the salmon is opaque all the way through and flakes easily with a fork. A thermometer should read 158 F (70 C) at the thickest part.
Meanwhile, steam the broccoli for 5 minutes, until tender but still bright green. Toss with the oil, the rest of the garlic, lemon juice, iodized salt and pepper.
Serve the salmon on the rice with the broccoli.
tip: Cook extra rice if you like. Cool it quickly, chill it within 2 hours and use it within a day.

name: Tuscan-style red lentil and spinach soup
inspiredBy: Inspired by Italian zuppa di lenticchie, a simple lentil soup
about: Red lentils simmered with carrot, onion, tomato and a little whole-wheat pasta, then finished with spinach, lemon and a sprinkle of Parmesan. **Lentils bring folate and iron**, and the lemon helps your body use the iron. It makes two portions, so tomorrow's lunch is done.
steps: Warm the oil in a pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and carrot with the oregano until soft, about 7 minutes. Add the garlic for the last minute.
Stir in the lentils, tomatoes, broth and 2 cups (500 ml) of water. Bring to a boil, then simmer, partly covered, for 15 minutes.
Add the pasta and cook until the pasta and lentils are tender, about 8 more minutes. Stir in the spinach and the iodized salt and cook for 2 minutes, until the spinach is silky.
Finish with the lemon juice and a good grind of pepper. Ladle into bowls and sprinkle with the Parmesan.

Cool the second portion quickly, pack it into a shallow container and get it into the fridge within 2 hours. Tomorrow, reheat it until it reaches 165 F (74 C) and is steaming hot all the way through. Eat it within 2 days.
tip: The pasta soaks up broth overnight, so loosen the leftover with a splash of water. Freeze the second portion if you will not eat it tomorrow.

name: Beef and black bean chili with carrots and peppers
inspiredBy: Inspired by Tex-Mex chili con carne, with extra beans and vegetables
about: A hearty chili of lean ground beef and black beans with onion, carrot, red pepper and tomato, spiced with chili powder and cumin. **Beef and beans are a big iron source**, and the tomatoes and pepper bring vitamin C. It makes two portions, so tomorrow's lunch is done.
steps: Rinse the pepper and carrot before you dice them. Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the ground beef and cook, breaking it up, until it is browned all the way through with no pink left, about 6 minutes. Ground beef is done at 160 F (71 C). Wash your hands after handling the raw beef.
Add the onion, pepper and carrot and cook for 5 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic, chili powder, cumin and oregano and stir for a minute, until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, beans, iodized salt and 1 cup (250 ml) of water. Bring to a boil, then simmer, partly covered, for 25 minutes, until the chili is thick and the carrot is tender.
Serve with the toast alongside for scooping.

Cool the second portion quickly, pack it into a shallow container and get it into the fridge within 2 hours. Tomorrow, reheat it until it reaches 165 F (74 C) and is steaming hot all the way through. Eat it within 2 days.
tip: For a milder pot, use half the chili powder. Reheat leftover chili to 165 F (74 C), steaming hot all the way through.

name: Ginger-soy glazed trout with rice, edamame and soy-dressed spinach
inspiredBy: Inspired by Japanese teriyaki-style fish, with maple and lemon in place of mirin
about: Trout fillets glazed with ginger, garlic, reduced-sodium soy and maple, served with rice, edamame and a simple soy-dressed spinach. It is **a light Japanese-style dinner** with omega-3 DHA from the trout and folate from the edamame and spinach.
steps: Rinse the rice and simmer it in plenty of water until tender, about 25 minutes, then drain.

Stir the soy sauce, maple syrup, ginger, garlic and lemon juice together. Pour a third over the trout and leave a third for the spinach and a third for the pan. Wash your hands after touching the raw fish.

Heat the oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat and cook the trout about 4 minutes a side, until opaque all the way through and flaking easily. A thermometer should read 158 F (70 C) at the thickest part. Tip the last third of the glaze (from a clean spoon) into the pan for the final minute and let it bubble.

Boil the edamame for 5 minutes, until tender. Lift it out, then drop the spinach into the same water for 1 minute, until wilted. Drain the spinach, squeeze out the water and toss it with the middle third of the glaze.
Serve the trout on the rice with the edamame and spinach, drizzling any glaze left in the pan over the top.
tip: This works with salmon too. Tuck in a few slices of cucumber on the side for crunch.

name: Chicken and black bean enchilada bake
inspiredBy: Inspired by Mexican enchiladas, baked in layers like a casserole
about: Corn tortillas layered with small pieces of chicken, black beans and spinach under a homemade mild red sauce, baked with a little cheddar until bubbling. A **weekend project** that is made once and eaten twice, with iron and folate from the beans and spinach.
steps: Heat the oven to 375 F (190 C). Rinse the pepper before you dice it, and rinse the spinach. Warm the oil in a pan and cook the onion and pepper for 5 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic, chili powder and cumin for 1 minute.
Spoon half of this mixture into a bowl. Add the tomatoes and iodized salt to the pan and simmer 10 minutes, until thick. This is your sauce.

Cut the chicken into small pieces, then wash your hands, the board and the knife with hot soapy water. Cook the chicken in a second pan, stirring, until white all the way through with no pink left (165 F, 74 C), about 8 minutes. Stir in the reserved mixture, the beans, the washed spinach and the lemon juice and cook until the spinach wilts.

Spread a few spoonfuls of sauce over the bottom of a baking dish. Layer in half the tortillas, half the filling and a third of the remaining sauce. Repeat, then top with the last of the sauce and the cheddar.
Cover with foil and bake for 20 minutes, then uncover and bake 10 more minutes, until bubbling and 165 F (74 C) in the middle.

Cool the second portion quickly, pack it into a shallow container and get it into the fridge within 2 hours. Tomorrow, reheat it until it reaches 165 F (74 C) and is steaming hot all the way through. Eat it within 2 days.
tip: Warm the tortillas for 20 seconds in the microwave so they do not crack when you layer them.

name: Lemon salmon pasta with broccoli and spinach
inspiredBy: Inspired by Italian lemon pasta with greens
about: Whole-wheat pasta tossed with flaked baked salmon, broccoli, spinach, lemon and a little Parmesan. It is **comforting and quick**, and the salmon brings omega-3 DHA while the broccoli and spinach bring folate.
steps: Heat the oven to 400 F (200 C). Place the salmon on a lined tray, brush with a little of the oil and season with a pinch of the iodized salt. Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, until it is opaque all the way through and flakes easily. A thermometer should read 158 F (70 C) at the thickest part. Wash your hands after touching the raw fish.
Cook the pasta in a large pot of boiling water until tender, adding the broccoli for the last 3 minutes. Save a cup of the pasta water, then drain.

In the empty pot, warm the rest of the oil with the garlic for 30 seconds. Add the spinach and stir until wilted, then add the pasta, broccoli, the zest and juice of the scrubbed lemon and a splash of the pasta water.
Flake the salmon into big pieces and fold it in gently. Season with pepper and the rest of the salt.
Serve with the Parmesan on top.
tip: Want it creamier? Stir in an extra splash of the pasta water and a little more Parmesan.
ingredients: from a lemon; zest it first

name: Light tuna and chickpea sandwich with avocado
inspiredBy: Inspired by a classic Canadian tuna salad sandwich
about: Canned light tuna mashed with chickpeas, yogurt, onion, lemon and Dijon open-faced on whole-wheat toast with avocado, with a spinach salad on the side. A quick **no-cook lunch** with some omega-3 from the tuna and fibre from the chickpeas. Light tuna is the low-mercury kind.
steps: Mash the chickpeas with a fork in a bowl until mostly broken down.
Stir in the tuna, yogurt, onion, lemon juice and Dijon. Taste and add pepper.
Toast the bread. Rinse the avocado skin before you cut it. Spread the toast with the mashed avocado and pile on the tuna salad for an open-faced sandwich.
Toss the spinach with a squeeze of the lemon and serve it alongside with the carrot sticks as a quick salad. Keep the filling chilled until you eat it, and refrigerate any extra within 2 hours.
tip: Choose canned light tuna. Skip the albacore (white) tuna here: it is higher in mercury. If you pack it, keep it cold with an ice pack and eat it within 4 hours.

name: Greek-style chickpea and cucumber bowl with lemon yogurt
inspiredBy: Inspired by a Greek-style chickpea salad with tzatziki
about: Chickpeas tossed with cucumber, tomato and onion, spooned over a garlicky lemon yogurt with toasted whole-wheat bread alongside. A **fresh, crunchy lunch** that is rich in fibre, folate and iron.
steps: Stir the yogurt with half the lemon juice, the garlic and a pinch of the iodized salt.
Rinse the tomato. Toss the chickpeas, cucumber, tomato and onion with the oil, the rest of the lemon juice, the oregano and a little more salt.
Spread the yogurt in a bowl, spoon the chickpea salad on top. Toast the bread and serve it alongside.
tip: Toast the bread and rub it with half a cut garlic clove for extra flavour.

name: Egg salad sandwich with cucumber
inspiredBy: Inspired by the Canadian egg salad sandwich
about: Hard-boiled eggs, cooked until the yolks are fully set, mashed with yogurt and Dijon, on whole-wheat bread with cucumber. A **cool, comforting lunch** that is rich in choline.
steps: Place the eggs in a small pot, cover with cold water and bring to a boil. Cover, turn off the heat and let them sit for 12 minutes, until the whites and yolks are completely firm.
Cool the eggs in cold water, then peel and chop them.
Stir the eggs with the yogurt, Dijon, onion, lemon juice, iodized salt and pepper.
Pile onto the bread with the cucumber and close the sandwich. Eat it soon and keep any extra chilled.
tip: Make it fresh and don't keep it more than 2 days. Boil an extra egg or two for snacks and keep them in the fridge in their shells.

name: Banana with peanut butter
about: A ripe banana sliced and spread with smooth peanut butter. A **soft, filling snack** with potassium and a little protein.
steps: Peel and slice the banana.
Serve with the peanut butter for dipping or spreading.

name: Orange segments and sunflower seeds
about: Juicy orange segments with a handful of sunflower seeds. A **bright, easy snack** with vitamin C and some vitamin E and magnesium from the seeds.
steps: Wash the orange, peel it and break it into segments.
Serve with the sunflower seeds.

name: Blueberry-ginger yogurt
about: Thick yogurt with fresh blueberries, a little grated fresh ginger and a drizzle of maple syrup. **Cool and soothing**, with calcium and iodine from the yogurt.
steps: Rinse the blueberries.
Stir the ginger into the yogurt and spoon into a bowl. Top with the blueberries and drizzle with maple syrup.

name: Crispy cumin chickpeas
about: Chickpeas roasted until crunchy with cumin, paprika and a pinch of salt. A **crunchy, salty snack** with fibre, folate and iron.
steps: Heat the oven to 400 F (200 C). Pat the chickpeas very dry so they crisp.
Toss them with the oil, cumin, paprika and iodized salt on a tray.
Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, shaking the tray halfway, until crisp and golden. They crisp further as they cool.
ingredients: rinsed, drained and patted very dry

name: No-bake peanut butter oat bites
about: Iron-fortified instant oats stirred with peanut butter, chopped walnuts and a little maple syrup and rolled into bites. A **sweet little snack** with fibre and some iron from the oats.
steps: Stir the oats, peanut butter, walnuts, maple syrup and cinnamon together in a bowl. Add water a teaspoon at a time, usually 2 or 3, until it holds firmly when pressed.
Press into 3 small balls and chill for 10 minutes. Keep leftovers in the fridge.
tip: Press a few blueberries into the middle of each bite for a juicy surprise.
ingredients: Plain instant oats with iron on the label, such as Quaker Instant Oatmeal, Original. Iron varies by brand, so do not stack other iron-fortified cereal on the same day

name: Maple-roasted walnuts and sunflower seeds
about: Walnuts and sunflower seeds toasted in a pan with a little maple syrup and cinnamon. A **warm, crunchy snack** with omega-3 from the walnuts and vitamin E and magnesium from the seeds.
steps: Toast the walnuts and sunflower seeds in a dry pan over medium heat for 3 minutes, until fragrant.
Stir in the maple syrup, cinnamon and iodized salt for 30 seconds, until sticky. Tip onto a plate to cool and crisp.

name: Veggie sticks with lemony yogurt dip
about: Crunchy carrot, cucumber and red pepper sticks with a cool lemon and garlic yogurt dip. **Crisp and refreshing**, with vitamin C from the pepper and calcium from the yogurt.
steps: Wash the vegetables and cut them into sticks.
Stir the yogurt with the lemon juice, garlic and iodized salt. Serve with the vegetables.

name: Blueberry-banana yogurt smoothie
about: A smoothie of milk, banana, blueberries, a handful of spinach and a spoonful of yogurt, blended until smooth. **Cold, sippable and gentle**, with calcium from the milk and yogurt and a little folate from the spinach.
steps: Wash the spinach well.
Blend everything with a few ice cubes until completely smooth, about 1 minute. Drink right away.

name: Warm edamame with lemon and a pinch of salt
about: Shelled edamame boiled until tender and sprinkled with a little iodized salt and lemon. A **fun, protein-rich snack** with folate and iron.
steps: Boil the edamame in a small pot of water until tender, about 5 minutes. Drain.
Sprinkle with the iodized salt and a few drops of lemon juice and serve warm.

name: Egg and tomato toast
about: A hard-boiled egg, cooked until the yolk is fully set, sliced over whole-wheat toast with juicy tomato. A **warm-and-cool little snack** with choline from the egg.
steps: Place the egg in a small pot, cover with cold water and bring to a boil. Cover, turn off the heat and let it sit for 12 minutes, until the yolk is completely firm. Cool in cold water and peel.
Rinse and slice the tomato. Toast the bread, top with the tomato slices and the sliced egg, and season with the iodized salt and pepper.

name: Egg and avocado toast
about: Whole-wheat toast with mashed avocado and a hard-boiled egg, cooked until the yolk is fully set. **Creamy and filling**, with choline from the egg and healthy fats from the avocado.
steps: Place the egg in a small pot, cover with cold water and bring to a boil. Cover, turn off the heat and let it sit for 12 minutes, until the yolk is completely firm. Cool in cold water and peel.
Rinse the avocado skin before you cut it. Mash the avocado with the lemon juice, iodized salt and a pinch of red pepper flakes.
Toast the bread, spread with the avocado and top with the sliced egg.

name: Gentle lemon poha with moong dal, peas and cashews, and a glass of warm milk
inspiredBy: Inspired by Maharashtrian kanda poha, with moong dal, peas, carrot and cashews and no fried extras
about: Soft flattened rice tossed with mustard seed, turmeric, a little split moong dal, sweet peas and golden cashews, with just enough lemon to wake up a sleepy appetite. It is mild and easy on a queasy morning. The moong dal and the glass of milk on the side add **protein and calcium**.
steps: Rinse the poha in a sieve under cool running water for about 30 seconds, tossing it with your fingers, then leave it to drain and soften. It should feel tender but still hold its shape.
Warm the oil in a wide pan and add the mustard seed. When it pops, add the cashews and curry leaves and stir for a minute until the cashews are pale gold.
Add the ginger, green chili, onion and carrot and cook for about 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the soaked moong dal, peas and turmeric with 100 ml of water, cover and cook for 8 minutes until the dal and peas are tender.
Fold in the drained poha and the salt and warm through for 2 minutes, stirring gently. Finish with the lemon juice and cilantro.
Warm the milk until it is steaming and serve it alongside.
tip: On a rushed morning, cook the moong dal and peas the night before and chill them, and the poha takes about 10 minutes. If the smell of onion is too much, leave it out and add a little extra grated carrot.
ingredients: split yellow moong dal, soaked for 30 minutes and drained
seeded, or leave out for a plain morning

name: Firm egg bhurji with tomato and spinach, a warm roti and orange
inspiredBy: Inspired by Punjabi anda bhurji
about: A homestyle Punjabi scramble with soft onion, ripe tomato and wilted spinach, cooked until the eggs are completely set. Two eggs bring **choline**, and the orange on the side gives vitamin C, which helps with absorbing iron from the roti and the egg.
steps: Mix the atta with warm water into a soft dough, knead for a minute, cover and rest while you cook the eggs.
Warm the oil in a pan and add the cumin. When it sizzles, add the onion, ginger and green chili and cook for about 4 minutes until soft.
Add the tomato and turmeric and cook for 4 minutes until the tomato breaks down. Stir in the spinach until it wilts.

Pour in the whisked eggs and stir slowly over medium heat. Keep cooking, breaking up the curds, until the eggs are firm all the way through, with no wet or liquid egg left and the yolk set, 3 to 4 minutes. Scatter over the cilantro.
Roll the dough into 2 small rounds and cook in a hot dry pan for about a minute on each side until they puff and have brown spots. Keep them warm in a clean towel.
Serve the bhurji with the rotis and the orange.

name: Soft moong dal cheela with spinach and carrot, curd and a banana
inspiredBy: Inspired by Punjabi and Gujarati moong dal cheela
about: Thin, tender pancakes of ground split moong dal with spinach and grated carrot, cooked until golden and served with cool curd and a ripe banana. It is a mild Gujarati and Punjabi favourite with no chili, so it sits easily in the morning. The dal brings **protein, folate and iron**, and the spinach adds folate.
steps: Blend the soaked dal with the ginger, hing, turmeric, salt and about 100 ml of cold water until completely smooth. The batter should pour like thin pancake batter.
Stir in the spinach, carrot, onion, cumin and cilantro.
Warm a non-stick pan over medium heat and wipe it with a little of the oil. Pour in a ladleful of batter and spread it into a thin round.

Cook for 2 to 3 minutes until the underside is golden and the top looks dry, drizzle a little oil around the edge, flip and cook 1 to 2 minutes more, until cooked through with no raw batter left. Repeat with the rest.
Serve warm with the curd and the banana.
tip: Soak the dal in the fridge overnight, and blend the batter fresh in the morning.
ingredients: split yellow moong dal, soaked for 4 hours or overnight and drained

name: Dalia and dal khichdi with cauliflower and ghee, and a bowl of curd
inspiredBy: Inspired by Gujarati and North Indian dalia khichdi
about: Cracked wheat, split moong and red lentils cooked together until soft and almost creamy, with cauliflower, carrot and peas and a spoon of ghee. This is the broken-wheat style of khichdi made in Gujarat and Uttar Pradesh, comforting and easy on the stomach. Two kinds of dal bring **protein, folate and iron**, and the curd adds calcium.
steps: Rinse the dalia and both dals together until the water runs mostly clear.
Warm half the ghee in a small pressure cooker or heavy pot and add the cumin and hing. When the cumin sizzles, add the ginger and tomato and cook for 2 minutes.

Add the dalia and dals, cauliflower, carrot, peas, turmeric and salt with about 4 cups of water for every cup of dalia and dal. Pressure cook for 3 whistles, or simmer covered for about 30 minutes, until everything is very soft and porridge-like.
Add a splash of hot water if you like it looser and stir well, mashing the cauliflower in lightly.
Finish with the lemon juice and the rest of the ghee, and serve with the curd.
tip: The dalia is bulgur or any cracked wheat. For a smoother khichdi, mash it lightly with the back of a spoon.

name: Chickpea chaat bowl with pomegranate, tamarind and yogurt, and a warm roti
inspiredBy: Inspired by North Indian chana chaat, with everything cooked and no sprouts
about: Soft chickpeas tossed with tomato, cucumber, red onion, cilantro, pomegranate and a tangy lemon and tamarind dressing, topped with whisked yogurt the dahi chaat way, and a few crunchy cashews. It is a street-food idea made into a proper lunch, and it works warm or cool. The chickpeas bring **folate, iron and protein**, and the lemon, tomato and pomegranate bring vitamin C along.
steps: Mix the atta with warm water into a soft dough and rest it while you make the chaat.
Roast the cashews in a dry pan for 2 to 3 minutes until golden, then crush the cumin seeds in the same hot pan for 30 seconds.

Warm the chickpeas with a splash of water for 3 minutes until steaming, then drain. Wash the tomato, cucumber, onion and cilantro under running water, and the pomegranate arils in a sieve. Cut them and toss with the chickpeas.
Stir the tamarind into the lemon juice with a spoonful of warm water, then dress the chaat with it, the cumin, chaat masala and salt.
Cook the roti in a hot dry pan for about a minute on each side until it puffs. Top the chaat with the yogurt, pomegranate seeds and cashews and serve with the roti.

name: Pepper sardine fry with a roti and kachumber
inspiredBy: Inspired by Kerala and Goan sardine fry, made with pantry sardines
about: Canned sardines folded into a drier onion, ginger and black pepper fry, a quick take on the sardine fries of Kerala and Goa. Mash in the soft bones too: they add **calcium**. Sardines are a low-mercury oily fish, rich in omega-3. Served with a hot roti and a crisp cucumber and tomato kachumber.
steps: Mix the atta with warm water into a soft dough, knead briefly and rest it.

Warm the oil and add the mustard seed. When it pops, add the curry leaves and the onion and cook for about 8 minutes until golden at the edges. Stir in the ginger, garlic and green chili for a minute.
Add the ground coriander, turmeric and black pepper and cook for 2 minutes until fragrant. Add a splash of water and the salt, sparingly since the sardines are already salty.
Flake in the sardines and mash the soft bones into the onion. Warm through for 3 minutes and finish with half the lemon and half the cilantro.

Cook the roti in a hot dry pan, about a minute on each side. Wash the cucumber, tomato and the rest of the cilantro under running water, cut them and toss with the rest of the lemon for the kachumber, and serve it all together.
tip: Canned light or skipjack tuna works if you prefer a milder fish (not albacore or white), but leave out the bones.

name: Masoor and moong dal palak with a roti and cucumber raita
inspiredBy: Inspired by Punjabi dal palak
about: A thick, homestyle dal of red lentils and split moong cooked with plenty of spinach and finished with a sizzling cumin, garlic and ghee tadka. The dal brings **iron and protein**, the spinach brings folate, and the lemon at the end helps your body use the iron. Makes two portions, so tomorrow's lunch is done.
steps: Rinse the masoor and moong dal. Cook them with the onion, tomato, ginger, turmeric, salt and about 550 ml of water in a pressure cooker for 3 whistles, or simmer covered for about 30 minutes, until completely soft. Mash lightly.
Stir the spinach into the hot dal and cook for 3 minutes until it wilts and turns deep green.

For the tadka, warm the ghee in a small pan, add the cumin, then the garlic. When the garlic turns golden, take the pan off the heat and add the Kashmiri chili and hing. Pour it over the dal and finish with the lemon and cilantro.
Mix the yogurt with the cucumber and a pinch of salt for the raita. Mix the atta with water into a soft dough and cook the rotis in a hot dry pan.
Eat one portion now. Chill the second portion of dal and raita within 1 to 2 hours. Tomorrow, reheat the dal to 74 C (165 F), steaming all the way through, and make fresh rotis.
tip: The dal freezes well for a month. Thaw it overnight in the fridge and reheat to 74 C (165 F), steaming all the way through.
ingredients: washed and grated, for the raita

name: Salmon in a mustard and yogurt curry with cauliflower and rice
inspiredBy: Inspired by Bengali shorshe maach, without mustard oil
about: A Bengali-inspired fish curry: salmon simmered in a sharp, tangy sauce of ground mustard seed, yogurt and green chili with cauliflower and green beans, served over fluffy basmati. Salmon brings **omega-3, DHA and vitamin D**, and it is a low-mercury fish. Cooked fresh and eaten the same day.
steps: Soak the mustard seed in 3 tablespoons of warm water for 10 minutes. Blend it with the green chili, a pinch of salt and a splash of water for just 20 to 30 seconds, then stir in the yogurt. Blending longer makes it bitter.
Cook the rice with twice its volume of water, covered, over low heat for about 30 minutes until tender.

Warm the oil in a wide pan. Add the cauliflower, green beans and turmeric and fry for 5 minutes. Turn the heat to low and stir in the mustard-yogurt mix, the rest of the salt and 150 ml of water. Cover and keep it at a gentle simmer for 8 minutes, until the vegetables are nearly tender. A hard boil will split the yogurt.
Nestle the salmon into the sauce, spoon some over it, cover and cook gently for 8 to 10 minutes, until the fish is opaque and flakes easily, and a thermometer in the thickest part reads 70 C (158 F).
Finish with the lemon and cilantro and serve over the rice.
tip: Trout or arctic char work as well as salmon.

name: Lean goat and fenugreek keema with peas and a roti
inspiredBy: Inspired by Punjabi and Karachi-style keema methi
about: A Pakistani and Punjabi keema: minced lean goat cooked slowly with onion, tomato, ginger, garam masala, sweet peas and a good handful of fresh fenugreek leaves until fully browned and tender. The goat is a good source of **iron and zinc**, and the tomato and lemon bring vitamin C along. Makes two portions, so tomorrow's lunch is done.
steps: Mix the atta with warm water into a soft dough, knead briefly and rest it.
Warm the oil in a heavy pan and add the cumin. When it sizzles, add the onion and cook for about 8 minutes until deep golden. Stir in the garlic, ginger and green chili.
Add the minced goat, breaking it up with a spoon, and cook over medium-high heat for 8 minutes until it is browned and no pink is left.

Add the tomato, carrot, ground coriander, turmeric, salt and yogurt and cook for 8 minutes, stirring, until the sauce is thick. Add the peas, fenugreek leaves and 100 ml of water, cover and simmer for 10 minutes until the meat reaches 71 C (160 F) on a thermometer and is tender.
Stir in the garam masala, lemon and cilantro. Cook the rotis in a hot dry pan and serve.
Chill the second portion within 1 to 2 hours. Tomorrow, reheat the keema to 74 C (165 F), steaming all the way through.
tip: Lean minced beef works if you cannot find goat. Frozen fenugreek leaves are fine.
ingredients: washed well if fresh, or frozen

name: Tamarind trout curry with green beans and brown rice
inspiredBy: Inspired by Tamil meen kuzhambu, with a handful of spinach stirred in
about: A Tamil-inspired meen kuzhambu: rainbow trout simmered in a tangy tamarind and tomato gravy with curry leaves, shallot-style onion, green beans and a handful of spinach, over brown rice. Trout brings **omega-3, DHA and vitamin D** and is a low-mercury fish. Tamarind adds the sour that makes South Indian curries taste bright.
steps: Cook the brown rice with twice its volume of water, covered, over low heat for about 30 minutes until tender.
Warm the sesame oil in a wide pan. Add the mustard seed. When it pops, add the curry leaves, onion and garlic and cook for 6 minutes until golden.
Add the green beans and cook for 5 minutes. Stir in the tomato, ground coriander, Kashmiri chili, turmeric and salt and cook for 5 minutes until the tomato breaks down.
Dissolve the tamarind in 250 ml of hot water, pour it in and simmer for 8 minutes. Stir in the spinach.
Slide in the trout, cover and cook gently for 8 minutes, until the fish is opaque and flakes easily, and a thermometer in the thickest part reads 70 C (158 F). Do not stir hard.
Scatter with the cilantro and serve over the rice.
ingredients: trimmed and cut in short lengths
untoasted (gingelly), not the dark toasted kind

name: Methi matar paneer in a tomato-cashew gravy with a roti
inspiredBy: Inspired by Punjabi methi matar paneer
about: Cubes of paneer, sweet green peas and a few chickpeas in a smooth tomato gravy thickened with a little cashew, with fresh fenugreek leaves stirred in. Buy paneer that says it is made from pasteurised milk on the label, and simmer it until steaming, as the recipe does. The paneer brings **calcium and protein**, the peas and chickpeas bring folate, and the tomato gives vitamin C. The fenugreek is the fresh leaf, cooked as a green. Makes two portions, so tomorrow's lunch is done.
steps: Mix the atta with warm water into a soft dough, knead briefly and rest it. Soak the cashews in hot water for 10 minutes.
Warm the oil and add the cumin. Add the onion, garlic and ginger and cook for 8 minutes until golden. Add the tomato, Kashmiri chili, turmeric and salt and cook for 8 minutes until soft and jammy.
Let the mixture cool for a few minutes, then blend it with the drained cashews and a splash of water until completely smooth.
Return the gravy to the pan with 100 ml of water. Add the peas, chickpeas and fenugreek leaves and simmer for 6 minutes. Add the paneer, garam masala and kasuri methi and simmer for 4 minutes.
Top with the cilantro. Cook the rotis in a hot dry pan and serve.
Chill the second portion within 1 to 2 hours. Tomorrow, reheat the curry to 74 C (165 F), steaming all the way through.
ingredients: washed well if fresh, or frozen

name: Chicken and vegetable dum pulao with cucumber raita
inspiredBy: Inspired by Hyderabadi and Pakistani dum pulao
about: A weekend one-pot pulao: chicken marinated in yogurt and ginger, layered over half-cooked basmati with peas, saffron, fried onion and cashews, then sealed and steamed on low heat until fragrant. It is a Hyderabadi and Pakistani celebration idea made lighter with brown basmati. The chicken is cooked all the way through. Makes two portions for tomorrow's lunch.
steps: Marinate the chicken with half the yogurt, the ginger, garlic, green chili, garam masala and half the salt for at least 30 minutes in the fridge, and up to 4 hours. Wash your hands, board and knife after handling the raw chicken.

Warm the oil in a heavy pot and fry the cashews for a minute until pale gold, then lift them out. Fry the onion in the same oil over medium heat for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden brown. Take out half for the top.
Add the chicken with its marinade to the pot and cook for 12 minutes, stirring now and then. Add the peas.
Meanwhile boil the rice in plenty of water with the bay leaf and clove for 22 minutes until about three-quarters cooked, then drain.

Spread the rice over the chicken. Top with the reserved onion, the cashews, the cilantro, the lemon and the saffron with its soaking liquid. Cover tightly with foil and the lid and cook on the lowest heat for 25 minutes. The chicken must reach 74 C (165 F) on a thermometer, with clear juices.
Stir the rest of the yogurt with the cucumber and a pinch of salt for the raita. Rest the pulao for 5 minutes, then fluff and serve.

Chill the second portion of pulao and raita within 1 hour, spread thin in a shallow dish so the rice cools quickly. Eat both by tomorrow's lunch, and reheat the pulao only once, to 74 C (165 F), steaming all the way through.
tip: Cooked rice must cool fast: spread it thin, chill within 1 hour, eat it by the next day and reheat it only once.
ingredients: plain, pasteurised, half for the raita
a pinch, soaked in warm water
washed and grated, for the raita

name: Bengali-style rohu jhol with cauliflower, green beans, spinach and rice
inspiredBy: Inspired by Bengali maacher jhol, with a three-seed tempering in place of panch phoron
about: A light, golden fish stew of rohu, the freshwater carp Bengali homes cook most weeks, with cauliflower, green beans and spinach in a thin ginger and cumin gravy. It is a soothing, brothy dish, like a Sunday lunch, and a fish that is generally low in mercury. It brings lean protein and **B12**. Cooked fresh.
steps: Pat the rohu dry and rub it with a little turmeric and half the salt. Cook the rice with twice its volume of water, covered, over low heat for about 30 minutes.
Warm half the oil in a wide pan and sear the fish for 2 minutes a side, just to firm it. Lift it out onto a plate.
Add the rest of the oil to the pan and the cumin, fennel and mustard. When they sizzle, add the ginger, green chili and tomato and cook for 4 minutes.
Add the cauliflower, green beans, remaining turmeric and salt and 400 ml of water. Cover and simmer for 12 minutes until the vegetables are tender. Stir in the spinach.

Lay the fish in the stew and simmer gently for 8 minutes, until it is opaque and flakes easily, and a thermometer in the thickest part reads 70 C (158 F). Finish with the lemon and cilantro and serve with the rice.
tip: Frozen rohu from an Indian or Bangladeshi grocer is common. Thaw it in the fridge and cook it the same day. Rohu has fine bones, so take your time with it. Cod works if you cannot find it.
ingredients: steaks, or fillets if you can get them

name: Guava, orange and pomegranate fruit chaat
inspiredBy: Inspired by Delhi phal chaat
about: Juicy guava, orange segments and pomegranate seeds with lemon and a pinch of chaat masala, the classic street-side fruit plate. It gives a big hit of **vitamin C**, which goes well with the iron in the meals around it.
steps: Scrub the guava and orange under running water, then cut the guava into cubes and segment the orange. Rinse the pomegranate seeds in a sieve.
Toss with the pomegranate seeds, lemon juice and chaat masala just before eating.
ingredients: washed and cubed, seeds and all

name: Cardamom and ginger masala chai with almonds
inspiredBy: Inspired by North Indian masala chai
about: A cup of milky chai with fresh ginger, cardamom and a little jaggery, with a small handful of almonds on the side. One cup is well under Health Canada's 300 mg a day caffeine limit for pregnancy, so just count it along with any other tea, coffee or cola that day. Have it between meals rather than with the iron-rich ones. The almonds bring **vitamin E**.
steps: Put the water for the tea in a small pan with the ginger and cardamom and simmer for 2 minutes, until it smells warm and spicy.
Add the tea bag and simmer for 2 minutes more, until it is a deep amber. Pour in the milk and jaggery and bring it just up to the boil.
Strain into a cup and serve with the almonds.
ingredients: black tea bag and its water

name: Carrot and cucumber raita with cashews
inspiredBy: Inspired by North Indian vegetable raita
about: Cool yogurt with grated carrot, cucumber, roasted cumin and a few crushed roasted cashews. A light, crunchy raita to eat from a bowl, with **protein, calcium and beta-carotene** from the carrot.
steps: Dry-roast the cashews in a pan until pale gold, then crush them. Crush the cumin seeds in the same hot pan.
Whisk the yogurt until smooth and stir in the carrot, cucumber, cumin and salt.
Top with the cashews and cilantro.

name: Banana and cardamom lassi
inspiredBy: Inspired by Punjabi lassi
about: Ripe banana blended with cold yogurt and a pinch of cardamom. Store-bought yogurt or dahi you set at home from pasteurised milk both work. It brings **calcium and potassium**, and it is a cooling snack.
steps: Blend the banana, yogurt, cardamom and a splash of cold water until smooth.
Serve cold right away.

name: Masoor dal shorba in a mug
inspiredBy: Inspired by North Indian dal ka shorba
about: A thin, warm, lemony soup of red lentils with tomato, ginger and cumin, sipped from a mug between meals. Red lentils are a good source of **iron, folate and protein**, and the lemon helps with absorbing that iron.
steps: Simmer the lentils with the tomato, ginger, turmeric, salt and 350 ml of water for about 20 minutes, until completely soft. Blend or mash until smooth.
Warm the ghee in a small pan, crackle the cumin for 20 seconds and pour it into the soup.
Finish with the lemon and cilantro and pour into a mug. Eat it hot.

name: Chickpea sundal with curry leaves and lemon
inspiredBy: Inspired by Tamil sundal
about: Chickpeas tossed in a quick tempering of mustard seed, curry leaves and green chili with a squeeze of lemon, the South Indian temple snack. A fibre-rich snack with **folate and protein**.
steps: Warm the oil and add the mustard seed. When it pops, add the curry leaves, green chili and hing.
Add the chickpeas and warm them through for 3 minutes until steaming hot.
Turn off the heat and add the lemon juice.

name: Banana with almonds and cardamom
about: A ripe banana sliced with a handful of almonds and a pinch of cardamom. Plain, quick and gentle on the stomach, with **potassium and vitamin B6**.
steps: Slice the banana and top with the almonds and cardamom.

name: Pomegranate raita bowl with roasted cumin and almonds
inspiredBy: Inspired by pomegranate raita
about: Cool yogurt with ruby pomegranate seeds, roasted cumin, slivered almonds and a pinch of salt. A refreshing, light snack with **calcium, vitamin C and vitamin E**.
steps: Whisk the yogurt until smooth and stir in the cumin and salt.
Rinse the pomegranate seeds in a sieve.
Top the yogurt with the pomegranate seeds and almonds.

name: Sesame, cashew and jaggery ladoo
inspiredBy: Inspired by North Indian til ladoo
about: Toasted sesame seeds and cashews pounded with jaggery and cardamom into little balls, a winter staple in many North Indian homes. Sesame brings **iron, calcium and zinc**.
steps: Dry-roast the sesame seeds and cashews separately in a pan over low heat for 2 to 3 minutes, until pale golden and fragrant.
Grind them coarsely with the cardamom. Melt the jaggery with a spoon of water until it bubbles, about 2 minutes, then stir in the ground mix.
Let it cool for a minute until you can handle it, then press into two tight balls with damp hands while it is still warm.

name: Spiced cumin chaas
inspiredBy: Inspired by North Indian chaas
about: A tall glass of cold, thin, salty-sour yogurt drink with roasted cumin, the traditional cooling drink with a meal. It is a source of **calcium and protein**.
steps: Whisk the yogurt with 200 ml of cold water, the cumin and the salt until frothy.
Serve cold.

name: Warm almond and cardamom milk
inspiredBy: Inspired by badam doodh
about: A mug of warm milk with a few almonds ground in and a pinch of cardamom, a comforting evening drink in many homes. It brings **calcium, protein and vitamin E**.
steps: Warm the milk with the ground almonds and cardamom until steaming, about 5 minutes, stirring so it does not catch.
Stir in the jaggery and pour into a mug.

name: Guava with lemon and chaat masala
inspiredBy: Inspired by amrood chaat
about: Ripe guava cut into wedges with lemon and a pinch of chaat masala. A simple street-side snack that is very high in **vitamin C** and fibre.
steps: Wash the guava well and cut it into wedges.
Squeeze over the lemon and sprinkle with the chaat masala.
ingredients: washed, in wedges, seeds and all

name: Saffron and cardamom lassi
inspiredBy: Inspired by Punjabi lassi
about: Cold yogurt whisked with a few saffron threads, cardamom and a little jaggery, a gently sweet lassi. Store-bought yogurt or dahi you set at home from pasteurised milk both work. It brings **calcium and protein**.
steps: Soak the saffron in a spoonful of warm water for 5 minutes.
Whisk the yogurt with the saffron water, cardamom, jaggery and a splash of cold water until smooth and serve cold.
ingredients: a few threads, soaked in a spoon of warm water

name: Pepper sardines with cucumber and lemon
inspiredBy: Inspired by Kerala sardine fry, served cold
about: Canned sardines with sliced cucumber, a squeeze of lemon, black pepper and cilantro, a quick no-cook plate. Mash in the soft bones too: they add **calcium**. A low-mercury oily fish with omega-3 and **choline**.
steps: Drain the sardines and lay them on a plate with the sliced cucumber.
Squeeze over the lemon and finish with the black pepper and cilantro.
Mash a few of the soft bones into the fish as you eat.

name: Overnight oats with berries and walnuts
inspiredBy: Inspired by Swiss bircher muesli, made the Canadian way with oats and milk
about: Rolled oats soaked overnight in milk and yogurt until creamy, with frozen berries that thaw into a jammy swirl and a crunch of walnuts and pumpkin seeds. Made in five minutes the night before, it gives you **fibre, protein and a little omega-3** with nothing to cook in the morning.
steps: Wash your hands, then stir the oats, milk, yogurt and cinnamon together in a jar until no dry oats are left.
Spoon the frozen berries on top (see the tip about frozen fruit), put the lid on and refrigerate overnight. The berries thaw and bleed into the oats, which is exactly what you want.
In the morning, stir it up. If it is thick, loosen it with a splash of milk. Scatter on the walnuts and pumpkin seeds so they stay crisp.
Eat within 2 days of making it, and keep it in the fridge until you do.
tip: Make it the night before, Monday for Tuesday and Thursday for Friday, and eat each jar within 2 days. If you are cooking for someone who is pregnant, 60 or older, 5 or under, or has a weak immune system, boil the frozen berries for 1 minute and cool them before they go in the jar, or use fresh.

name: Spinach and tomato scrambled eggs on toast
inspiredBy: Inspired by a Canadian diner scramble
about: Soft scrambled eggs with wilted spinach and cherry tomatoes, on whole-wheat toast with orange wedges on the side. The eggs bring **protein, choline and a little vitamin D**, and the orange helps your body absorb the iron in the spinach.
steps: Wash the spinach, tomatoes and orange. Halve the tomatoes and beat the eggs with the salt and pepper. Put the bread in the toaster.
Warm the oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat. Add the tomatoes and cook about 1 minute, until they start to soften.

Add the spinach and stir until it wilts, about 30 seconds. Pour in the eggs and keep folding gently until they are set with no runny egg left, about 2 minutes. They should be firm, not wet, and reach 71 °C (160 °F).
Pile the eggs on the toast and serve with the orange wedges.
tip: Pull the pan off the heat just as the eggs look almost done. They finish cooking in their own heat.

name: Mango yogurt bowl with toasted oat crunch
inspiredBy: Inspired by the North American yogurt parfait
about: Thick Greek yogurt with frozen mango and a warm crunch of toasted oats and pumpkin seeds. It has **plenty of protein**, plus a little **iron and zinc** from the seeds, and takes under 10 minutes.
steps: Toast the oats and pumpkin seeds in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring, until they smell nutty, about 3 minutes. Tip them onto a plate to cool.
Meanwhile, microwave the frozen mango in 30-second bursts until just thawed, about 1½ minutes, or thaw it overnight in the fridge.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl, top with the mango, squeeze over the lime, and scatter on the crunch and cinnamon.
tip: Toast a big batch of the oats and pumpkin seeds on Sunday and keep it in a jar for the week. If you are cooking for someone who is pregnant, 60 or older, 5 or under, or has a weak immune system, boil the frozen mango for 1 minute and cool it, or use fresh.

name: Huevos rancheros with black beans
inspiredBy: Inspired by the Mexican ranch-style breakfast, with beans on the side
about: Two eggs on warm corn tortillas with a quick chili-spiced tomato salsa, creamy black beans and avocado. A slower weekend breakfast with **protein, fibre and folate**, ready in about 25 minutes.
steps: Wash the cilantro, lime and avocado. Warm half the oil in a small pan over medium heat and soften the onion and garlic for 3 minutes. Stir in the cumin and chili powder and cook 30 seconds, then add the tomatoes and simmer about 5 minutes, until thick. Add the lime juice, cilantro and half the salt.
Stir the black beans into a little of the salsa in a small pot and warm through over low heat, about 3 minutes.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan, about 30 seconds a side, and set them on a plate.
Fry the eggs in the rest of the oil over medium heat with a lid on, until the whites are firm and the yolks are set, about 4 minutes. Cook the yolks firm, not runny.
Set the eggs on the tortillas, spoon over the salsa, and serve with the beans and avocado.
tip: Add a minced fresh jalapeño to the salsa if you like it hotter. At smaller sizes use one tortilla, with the beans and both eggs on top.

name: Tuscan tuna and chickpea salad on baby spinach
inspiredBy: Inspired by Tuscan tonno e ceci
about: Flaked light tuna and chickpeas with cherry tomatoes, onion and baby spinach, dressed with lemon and olive oil and served with toast. It packs **protein, fibre and iron**, and the lemon and tomatoes help you absorb that iron.
steps: Wash the spinach, tomatoes and parsley. Halve the tomatoes, slice the onion very thin and chop the parsley. Put the bread in the toaster.
Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice, salt and pepper in a bowl. Add the beans, tomatoes, onion and parsley and toss gently.
Flake in the tuna and fold once so the pieces stay chunky.
Pile the salad over the spinach and serve with the toast. Keep any leftovers in the fridge and eat them within 2 days.
tip: Soak the sliced onion in cold water for 5 minutes if you find raw onion sharp. Keep the other half of the can in a lidded container, not the open tin, and use it within 2 days, for example on toast.

name: Maple-Dijon chicken cutlets with white beans, carrots and spinach
inspiredBy: Inspired by Canadian maple-mustard chicken
about: Thin chicken cutlets seared hot and glazed with maple syrup and Dijon, over warm white beans, tender carrots and wilted spinach. It makes **two portions, so tomorrow's lunch is done**, and the beans and spinach bring iron and folate while the carrots bring vitamin A.
steps: Wash the carrots, spinach and parsley. Cut the carrots into thin sticks and microwave them in a covered bowl with a splash of water until tender, about 6 minutes. Add the beans for the last 2 minutes.

Meanwhile, slice each chicken breast in half horizontally into thin cutlets about 1 cm (3/8 inch) thick. Wash your hands, the knife and the board straight away. Season the cutlets with half the salt and the pepper.

Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Cook the cutlets about 3 minutes a side, until golden, using two pans or two batches if they do not fit in one layer. Stir the Dijon, maple syrup, garlic and lemon juice together, pour it over, and turn the cutlets in the glaze for 1 minute. Check that the thickest piece reaches 74 °C (165 °F).
Drain the carrots and beans and toss them with the spinach, the rest of the salt and the parsley so the spinach wilts in the heat. Serve beside the chicken with the pan juices spooned over.
Pack the second portion into a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours. Eat it within 3 days, reheated once until steaming, 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Cutlets this thin cook in minutes, so start the carrots first and the rest lines up. Thin-sliced chicken breast from the store skips the slicing.

name: Broiled ginger-soy salmon with peppers and brown rice
inspiredBy: Inspired by Japanese teriyaki-style salmon
about: A salmon fillet brushed with soy, ginger, garlic and a touch of maple, broiled on one tray with sweet red pepper strips and served on ready-cooked brown rice. It brings **omega-3, vitamin D and B12**, and it takes about 18 minutes. The second portion makes tomorrow's lunch.
steps: Set an oven rack about 15 cm (6 inches) under the broiler and heat it on high. Line a sheet pan with foil.

Whisk the soy sauce, maple syrup, ginger, garlic and half the lime juice together, then pour half into a clean small bowl for the plate. Wash the peppers, cut them into thin strips and toss them on the pan with the olive oil.
Set the salmon on the pan and brush the other half of the glaze over the top, then throw away what is left in the brushing bowl. Wash your hands, the brush and the board after touching the raw fish.

Broil 9 to 11 minutes, until the salmon flakes and reaches 70 °C (158 °F) and the pepper edges are charred. For the last 4 minutes, microwave the rice and frozen edamame in a covered bowl with a splash of water, stirring once, until steaming hot, and refrigerate the rest of an opened pouch within 1 hour to use within 1 day.
Divide the rice and edamame onto plates, add the salmon and peppers, drizzle with the sesame oil, the clean glaze from the small bowl and the rest of the lime juice.
Pack the second portion into a shallow container before you sit down, and refrigerate it within 1 hour. Eat it within 2 days, cold or reheated once until steaming, 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Thicker fillets need a minute or two more. Check the middle with a thermometer.
ingredients: skin-on or skinless fillets, about 2 cm thick

name: Quick chana masala with spinach and brown rice
inspiredBy: Inspired by North Indian chana masala, done in a skillet in minutes
about: Canned chickpeas simmered in a tomato sauce with onion, garlic, ginger, toasted cumin and garam masala, then wilted spinach and lemon. It has **plant protein, iron and folate**, with lemon to help absorb the iron. It makes two portions.
steps: Wash the spinach and cilantro. Heat the oil in a wide skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the onion until soft and starting to colour, about 4 minutes. While it cooks, mince the garlic, grate the ginger and rinse the chickpeas.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, cumin, coriander, turmeric and chili and cook 30 seconds, until fragrant.

Add the crushed tomatoes, the chickpeas, the salt and a splash of water. Simmer, mashing a few chickpeas with the spoon, about 6 minutes, until thick. Microwave the rice pouch meanwhile, and refrigerate the rest of an opened pouch within 1 hour to use within 1 day.
Stir in the spinach until wilted, then the garam masala and lemon juice.
Serve over the rice with a spoonful of yogurt and the cilantro.
Pack the second portion into a shallow container before you sit down, and refrigerate it within 1 hour. Eat it within 3 days, reheated once until steaming, 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Mash more of the chickpeas for a thicker sauce. Jarred ginger-garlic paste, the Indian home cook's shortcut, saves a few minutes: use as much as the garlic and ginger together.

name: Chicken and vegetable rice noodle stir-fry with ginger
inspiredBy: Inspired by Japanese yakisoba, with ginger and lime and rice noodles for speed
about: Quick-cooking rice noodles tossed with thin strips of chicken, cabbage, carrot, red pepper and edamame in a ginger, garlic and soy sauce. It brings **protein, niacin and a big pile of vegetables**. It makes two portions.
steps: Boil the kettle and pour the very hot water over the rice noodles. Let them soak until tender, about 8 minutes. Drain and rinse under cold water.

Meanwhile, wash and slice the pepper, and rinse the coleslaw mix unless the bag says it is washed and ready to eat. Slice the chicken into thin strips and wash your hands, the knife and the board straight away. Stir the soy sauce, lime juice, ginger and garlic together in a small bowl.

Heat the olive oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Add the chicken in one layer (use two pans, or two batches, if it does not fit) and stir-fry about 4 minutes, until no pink is left and the thickest strip reaches 74 °C (165 °F). Tip the chicken onto a plate.
Add the cabbage, carrot, pepper and edamame to the hot pan and stir-fry about 3 minutes, until crisp-tender and the edamame are hot through.
Return the chicken, add the noodles and sauce, and toss about 1 minute until hot. Drizzle with the sesame oil and chili flakes.
Pack the second portion into a shallow container before you sit down, and refrigerate it within 1 hour. Eat it within 3 days, reheated once until steaming, 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: A bag of frozen stir-fry vegetables works in place of the fresh ones, straight from the freezer. Reheat leftovers with a splash of water so the noodles loosen.
ingredients: from a bag of coleslaw mix, or finely shredded
from the coleslaw mix, or coarsely grated

name: One-pan sardine and tomato spaghetti with lemon
inspiredBy: Inspired by Sicilian pasta con le sarde, simplified for a weeknight
about: Whole-wheat spaghetti cooked in the same wide pan as cherry tomatoes, garlic and chili, then folded with canned sardines, spinach, lemon and parsley. The sardines give you **omega-3, calcium and vitamin D**, and there is only one pan to wash. It makes two portions.
steps: Put the kettle on. Wash the tomatoes, spinach, parsley and lemon, then slice the garlic.

Warm the oil in your widest, deepest skillet over medium heat. Cook the garlic and chili flakes for 30 seconds, until fragrant. Add the whole tomatoes and salt and cook about 3 minutes, until they start to burst, then crush about half of them with the spoon.

Break the pasta in half if it will not lie flat, then add it with enough water from a just-boiled kettle to just cover it. Bring back to a boil, then cook, stirring often, until the pasta is tender and most of the water has become a light sauce, about 7 minutes. Add a splash more water if it dries out. While it cooks, zest and juice the lemon, chop the parsley and open the sardines.
Fold in the spinach until it wilts. Break the sardines into big chunks and fold them in gently with the lemon juice and zest.
Serve topped with the parsley.
Pack the second portion into a shallow container before you sit down, and refrigerate it within 1 hour. Eat it within 3 days, reheated once until steaming, 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: No thin spaghetti? Regular whole-wheat spaghetti works too, but it adds about 4 minutes.
ingredients: thin spaghetti or spaghettini, 7 to 8 minutes on the package
from a lemon; zest it first

name: Chicken cacciatore with white beans and spinach
inspiredBy: Inspired by Italian pollo alla cacciatora, with beans and greens for a one-pot supper
about: Chicken thighs simmered with peppers, tomatoes and oregano, then white beans and spinach stirred in at the end and a squeeze of lemon, with toast to mop up the sauce. It is the **weekend's slow simmer**, and the leftovers are even better the next day. It brings protein, iron and folate.
steps: Wash the pepper, spinach and parsley before cutting. Pat the chicken dry and season with half the salt and the pepper. Wash your hands and the board after the raw chicken.
Heat half the oil in a large, heavy pot over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken on all sides, about 6 minutes, and set it aside.
Add the onion and pepper to the pot with the rest of the oil and cook until soft and golden, about 8 minutes. Add the garlic, oregano and thyme and cook 1 minute.

Return the chicken, add the tomatoes and the rest of the salt, and simmer partly covered for 20 minutes. Stir in the beans and spinach and simmer 5 minutes more. Check that the thickest piece of chicken reaches 74 °C (165 °F).
Finish with the lemon juice and parsley and serve with the toast.
Pack the second portion into a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours. Eat it within 3 days, reheated once until steaming, 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Toast fresh bread for the second portion. Freeze it instead if you will not eat it within 3 days, thaw it in the fridge and use it within 2 days.

name: Salmon and black bean tacos with crunchy slaw
inspiredBy: Inspired by Baja-style fish tacos, with salmon and beans
about: Strips of salmon seared with chili and cumin, black beans and corn tortillas, with a lime-dressed cabbage and carrot slaw, avocado and a yogurt crema. The salmon brings **omega-3, vitamin D and B12**, the beans add fibre, and it takes about 20 minutes.
steps: Wash the cabbage, carrot, cilantro, lime and avocado. Toss the cabbage, carrot and cilantro with half the lime juice and a pinch of the salt. Stir the rest of the lime juice into the yogurt for the crema.
Toss the salmon strips with the chili, cumin, garlic and the rest of the salt. Wash your hands and the board after the raw fish.

Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the salmon strips 2 to 3 minutes a side, until browned and 70 °C (158 °F) inside. Push them aside, add the black beans and a splash of water and warm 2 minutes.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan, about 30 seconds a side.
Fill the tortillas with the salmon and beans, then the slaw, avocado and a spoonful of crema.
tip: Break the salmon into big flakes as you fill the tortillas. At smaller sizes you get fewer tortillas, so fill one and a half or use two small ones.
ingredients: skinless, cut into strips about 2 cm wide

name: Banana with peanut butter and cinnamon
about: A banana split lengthwise, spread with peanut butter and dusted with cinnamon. It is a snack with **potassium, fibre and a little vitamin E** that takes two minutes.
steps: Split the banana lengthwise and spread the cut sides with the peanut butter.
Dust with cinnamon and eat right away.

name: Carrot and pepper sticks with lemony yogurt dip
inspiredBy: Inspired by Middle Eastern yogurt dips
about: Crunchy carrot and red pepper sticks with a thick, lemony yogurt dip. It brings **vitamin A, vitamin C and calcium** and some protein from the yogurt.
steps: Wash the carrot and pepper, then cut them into sticks.
Stir the yogurt, lemon juice, garlic and salt together.
Serve the vegetables with the dip.

name: Greek yogurt with berries and walnuts
about: Thick Greek yogurt with thawed mixed berries and a few chopped walnuts. It gives you **protein, calcium and a little plant omega-3** in two minutes.
steps: Spoon the yogurt into a bowl.
Top with the berries and walnuts.
tip: If you are cooking for someone who is pregnant, 60 or older, 5 or under, or has a weak immune system, boil frozen berries for 1 minute and cool them, or use fresh.
ingredients: thawed overnight in the fridge, or fresh

name: Peanut butter banana toast
about: Whole-wheat toast with peanut butter, banana and cinnamon. A snack for **steady energy and fibre** that takes five minutes.
steps: Toast the bread.
Spread with the peanut butter, top with the banana and dust with cinnamon.

name: Boiled eggs with cherry tomatoes and paprika
about: Hard-boiled eggs with sweet cherry tomatoes and a dusting of smoked paprika. You get **protein and choline** from a snack you can make ahead.
steps: Boil water in the kettle, pour it into a small pot over high heat and lower in the eggs. Cook 10 minutes, then cool them in cold water for a few minutes and peel.
Wash and halve the tomatoes. Halve the eggs, sprinkle with the salt and paprika and serve with the tomatoes. Refrigerate any extra boiled eggs in the shell and eat them within 7 days.
tip: Boil 6 eggs together on Monday night, cool them in cold water and keep them in the shell in the fridge for the week. Then the snack takes 2 minutes.

name: Banana oat smoothie
about: Banana, oats, milk and a spoonful of peanut butter blended smooth. It gives you **calcium, protein and slow-burning energy**.
steps: Blend everything until smooth, about 1 minute, adding a few ice cubes if you like it cold.

name: Avocado and tomato toast with lime
about: Mashed avocado and juicy cherry tomatoes on whole-wheat toast with a squeeze of lime. A snack with **healthy fats, potassium and fibre**.
steps: Toast the bread. Wash the tomatoes, avocado and lime, then halve the tomatoes.
Mash the avocado with the lime juice and salt, spread it on the toast and top with the tomatoes.

name: Orange segments with yogurt and pumpkin seeds
about: Juicy orange segments over cool Greek yogurt with pumpkin seeds for crunch. It brings **vitamin C, calcium and zinc**.
steps: Wash the orange, then peel and segment it.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl, top with the orange and pumpkin seeds.

name: Boiled egg and avocado toast with lime
about: Whole-wheat toast with mashed avocado, a sliced boiled egg and cherry tomatoes, finished with lime. A snack with **protein, choline and healthy fats**. At smaller sizes it is an open half-slice.
steps: Boil water in the kettle, pour it into a small pot over high heat and lower in the egg. Cook 10 minutes, then cool it in cold water for a few minutes and peel. Toast the bread. Wash the tomatoes, avocado and lime, then halve the tomatoes.
Mash the avocado with the lime juice and salt and spread it on the toast. Slice the egg over the top and add the tomatoes. Refrigerate any extra boiled eggs in the shell and eat them within 7 days.
tip: Boiled a batch on Monday night? Use one of those eggs and this takes 5 minutes.

name: Suhoor ful with tahini, lemon and cucumber
inspiredBy: Egyptian and Gulf ful medames, kept low in salt for suhoor
about: Warm, lightly mashed fava beans with garlic, cumin and lemon, a boiled egg, a drizzle of tahini, and a plate of cucumber and tomato to scoop up with warm whole-wheat khubz. The beans digest slowly, and the cucumber and tomato bring water to the plate. The fava beans carry **iron, folate and fibre**, and the salt is held low on purpose for suhoor.
steps: Wash the tomato, cucumber and parsley. Lower the egg into a small pot of boiling water and cook it for 10 minutes so the yolk is set, then cool it under cold water and peel it.
Warm half the oil in a small pan, stir in the garlic and cumin for 20 seconds, then add the fava beans, a splash of water and the salt.
Warm over medium heat for 5 minutes, then mash about half the beans with a fork so the ful is chunky and creamy. Take it off the heat and stir in half the lemon juice.
Warm the khubz in a dry pan until it is soft with a few toasty spots.
Spoon the ful into a shallow bowl and drizzle with the tahini, the rest of the oil and the rest of the lemon juice. Scatter over the parsley.
Serve with the halved egg, the tomato and cucumber, and the khubz for scooping. Drink a big glass of water with it.
tip: To cook from dried, soak about 250 g fava beans overnight, then simmer for 1½ to 2 hours (30 minutes in a pressure cooker). That makes about four portions. Keep what you will eat in the next 3 days in a shallow container in the fridge, and freeze the rest in single portions. Thaw them in the fridge, use within 2 days and reheat until steaming hot (74 °C). With regular tinned fava, rinse well and leave out the added salt. If anyone at your table has G6PD deficiency (favism), use chickpeas or white beans instead of fava.
ingredients: cooked from dried, or tinned and rinsed well (no salt added if you can find it)
boiled until the yolk is set

name: Cardamom oats with walnuts, a boiled egg and watermelon
inspiredBy: Ramadan suhoor porridge, with the Gulf's cardamom and a wedge of watermelon for water
about: Rolled oats simmered in milk with cardamom and cinnamon until creamy, topped with toasted walnuts and almonds and soft dried apricot, with a boiled egg and cold watermelon on the side. Oats and egg digest slowly, so this is a steady start before the fast. The oats and nuts bring **magnesium, fibre and vitamin E**, and the egg brings choline.
steps: Wash the outside of the watermelon before you cut it, then cut it into wedges and chill them. Lower the egg into a small pot of boiling water, cook it for 10 minutes so the yolk is set, then cool it under cold water and peel it.
Heat the milk with the cardamom, cinnamon and salt in a small pot over medium heat until it just begins to steam. Keep an eye on it so it does not boil over.
Stir in the oats and cook for about 6 minutes, stirring often, until the porridge is thick and creamy.
Stir in the apricot for the last minute so it plumps up.
Spoon into a bowl and scatter over the walnuts and almonds.
Serve with the halved egg, the watermelon and a big glass of water.
tip: Prefer no cooking before dawn? Stir the oats into the milk the night before, keep it in the fridge, and eat it cold with the nuts. The egg can be boiled ahead and kept in its shell in the fridge.
ingredients: boiled until the yolk is set

name: Zucchini and herb eggah with labneh and khubz
inspiredBy: Levantine ijjeh and Egyptian eggah, a thick herb omelette set in the pan
about: A thick, green omelette of grated zucchini, parsley and mint, set in the pan and cut into wedges, with a spoonful of cool labneh, cucumber and warm khubz. It is easy on the stomach and low in salt, and the second portion is good cold tomorrow. The eggs bring **protein and choline**, and the labneh adds calcium.
steps: Wash the zucchini, cucumber and herbs. Grate the zucchini, sprinkle it with a pinch of the salt, leave it for 5 minutes, then squeeze out the water with your hands.
Beat the eggs with the flour, cumin, pepper and the rest of the salt, then stir in the zucchini, parsley and mint.
Warm the oil in a non-stick pan with a lid. Soften the onion for 3 minutes, then pour in the egg mixture.
Cover and cook over low heat for about 10 minutes, until the top is mostly set with no runny egg left.
Finish under a hot broiler for 2 minutes until golden, or flip it with a plate. The centre should be firm and reach 74 °C.
Cut into wedges and serve with the labneh, cucumber and warm khubz.
Before you eat, put the second portion in a shallow container, cool it, and refrigerate it within 2 hours. Eat it within 3 days, cold or reheated until steaming hot (74 °C).
tip: Short on time before dawn? Cook it after iftar the night before and chill it within 2 hours. Eaten cold, tucked into khubz with the labneh, it is a good suhoor in a hurry.

name: Dates, water and Gulf lentil soup (shorbat adas)
inspiredBy: shorbat adas, the lentil soup on iftar tables from the Gulf to the Levant, with chickpeas for body
about: Break the fast with dates and water, then a bowl of silky red lentil soup scented with cumin and turmeric, blended halfway so it stays thick, and finished with lemon and fresh parsley. It is gentle after a day without food. The lentils and chickpeas bring **iron, folate and protein**, and the lemon helps your body use that iron.
steps: Rinse the lentils until the water runs clear. Wash and dice the carrot and onion, and wash and chop the parsley.
Warm the oil in a pot and soften the onion and carrot for about 6 minutes. Add the garlic, cumin and turmeric and stir for 30 seconds, then stir in the tomato paste for a minute.
Add the lentils, the chickpeas and enough water to cover by about 4 cm. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 20 to 25 minutes, until the lentils have fallen apart.
Blend about half the soup with an immersion blender, then season with the salt, pepper and half the lemon juice.

Before you sit down, pour the second portion into a shallow container, cool it, and get it into the fridge within 2 hours. Tomorrow, reheat it once, until steaming hot at 74 °C. It keeps up to 3 days.
To open the fast, eat the dates with a glass of water first, then ladle out the soup. Take a short pause before the main plate. Finish each bowl with the rest of the lemon and the parsley.
tip: A spoonful of cumin-toasted chickpeas on top gives it crunch.

name: Dates, water and chicken and cracked wheat soup
inspiredBy: Levantine shorbat freekeh, made with coarse bulgur because freekeh is hard to find
about: Break the fast with dates and water, then a warm, brothy soup of chicken, carrot and cracked wheat, fragrant with cinnamon, cardamom and a little baharat. The wheat swells to a hearty, nutty bowl that feels like a meal. The chicken brings **protein and niacin**, and the bulgur adds fibre.
steps: Wash the carrot and parsley, then dice the carrot. Wash your hands, knife and board after handling the raw chicken.
Warm the oil in a pot and brown the chicken pieces for 4 minutes. Add the onion and carrot and cook for 6 minutes, until the onion is soft.
Stir in the garlic, baharat, cinnamon, cardamom and tomato paste for 1 minute, then add enough water to cover by about 5 cm.
Simmer for 15 minutes, then stir in the bulgur and simmer another 15 minutes, until the wheat is tender and the chicken reaches 74 °C.
Season with the salt, pepper and lemon juice, and stir in the parsley.

Before you sit down, pour the second portion into a shallow container, cool it, and get it into the fridge within 2 hours. Tomorrow, reheat it once, until steaming hot at 74 °C. It keeps up to 3 days.
To open the fast, eat the dates with a glass of water first, then ladle out the soup. Take a short pause before the main plate.
tip: Real freekeh works the same way if you can find it; cook it until tender, about 25 minutes.

name: Dates, water and harira-style tomato, lentil and chickpea soup
inspiredBy: Moroccan harira, the soup that opens the fast across North Africa, with a swirl of beaten egg
about: Break the fast with dates and water, then a tomato soup thick with lentils and chickpeas, parsley and a ribbon of beaten egg stirred in at the end. A squeeze of lemon makes it bright. The legumes and egg bring **iron, folate and protein**, and the tomato and lemon add vitamin C.
steps: Rinse the lentils. Wash the tomatoes, carrot and parsley. Grate the tomatoes, dice the carrot and chop the parsley.
Warm the oil in a pot and soften the onion and carrot for 6 minutes. Stir in the turmeric, ginger, cinnamon and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add the grated tomato, lentils, chickpeas and enough water to cover by about 5 cm. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 25 minutes, until the lentils are tender.
Turn the heat to low. Pour the beaten egg in a thin stream while stirring, so it sets in ribbons, and cook for 1 minute until no runny egg remains. Stir in the salt, pepper, lemon juice and parsley.

Before you sit down, pour the second portion into a shallow container, cool it, and get it into the fridge within 2 hours. Tomorrow, reheat it once, until steaming hot at 74 °C. It keeps up to 3 days.
To open the fast, eat the dates with a glass of water first, then ladle out the soup. Take a short pause before the main plate.
tip: Leave the egg out of the portion you keep for tomorrow if you like, and stir a fresh egg into it when you reheat.

name: Dates, water and Saudi-style barley soup with lean beef
inspiredBy: shorbat shaeer, the barley soup on many Saudi iftar tables
about: Break the fast with dates and water, then a comforting barley soup with lean ground beef, carrot, tomato paste and lots of parsley, finished with lemon. The pearled barley softens into the broth and makes it thick and satisfying. The beef brings **iron and zinc**, and the barley adds fibre.
steps: Rinse the barley. Wash and dice the carrot, and wash and chop the parsley. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw beef.
Warm the oil in a pot and cook the onion for 5 minutes. Add the beef and break it up with a spoon, cooking until no pink remains and it reaches 71 °C.
Stir in the garlic, cumin, cardamom and tomato paste for 1 minute, then add the carrot, barley and enough water to cover by about 5 cm.
Simmer for 35 to 40 minutes, until the barley is tender and the soup is thick. Add water if it gets too thick.
Season with the salt, pepper and lemon juice, and stir in the parsley.
To open the fast, eat the dates with a glass of water first, then ladle out the soup. Take a short pause before the main plate.
tip: Make a double batch on a quiet day. Before you sit down, pour half into a shallow container, cool it and freeze it within 2 hours. Thaw it in the fridge, use it within 2 days and reheat until steaming hot (74 °C).

name: Lighter chicken kabsa with brown basmati and cucumber salad
inspiredBy: Saudi and Gulf chicken kabsa and machboos, with more vegetables and less rice and fat
about: Chicken simmered with tomato, loomi and warm spices, with brown basmati rice cooked in the same pot and topped with toasted almonds. A cool cucumber and parsley salad with lemon sits beside it. It is the full, fragrant Gulf iftar plate with the rice portion trimmed and the carrot and tomato doing more of the work, and the brown basmati brings **fibre and B vitamins**.
steps: Wash the carrot, tomato, cucumber and parsley. Pat the chicken dry and rub it with half the baharat, the turmeric and a splash of the lemon juice. Cover and keep it in the fridge while you make the base. Wash your hands, knife and board after handling the raw chicken, and do not reuse that rub.

Warm the oil in a wide, heavy pot and soften the onion for 6 minutes. Stir in the garlic, the rest of the baharat, the cinnamon and cardamom for 30 seconds, then add the tomato paste and grated tomato and cook for 5 minutes until jammy.
Add the loomi, the carrot, the salt and enough hot water to cover the rice by about 1.5 cm once it goes in. Stir in the rinsed rice, cover and cook on low.

After about 10 minutes, lay the chicken on top of the rice, cover again and keep cooking on low for another 25 minutes, until the rice is tender and the chicken reaches 74 °C. Added late, the chicken stays juicy instead of drying out.
Toast the almonds in a dry pan until golden, scatter them over the rice and let it rest, covered, for 10 minutes.
Toss half the cucumber and parsley with half the remaining lemon juice and a pinch of salt. Keep the other half undressed in the fridge and dress it tomorrow.

Before you sit down to eat, spoon the second portion into a shallow container and get it into the fridge within 1 hour, since rice does not wait. Eat it within 3 days and reheat it once, until steaming hot at 74 °C. Then serve the kabsa with the salad.
tip: A pressure cooker makes the brown rice ready in about 20 minutes. A spoonful of chopped green chili with tomato is the traditional daqoos on the side.

name: Baked salmon with lemon tahini and fattoush
inspiredBy: Gulf and Levantine baked fish with tarator, and a classic fattoush
about: Salmon baked with cumin and garlic and finished with a lemony tahini sauce, beside a big fattoush of romaine, cucumber, tomato and herbs with toasted khubz and a dusting of sumac. The salmon is rich and the salad is sharp and crunchy. The salmon brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the peppers and tomato bring vitamin C.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Wash the romaine, cucumber, tomato, pepper and herbs. If the salmon was frozen, thaw it in the fridge and cook it within 2 days.
Rub the salmon with a third of the oil, the garlic, cumin, paprika and a pinch of the salt, and lay it on a lined tray. Wash your hands after touching the raw fish.
Tear the khubz into pieces, toss with a teaspoon of the oil and bake beside the salmon for 6 to 8 minutes until crisp.
Bake the salmon for 12 to 15 minutes, until it flakes easily and reaches 70 °C.
Whisk the tahini with half the lemon juice and a splash of water until it pours like cream.
Toss the romaine, cucumber, tomato, pepper, parsley and mint with the rest of the lemon juice and oil, the sumac and the remaining salt. Add the khubz chips just before serving so they stay crunchy.
Serve the salmon with the tahini spooned over and the fattoush on the side.
tip: Trout works the same way if you prefer it.

name: Grilled beef kofta with tabbouleh and lemon tahini
inspiredBy: Levantine kofta with tabbouleh, with a little bulgur and plenty of parsley and mint
about: Herby lean beef kofta shaped on skewers and grilled until browned, with a bright tabbouleh of parsley, tomato, mint and a little bulgur, and a lemony tahini sauce. It is smoky, fresh and light. The beef brings **iron, zinc and B12**, and the tabbouleh brings vitamins C and K.
steps: Wash the tomato, cucumber, parsley and mint. Cover the bulgur with boiling water by 2 cm and leave it for 15 minutes, then drain well and press out the extra water.

Mix the beef with the onion, half the parsley, the baharat, cinnamon, pepper and half the salt. Mix with your hands until it holds together, then shape it into long ovals on skewers. Wash your hands, board and bowl afterwards.
Whisk the tahini with half the lemon juice, the garlic and a splash of water until smooth and pourable.
Brush a grill pan or skillet with half the oil and cook the kofta over medium-high heat for 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until browned and the centre reaches 71 °C.
Toss the bulgur with the tomato, cucumber, the rest of the parsley, the mint, the rest of the lemon juice and oil, and the remaining salt.
Serve the kofta over the tabbouleh with the tahini sauce spooned on top.
tip: Chilling the shaped kofta for 15 minutes helps it hold on the skewer. Buy halal meat if that matters at your table.

name: Baked mackerel with cumin potatoes, chickpeas and red pepper
inspiredBy: spice-rubbed baked fish from Egypt and the Gulf coast
about: Atlantic mackerel rubbed with cumin, garlic, paprika and lemon, baked over potatoes, chickpeas, tomato and red pepper until the juices turn into a sauce, with a crunchy cucumber salad and khubz. It is rich, tangy and quick to put together. The mackerel brings **omega-3, vitamin D and B12**, and the potatoes bring potassium.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Wash the potato, tomato, red pepper, cucumber and parsley. If the fish was frozen, thaw it in the fridge and cook it within 2 days.
Toss the potatoes, chickpeas, onion, pepper and half the oil with half the cumin and paprika and half the salt, and spread them in a baking dish. Roast for 20 minutes.

Mix the garlic, half the lemon juice, the remaining oil, cumin, paprika and a pinch of salt into a paste and rub it over the mackerel. Wash your hands and the board afterwards, and do not reuse anything that touched the raw fish.
Lay the tomato slices over the potatoes and set the mackerel on top. Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, until the fish flakes and reaches 70 °C.
Toss the cucumber with the parsley, the rest of the lemon juice, a pinch of black pepper and a pinch of salt. Warm the khubz.
Spoon the pan juices over the fish and potatoes and serve with the salad and khubz.
tip: Sardine fillets or trout are good in the same dish.

name: Baked lamb sambousek with fattoush
inspiredBy: Levantine and Egyptian meat sambousek, baked on a tray instead of deep-fried
about: Half-moon pastries of whole-wheat dough around spiced lamb and onion, brushed with a little oil and baked until golden and crisp, with a big lemony fattoush on the side. You get the Ramadan favourite without a pan of frying oil. The lamb brings **iron and zinc**, and the vitamin C in the salad helps you absorb that iron.
steps: Mix the flour with a pinch of the salt, a third of the oil and enough warm water to make a soft, smooth dough. Knead for 5 minutes, then cover and rest for 20 minutes.

Soften the onion in a teaspoon of the oil for 4 minutes. Add the lamb, cumin, cinnamon, baharat and half the remaining salt and cook, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it reaches 71 °C. Stir in a squeeze of the lemon juice and let it cool. Wash your hands, board and spoon after handling the raw lamb.
